<!-- =====================================================================
 RESTRUCTURE NOTE

 This notebook reorganizes the original exploratory Aging_organoids_30weeks.Rmd
 into linear, self-contained SESSIONS, and folds in the corrected QC and
 trajectory findings (the "CR" re-analysis, June 2026):

   * Cell QC: cell DIAMETER is the dominant good/bad discriminator (AUC 0.88).
     Two-stage QC = front-end gate (diameter>12.5 & count>2000 & contam<50)
     THEN a downstream compositional check (a hard gate alone misses ~27% of
     bad cells that are large/high-count but compositionally off).
   * Trajectory: the naive Slingshot pseudotime was a global proteome-quality
     artifact. A real progenitor->neuron trajectory is recovered ONLY after
     (a) dropping low-quality cells and (b) compositional (per-cell-centered)
     normalization. Drivers (UP = neuronal cytoskeleton; DOWN = ribosome +
     mito OXPHOS) replicate on ABSOLUTE abundances. Stable across 10-50% drop.
   * NA_C3 (missingness cluster) is enriched for bad cells but entangled with
     low input -> use as a flag/biology question, not a hard QC filter.

 DECISIONS (agreed): R-native reimplementation; marker zoo -> module scores +
 curated subset; imputed pipeline -> appendix.
 ===================================================================== -->

# Session 0 — Setup & global parameters

<!-- Libraries + every threshold/knob in ONE place so the pipeline is tunable
     and self-documenting. Replaces scattered library() calls and hard-coded
     numbers throughout the original. -->

```{r libraries}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  ## core SCP / SCE
  library(scp); library(SingleCellExperiment); library(QFeatures)
  library(scater); library(scran); library(scuttle); library(bluster)
  ## modeling / trajectory / enrichment
  library(slingshot); library(TrajectoryUtils); library(mgcv)  # mgcv: Gaussian GAMs
  library(clusterProfiler); library(org.Hs.eg.db)
  library(AUCell); library(GSEABase)
  library(SingleR); library(celldex)
  ## tidy / viz
  library(tidyverse); library(patchwork); library(ggrepel)
  library(ComplexHeatmap); library(circlize); library(pheatmap)
  library(viridis); library(RColorBrewer); library(MASS)
})
```

```{r params}
## ---- paths -----------------------------------------------------------------
PATHS <- list(
  base    = "D:/Documents/Projetos/Aging_organoids_SCP/Full_analysis/20250502_SCP_WT83_7point5_Months",
  report  = "DIANN/DIANN/report_arrow/part-0.tsv",           # single-cell DIA-NN
  blanks  = "Blanks/DIANN/DIANN/report_arrow/part-0.tsv",
  sampAnn = "DIANN/sampleAnnotation.csv",
  ## dedicated output dir for this restructured pipeline
  results = "DIANN/DIANN/scp/Restructured_results"
)
## subfolders for figures / tables / saved objects (created if missing)
PATHS$fig <- file.path(PATHS$results, "Figures")
PATHS$tab <- file.path(PATHS$results, "Tables")
PATHS$obj <- file.path(PATHS$results, "Objects")
for (p in c(PATHS$results, PATHS$fig, PATHS$tab, PATHS$obj))
  dir.create(file.path(PATHS$base, p), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

## small helpers so every session saves to the right place.
## save_fig() writes BOTH a 300-dpi anti-aliased PNG and a vector PDF.
save_fig <- function(plot, name, w = 7, h = 5) {
  stem <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(name)
  ## wrap in try(): a transient graphics-device hiccup (e.g. cairo) must not abort
  ## the whole pipeline/knit — the inline HTML figure comes from print(), not here.
  ok_png <- try(ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$fig, paste0(stem, ".png")),
                  plot, width = w, height = h, dpi = 300,
                  device = grDevices::png, type = "cairo"), silent = TRUE)
  if (inherits(ok_png, "try-error"))                    # fall back to the default png device
    try(ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$fig, paste0(stem, ".png")),
                        plot, width = w, height = h, dpi = 300), silent = TRUE)
  try(ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$fig, paste0(stem, ".pdf")),
                  plot, width = w, height = h, device = grDevices::cairo_pdf), silent = TRUE)
  invisible(NULL)
}
save_tab <- function(df, name)
  utils::write.csv(df, file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$tab, name), row.names = FALSE)

## ---- QC thresholds (Session 3) --------------------------------------------
QC <- list(
  pg_qvalue      = 0.01,   # Global.PG.Q.Value <= this
  count_floor    = 2000,   # peptides/cell (raised from original 1500 per CR7/8)
  contam_ceiling = 50,     # contaminant % (kept; tightening hurts good cells)
  diameter_floor = 12.5,   # um  (front-end gate; best single discriminator, ~ Youden-J optimum 12.46)
  drop_fraction  = 0       # keep ALL 131 cells for the trajectory. The quality composite
                           # (count + log_sumsRI_NoCRAP + mean intensity) is purely TECHNICAL
                           # and computed BEFORE the fit, so the drop is not trajectory-derived
                           # (no circularity); but those QC metrics correlate with cell state,
                           # and the trifurcation is stable at 0% drop (10.3 sweep), so keeping
                           # all 131 QC-gated cells avoids any proportion bias. (Was 0.22.)
)

## ---- processing / clustering ----------------------------------------------
PROC <- list(
  na_pep_max   = 0.99,     # filterNA on peptides
  minimal_form = ~ 1 + log_sumsRI_NoCRAP,            # scplainer minimal model (contaminant-free loading)
  cluster_form = ~ 1 + log_sumsRI_NoCRAP + Cluster,  # scplainer cluster model (contaminant-free loading)
  nn_k         = 6,        # scran NNGraph k (S10 trajectory graph)
  clust_k      = 10,       # S7 descriptive clustering: SNN k (k-sweep optimum -> 4 clusters)
  clust_fun    = "louvain",# S7 clustering algorithm (k-sweep used louvain)
  umap_nn      = 20,
  marker_min_det = 0.10,   # S8: a marker "counts" only if detected in >=10% of cells
  na_k_prot    = 5,        # NA protein-module clusters
  na_k_cell    = 3         # NA cell clusters
)

## ---- trajectory (Session 10) ----------------------------------------------
TRAJ <- list(
  start_markers = c("PCNA", "RRM1", "NASP", "HMGB2", "HMGB1", "HMGB3"),  # CYCLING-module root: a lineage-specific progenitor signal. More robust than SOX2/NES, which is also high in astroglia and so cannot separate the C3 progenitor from the C1 glial branch (both pick C3 here, but cycling is unambiguous).
  end_clusters  = c("1", "2", "4"),  # the THREE terminal fates of the C3 progenitor declared as leaves: C1 astroglial, C2 neuronal, C4 splicing/RNA-processing. This makes C4 form its OWN branch (C3->C4) instead of hanging off the neuronal tip (C3->C2->C4). Corroborated by the UNFORCED npc=5 fit, which splits C4 off spontaneously (see 10.1.1); keeps full npc=15 resolution. Clusters absent at a given drop level are dropped from the set automatically.
  spline_df     = 4,
  go_libraries  = c("GO_Biological_Process_2021", "GO_Cellular_Component_2021")
)

set.seed(101)
```

# Session 1 — Data import & assembly

<!-- CONTENT: read DIA-NN single-cell + blank reports, File_info,
     sampleAnnotation; readSCP(); zeroIsNA().  (original lines ~42-205)
     OUTPUT: `scp` QFeatures object with raw precursor assays. -->

```{r import}
## --- read DIA-NN single-cell + blank precursor reports ----------------------
sc <- readr::read_tsv(file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$report), show_col_types = FALSE)
sc$Condition <- "SingleCell"
bl <- readr::read_tsv(file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$blanks), show_col_types = FALSE)
bl$Condition <- "Blank"

ScpData <- dplyr::bind_rows(sc, bl)
names(ScpData)[names(ScpData) == "Run"] <- "runCol"   # readSCP keys on runCol

## --- imaging / well metadata (becomes colData) ------------------------------
sampleAnnotation <- read.csv(file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$sampAnn))

## --- assemble QFeatures, one assay per run, zeros -> NA ----------------------
scp <- readSCP(assayData      = ScpData,
               colData         = sampleAnnotation,
               runCol          = "runCol",
               multiplexing    = "none",
               removeEmptyCols = TRUE)
scp <- zeroIsNA(scp, i = seq_along(scp))
rm(sc, bl, ScpData); invisible(gc())   # free the ~1 GB raw import (memory hygiene)
scp
```

# Session 2 — Contaminant annotation

<!-- CONTENT: curated skin/saliva/blood/Ig/casein gene list + cRAP; compute
     per-cell sum_contam_intensity and contam_percent into colData.
     (original lines ~152-205, 261-293) -->

```{r contaminants}
## Curated external-contaminant gene set (skin / saliva / blood / Ig / casein).
## Used both for the per-cell contaminant % here AND for feature removal in
## Session 4. KRT* and DIA-NN 'cRAP' tags are handled separately.
contam_genes <- c(
  ## skin / keratinocyte / cornified envelope
  "S100A7","S100A8","S100A9","DSP","IVL","LGALS7","JUP","FLG","FLG2","SBSN",
  "DCD","HRNR","CRNN","TGM3","CASP14",
  ## saliva / mucins
  "PIP","PIGR","PRR4","LACRT","LTF","MUC5B","MUCL1","MUC1","MUC2","MUC16","ZG16B",
  ## blood / serum
  "ALB","HP","HBA1","HBA2","HBB",
  ## immunoglobulins
  "IGHG1","IGHG2","IGHG3","IGHG4","IGKC","IGLC1","IGLC2","IGLC3","IGLC7","JCHAIN",
  ## milk caseins (environmental)
  "CSN1S1","CSN1S2","CSN2","CSN3")
## exact gene match with ';' boundaries (handles multi-gene "A;B" rows)
contam_pat <- paste0("(^|;)(", paste(contam_genes, collapse = "|"), ")(;|$)")

## per-cell contaminant intensity & % of total signal (computed BEFORE removing
## the contaminant features, which happens in Session 4)
for (i in names(scp)) {
  mat   <- assay(scp[[i]])
  genes <- rowData(scp[[i]])$Genes
  is_cRAP    <- grepl("cRAP", genes)
  is_curated <- grepl(contam_pat, genes)
  is_contam  <- is_cRAP | is_curated
  sum_cRAP   <- colSums(mat[is_cRAP,   , drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
  sum_contam <- colSums(mat[is_contam, , drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
  total      <- colSums(mat, na.rm = TRUE)
  colData(scp)[names(sum_cRAP),   "sum_cRAP_intensity"]   <-
    log(replace(sum_cRAP,   sum_cRAP   == 0, NA))
  colData(scp)[names(sum_contam), "sum_contam_intensity"] <-
    log(replace(sum_contam, sum_contam == 0, NA))
  colData(scp)[names(total),      "contam_percent"]       <- 100 * sum_contam / total
  ## contaminant-FREE summed intensity: drop cRAP + KRT + curated (matches the
  ## Session-4 feature removal), so this loading estimate excludes contaminant ion
  ## current. On average ~34% of the raw summed intensity is contaminant.
  is_full   <- is_contam | grepl("^KRT", genes)
  sum_clean <- colSums(mat[!is_full, , drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
  colData(scp)[names(sum_clean), "log_sumsRI_NoCRAP"] <-
    log(replace(sum_clean, sum_clean == 0, NA))
}
```

# Session 3 — Cell quality control & filtering  ⭐ (upgraded)

## 3.1 Per-cell QC metrics
<!-- count (countUniqueFeatures), log_medianRI, log_sumsRI, contam_percent,
     Trans_Diameter; PSM q-value filter + contaminant/KRT feature removal. -->

```{r qc-metrics}
## per-cell median and summed reporter intensity (on raw, pre-filter assays)
for (i in names(scp)) {
  logAssay <- log(assay(scp[[i]]))
  colData(scp)[colnames(logAssay), "log_medianRI"] <-
    colMedians(logAssay, na.rm = TRUE, useNames = TRUE)
  colData(scp)[colnames(logAssay), "log_sumsRI"] <-
    log(colSums2(assay(scp[[i]]), na.rm = TRUE, useNames = TRUE))
}

## peptides identified per cell (count) -- on raw features, to match the QC
## calibration. Contaminant/q-value FEATURE removal happens in Session 4.
scp <- countUniqueFeatures(scp, i = seq_along(scp),
                           groupBy = "Stripped.Sequence", colDataName = "count")
scp$LogCount <- log2(scp$count)

## Trans_Diameter (imaging) is already in colData from sampleAnnotation.
summary(as.data.frame(colData(scp))[, c("count","contam_percent",
                                        "log_sumsRI","Trans_Diameter")])
```

## 3.2 QC landscape — diameter x count x contamination
<!-- The CR6 plot: all cells, X=diameter, Y=count, fill=contam%. Visualizes the
     bad-cell cluster (small / low-count / contaminated, bottom-left). -->

```{r qc-landscape, fig.width=8, fig.height=6}
qc_df <- as.data.frame(colData(scp)) |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("cell") |>
  dplyr::filter(Condition == "SingleCell")

## X = diameter, Y = count, colour = contaminant %. The bad-cell population sits
## bottom-left: small, low-count, contaminated. Dashed lines = the front-end gate.
ggplot(qc_df, aes(Trans_Diameter, count, colour = pmin(contam_percent, 60))) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(name = "contam %") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = QC$count_floor,    linetype = "dashed", colour = "firebrick") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = QC$diameter_floor, linetype = "dashed", colour = "firebrick") +
  labs(x = "Trans_Diameter (µm)", y = "count (peptides identified)",
       title = "Per-cell QC landscape",
       subtitle = "dashed = front-end gate; bottom-left cloud = bad cells") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 13)
```

## 3.2b Blanks vs single cells — summed intensity separates empty droplets
<!-- Log summed intensity (log_sumsRI) vs peptide count for ALL samples (blanks
     still in the object here, before the gate). Blanks = distinct SHAPE. -->

Plotting per-cell **summed intensity** (`log_sumsRI`) against peptide IDs — with the
Blank controls drawn as a distinct shape — shows the blanks collapsing into the
low-intensity / few-ID corner, cleanly separated from real single cells. This is the
negative-control check that the single-cell signal is not background.

```{r qc-intensity-blanks, fig.width=8, fig.height=6}
qc_all <- as.data.frame(colData(scp))
qc_all <- qc_all[!is.na(qc_all$Condition), ]
qc_all$Condition <- factor(qc_all$Condition, levels = c("SingleCell", "Blank"))
p_ib <- ggplot(qc_all, aes(log_sumsRI, count)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = QC$count_floor, linetype = "dashed", colour = "firebrick") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = pmin(contam_percent, 60), shape = Condition), size = 2.6, alpha = 0.85, stroke = 0.7) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(SingleCell = 16, Blank = 15), name = "Sample type") +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(name = "cRAP %") +
  labs(x = "Log summed intensity (log_sumsRI)", y = "Identified peptides per cell",
       title = "Per-cell QC: peptide IDs vs summed intensity",
       subtitle = "blanks (squares) collapse to low summed intensity + few IDs; dashed = count gate") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 13) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
print(p_ib); save_fig(p_ib, "S3_intensity_vs_count_blanks.png", 8, 6)
```

## 3.3 What discriminates good vs bad cells
**QC calibration (from the CR re-analysis, documented once).** Ranking every QC
metric by its power to separate good from bad cells across three quality tiers
(excluded / low-quality / high-quality), **cell diameter is the single best
discriminator (AUC 0.88)** and an imaging-only classifier reaches AUC 0.86.
Crucially, **contaminant % does *not* separate the subtle (trajectory-bad)
cells** — it only flags gross contamination, which the `< 50 %` rule already
removes. The full calibration lives in `Images/TrajectoryAnalysis/CR5*` and
motivates the thresholds in `QC`. The plot below shows the core relationship
(forward-runnable): larger cells clear the depth floor.

```{r qc-discriminators, fig.width=6, fig.height=4}
qc_df$count_pass <- qc_df$count > QC$count_floor
ggplot(qc_df, aes(Trans_Diameter, fill = count_pass)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = QC$diameter_floor, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey70", `TRUE` = "#2ca02c"),
                    labels = c("count ≤ floor", "count > floor"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Trans_Diameter (µm)", title = "Cell size tracks proteome depth") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 13)
```

## 3.4 Threshold sweet-spots & combined gate
**Sweet-spot thresholds (CR7/CR8).** Per-metric calibration for separating good
from trajectory-bad cells gave:

| Metric | Sweet spot | Note |
|---|---|---|
| diameter | **> 12.5 µm** | best balance; keeps 90 % good, removes 66 % bad; measured pre-MS |
| count | **> 2000** | gentler than the J-optimal 3115 (which loses 38 % of good cells) |
| contam % | **< 50** | keep as-is; tightening removes *good* cells (AUC 0.43) |

Combined gate `diameter > 12.5 & count > 2000 & contam < 50` keeps **131** single cells
at **92 % purity** (120/144 HighQ recovered, 11/41 LowQ admitted, 0/108 junk). The
stricter 12.5-µm floor (vs a looser 12-µm gate that admits ~17 more cells at 89 % purity)
is preferred: the extra cells are ~40 % low-quality and surface a spurious epithelial /
contaminant cluster on reclustering (standalone diagnostic). It cannot catch the
large/high-count-but-compositionally-off bad cells — those are removed later by the
compositional check in Session 10. The thresholds are held in `QC` (Session 0):

```{r qc-gate}
str(QC)
```

## 3.5 Apply front-end filter
<!-- Apply the gate -> retained cells. NOTE: a second, compositional quality
     check is applied later (Session 10) for the cells this gate cannot catch. -->

```{r qc-apply}
## Front-end gate: drop blanks + small / shallow / contaminated cells.
keep <- with(as.data.frame(colData(scp)),
             Condition == "SingleCell" &
             count          >  QC$count_floor &
             contam_percent <  QC$contam_ceiling &
             Trans_Diameter >  QC$diameter_floor)
keep[is.na(keep)] <- FALSE

n_sc <- sum(scp$Condition == "SingleCell", na.rm = TRUE)
message(sprintf("Front-end gate keeps %d of %d single cells (%.0f%%).",
                sum(keep), n_sc, 100 * sum(keep) / n_sc))

scp <- subsetByColData(scp, keep) |> dropEmptyAssays()
scp
```

## 3.6 Proteome depth scales with cell size (kept cells)
<!-- Correlation of diameter vs peptide count AMONG THE KEPT CELLS (post-gate),
     styled like the panel-e cell-size figure. Range-restricted vs the full set. -->

Among the cells that pass the gate, larger cells still yield deeper proteomes — the
imaging-based diameter tracks peptide identifications. The correlation is more modest
than across the *unfiltered* population because the gate removes the small/shallow tail,
restricting the diameter range (range restriction attenuates the coefficient).

```{r qc-diam-count-cor, fig.width=8, fig.height=6}
kept_cd <- as.data.frame(colData(scp))          # scp is now the gated set (all SingleCell)
.ct <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(kept_cd$Trans_Diameter, kept_cd$count, method = "spearman"))
.sp <- unname(.ct$estimate); .pv <- .ct$p.value
.r2 <- summary(lm(count ~ Trans_Diameter, kept_cd))$r.squared
.plab <- if (.pv < 2.2e-16) "p < 2.2e-16" else sprintf("p = %.1e", .pv)
p_dc <- ggplot(kept_cd, aes(Trans_Diameter, count)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, colour = "#B2182B", fill = "#B2182B", alpha = 0.18) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = log_sumsRI_NoCRAP), size = 2.6, alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(name = "log_sumsRI\n(no cRAP)") +
  annotate("label", x = -Inf, y = Inf, hjust = -0.05, vjust = 1.1, size = 4.2,
           label = sprintf("Spearman rho = %.2f\n%s\nR^2 = %.3f | n = %d", .sp, .plab, .r2, nrow(kept_cd))) +
  labs(x = "Trans_Diameter (µm)", y = "Identified peptides per cell",
       title = "Peptide identifications scale with cell size (kept cells)",
       subtitle = sprintf("cells passing the front-end gate (diam > %g, count > %d, contam < %d), n = %d",
                          QC$diameter_floor, QC$count_floor, QC$contam_ceiling, nrow(kept_cd))) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 13) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
print(p_dc); save_fig(p_dc, "S3_diameter_count_correlation_kept.png", 8, 6)
```

---

# Session 4 — Peptide processing & protein quantification

<!-- CONTENT: aggregateFeaturesOverAssays -> joinAssays -> filterNA(pNA) ->
     median/mean normalization -> log2 -> aggregateFeatures to Protein.Group;
     sensitivity curves + Jaccard; export Prots.csv.  (original norm/agg blocks)
     OUTPUT: clean log2 Protein.Group matrix (the canonical quant). -->

```{r processing}
## --- feature filtering: drop contaminants/keratins + low-confidence PGs ------
scp <- filterFeatures(scp, ~ !(grepl("cRAP", Genes) |
                                grepl("^KRT", Genes) |
                                grepl(contam_pat, Genes)))
## filterFeatures() reads the formula symbolically (all.vars), so `QC$pg_qvalue`
## would be mis-parsed as a rowData column named 'pg_qvalue'. Bind a plain local
## scalar instead (a bare symbol resolves from the calling env, like contam_pat).
pg_qvalue_thr <- QC$pg_qvalue
scp <- filterFeatures(scp, ~ Global.PG.Q.Value <= pg_qvalue_thr)

## --- precursors -> peptides (per run), then join across runs ----------------
scp <- aggregateFeaturesOverAssays(
  scp, i = seq_along(scp), fcol = "Stripped.Sequence",
  name = paste0("peptides_", names(scp)), fun = colMeans, na.rm = TRUE)
pep_assays <- grep("^peptides_", names(scp), value = TRUE)
scp <- joinAssays(scp, i = pep_assays, name = "peptides")

## PEAK-MEMORY POINT: free the 185 per-run precursor + per-run peptide assays
## immediately after the join (they are no longer needed). This is what tips a
## low-RAM PC over during this chunk.
scp <- removeAssay(scp, setdiff(names(scp), "peptides"))
invisible(gc())

## --- drop near-empty peptides ----------------------------------------------
scp <- filterNA(scp, i = "peptides", pNA = PROC$na_pep_max)

## --- minimal-processing log peptides for scplainer (NO normalization) -------
scp <- logTransform(scp, base = 2, i = "peptides", name = "peptides_log_noNorm")

## --- normalization for the descriptive / clustering branch ------------------
## divide each cell by its column sum, then each peptide by its row mean, log2
scp <- sweep(scp, i = "peptides", MARGIN = 2, FUN = "/",
             STATS = colSums2(assay(scp[["peptides"]]), na.rm = TRUE),
             name = "peptides_norm_col")
scp <- sweep(scp, i = "peptides_norm_col", MARGIN = 1, FUN = "/",
             STATS = rowMeans(assay(scp[["peptides_norm_col"]]), na.rm = TRUE),
             name = "peptides_norm")
scp <- logTransform(scp, base = 2, i = "peptides_norm", name = "peptides_log")

## --- aggregate peptides -> protein groups (gene level) ----------------------
scp <- aggregateFeatures(scp, i = "peptides_log", fcol = "Genes",
                         name = "Protein.Group", fun = colMeans, na.rm = TRUE)
scp <- zeroIsNA(scp, "Protein.Group")

## ALSO aggregate the NON-normalised log peptides -> protein = absolute log
## ABUNDANCE (NOT per-protein centred). Used only by Appendix A SingleR, which
## rank-correlates against absolute-expression references; the centred
## Protein.Group distorts within-cell ranks (verified: >60-90% of calls change).
scp <- aggregateFeatures(scp, i = "peptides_log_noNorm", fcol = "Genes",
                         name = "Protein.Group_abund", fun = colMeans, na.rm = TRUE)

## --- export the canonical protein matrix (log2, NA = not detected) ----------
Prots <- as.data.frame(assay(scp[["Protein.Group"]]))
write.csv(Prots, file.path(PATHS$base, "DIANN/DIANN/scp/Prots.csv"), row.names = TRUE)
cat(sprintf("Protein.Group: %d proteins x %d cells | peptide NA = %.0f%% | protein NA = %.0f%%\n",
            nrow(Prots), ncol(Prots),
            100 * mean(is.na(assay(scp[["peptides"]]))),
            100 * mean(is.na(assay(scp[["Protein.Group"]])))))

## free the per-run precursor assays + normalization intermediates (memory
## hygiene). Keep only what later sessions use.
keep_assays <- c("peptides", "peptides_log_noNorm", "Protein.Group", "Protein.Group_abund")
scp <- removeAssay(scp, setdiff(names(scp), keep_assays))
rm(Prots); invisible(gc())
```

```{r processing-diagnostics, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
## completeness diagnostics (Jaccard overlap + cumulative sensitivity)
ji  <- jaccardIndex(scp, "Protein.Group")
csc <- cumulativeSensitivityCurve(scp, "Protein.Group", niters = 10, nsteps = 30)
pred <- predictSensitivity(csc, nSample = seq_len(ncol(scp[["Protein.Group"]])))
( ggplot(ji, aes(jaccard)) + geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
    labs(title = "Pairwise Jaccard (Protein.Group)") + theme_bw() ) +
( ggplot(csc, aes(SampleSize, Sensitivity)) + geom_point(size = 1) +
    geom_line(data = pred) + labs(title = "Cumulative sensitivity") + theme_bw() )
```

---

# Session 5 — Missing-value characterization

## 5.1 MNAR / MAR / MCAR diagnostics
<!-- Missingness vs intensity (MNAR), per-cell missingness vs QC, histograms,
     Little's test. (original Missing-value section) -->

```{r mv-diagnostics, fig.width=11, fig.height=4.5}
mat <- assay(scp[["Protein.Group"]])
cat(sprintf("Protein.Group missingness: %.1f%%\n", 100 * mean(is.na(mat))))

## per-protein and per-cell missingness. ABUNDANCE for the MNAR diagnostic comes from the
## non-centred Protein.Group_abund assay -- `mat` (Protein.Group) is row-centred per protein
## (~0 mean), so using it as an abundance axis inverts the MNAR relationship (spurious +rho).
.abund <- as.matrix(assay(scp[["Protein.Group_abund"]]))[rownames(mat), , drop = FALSE]
prot_stats <- data.frame(protein = rownames(mat),
                         mean_int = rowMeans(.abund, na.rm = TRUE),   # mean log2 abundance (non-centred)
                         na_frac  = rowMeans(is.na(mat)))
cell_stats <- data.frame(cell    = colnames(mat),
                         na_frac  = colMeans(is.na(mat)),
                         n_obs    = colSums(!is.na(mat)))
cell_stats$log_sumsRI <- colData(scp)[cell_stats$cell, "log_sumsRI"]

## MNAR diagnostic: missingness vs mean intensity (negative => MNAR)
mnar <- cor.test(prot_stats$mean_int, prot_stats$na_frac,
                 method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
cat(sprintf("MNAR diagnostic: Spearman rho = %.3f (p = %.1e)\n",
            mnar$estimate, mnar$p.value))

p_mnar <- ggplot(prot_stats, aes(mean_int, na_frac)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 1) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", colour = "firebrick") +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = 0.97, hjust = 1.05,
           label = sprintf("rho = %.2f", mnar$estimate)) +
  labs(x = "mean log2 protein abundance", y = "fraction missing",
       title = "Missingness vs abundance (MNAR)") + theme_bw()
p_cell <- ggplot(cell_stats, aes(log_sumsRI, na_frac)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) + geom_smooth(method = "lm", colour = "firebrick") +
  labs(x = "log_sumsRI", y = "fraction missing",
       title = "Per-cell missingness vs library size") + theme_bw()
print(p_mnar + p_cell)
save_fig(p_mnar + p_cell, "S5_missingness_diagnostics.png", w = 11, h = 4.5)
```

## 5.1b Global missing-value metrics

Three complementary views of the missingness at the global level: **(a)** the per-cell
missingness fraction is high (median ~62 %) and left-skewed; **(b)** the **MNAR** dropout
curve — detection climbs monotonically with protein abundance, so low-abundance proteins
are preferentially lost; and **(c)** the shared proteome shrinks steeply as the
completeness threshold rises (the ≥10 % filter retains the analysis set).

```{r global-missingness-metrics, fig.width=13, fig.height=4.2, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
MB <- 12; MACC <- "#2166AC"; MTHR <- "#B2182B"; MMIN <- PROC$marker_min_det
m_theme <- theme_bw(base_size = MB, base_family = "sans") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = MB, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = MB - 3, colour = "grey35"),
        axis.text = element_text(size = MB - 3, colour = "grey20"), panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
.cmf <- 100 * cell_stats$na_frac                       # % missing per cell
.pdet <- 100 * (1 - prot_stats$na_frac)                # per-protein detection %
## (a) per-cell missingness distribution
.gm1 <- ggplot(data.frame(mf = .cmf), aes(mf)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 20, fill = MACC, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.15, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_density(colour = MTHR, linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = median(.cmf), linetype = "dashed", colour = MTHR, linewidth = 0.6) +
  annotate("text", x = median(.cmf), y = Inf, label = sprintf(" median %.0f%%", median(.cmf)),
           hjust = 0, vjust = 1.8, size = (MB - 4)/.pt, colour = MTHR) +
  labs(x = "Missing per cell (%)", y = "Density", title = "Per-cell missingness distribution") + m_theme
## (b) MNAR dropout curve (detection vs abundance)
.gm2 <- ggplot(data.frame(int = prot_stats$mean_int, det = .pdet), aes(int, det)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.4, colour = "#BDBDBD", alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", span = 0.5, se = FALSE, colour = MACC, linewidth = 1) +
  labs(x = "Mean protein log-intensity (abundance)", y = "Detected in % of cells",
       title = "MNAR — dropout tracks abundance",
       subtitle = sprintf("Spearman(abundance, missingness) = %.2f", mnar$estimate)) + m_theme
## (c) core-proteome completeness curve
.thr <- 0:100; .ncore <- vapply(.thr, function(t) sum(.pdet >= t), integer(1))
.key <- data.frame(x = c(100*MMIN, 50, 100), n = c(sum(.pdet >= 100*MMIN), sum(.pdet >= 50), sum(.pdet >= 100)))
.gm3 <- ggplot(data.frame(thr = .thr, n = .ncore), aes(thr, n)) +
  geom_line(colour = MACC, linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 100*MMIN, linetype = "dashed", colour = MTHR, linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(data = .key, aes(x, n), colour = MTHR, size = 1.9) +
  geom_text(data = .key, aes(x, n, label = n), vjust = -0.8, size = (MB - 4)/.pt, colour = "grey20") +
  annotate("text", x = 100*MMIN, y = Inf, label = sprintf("  %.0f%% filter", 100*MMIN), hjust = 0, vjust = 1.6,
           size = (MB - 4)/.pt, colour = MTHR) +
  labs(x = "Detected in ≥ X% of cells", y = "Proteins retained", title = "Core-proteome completeness") + m_theme
.gpanel <- (.gm1 + .gm2 + .gm3) + patchwork::plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a",
              theme = theme(plot.tag = element_text(size = MB + 3, face = "bold")))
print(.gpanel)
cat(sprintf("per-cell missingness: median %.0f%% (range %.0f-%.0f); core proteome: %d at >=%.0f%%, %d in all cells\n",
            median(.cmf), min(.cmf), max(.cmf), sum(.pdet >= 100*MMIN), 100*MMIN, sum(.pdet >= 100)))
.gpf <- file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$fig, "Panels"); dir.create(.gpf, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
.gst <- file.path(.gpf, "S5_global_missingness_metrics")
try(ggplot2::ggsave(paste0(.gst, ".png"),  .gpanel, width = 13, height = 4.2, dpi = 300, device = grDevices::png,  type = "cairo"), silent = TRUE)
try(ggplot2::ggsave(paste0(.gst, ".pdf"),  .gpanel, width = 13, height = 4.2, device = grDevices::cairo_pdf), silent = TRUE)
try(ggplot2::ggsave(paste0(.gst, ".tiff"), .gpanel, width = 13, height = 4.2, dpi = 300, device = grDevices::tiff, type = "cairo", compression = "lzw"), silent = TRUE)
```

## 5.2 NA pattern clustering (NA_CellCluster, C5 module)
<!-- Binary NA clustering -> protein modules (k=5) + cell clusters (k=3);
     NA_Module_C5 nuclear module; store scores in colData. -->

```{r na-clustering}
## binary presence/absence matrix, restricted to proteins detected in >= 10% of cells
## (SAME protein subset as the §5.2b heatmap, so NA_CellCluster matches the visualised
##  hierarchical clustering rather than a different 10-90%-NA band).
na_bin <- ifelse(is.na(mat), 1L, 0L)
detected10 <- prot_stats$na_frac <= (1 - PROC$marker_min_det)   # detection >= 10%
nb <- na_bin[detected10, ]
cat(sprintf("Clustering missingness of %d proteins (>= %.0f%% detected) x %d cells\n",
            nrow(nb), 100 * PROC$marker_min_det, ncol(nb)))

## cluster proteins (modules) and cells by EUCLIDEAN distance + Ward.D2 — identical to
## the §5.2b heatmap's clustering (euclidean on 0/1 is invariant to the missing/present
## flip, so cutree(hc_cell) blocks align with the heatmap's column dendrogram).
hc_prot <- hclust(dist(nb,    method = "euclidean"), method = "ward.D2")
hc_cell <- hclust(dist(t(nb), method = "euclidean"), method = "ward.D2")
clust_prot <- cutree(hc_prot, k = PROC$na_k_prot)
clust_cell <- cutree(hc_cell, k = PROC$na_k_cell)

## store cell NA cluster in colData
colData(scp)$NA_CellCluster <- paste0("NA_C", clust_cell[colnames(mat)])
print(table(colData(scp)$NA_CellCluster))

## per-cell module score + detection fraction for each protein NA module
for (cl in seq_len(PROC$na_k_prot)) {
  cl_prots <- names(clust_prot[clust_prot == cl])
  sub <- mat[cl_prots, , drop = FALSE]
  colData(scp)[[sprintf("NA_Module_C%d_score", cl)]]         <- colMeans(sub, na.rm = TRUE)
  colData(scp)[[sprintf("NA_Module_C%d_detected_frac", cl)]] <- colMeans(!is.na(sub))
}
## keep the protein->module map for downstream (e.g. ORA on the C5 module)
rowData(scp[["Protein.Group"]])$NA_Cluster <-
  paste0("NA_C", clust_prot[rownames(mat)])
```

## 5.2b Hierarchical missingness heatmap

Clustering the **presence/absence** matrix — restricted to proteins detected in
≥ 10 % of cells (the 762 ultra-sparse proteins are dropped as mostly noise) — on both
axes shows the MNAR structure directly: proteins fall into detection tiers
(top = near-ubiquitous, bottom = rarely seen) and the cells order by depth. The
raw-loading `Log(SumRI)` and detection-fraction column bars track the column dendrogram,
the missingness-based `NA_CellCluster` (§5.2 — same subset, distance and linkage)
partitions the columns cleanly (NA_C3 occupies a distinct low-detection block), and the
row bar shows the **protein NA-modules** (§5.2 row clustering, `k = na_k_prot = 5`) —
co-missing protein groups that make up the detection tiers.

```{r missing-heatmap, fig.width=9, fig.height=8.5, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(pheatmap))
.cd <- as.data.frame(colData(scp)); .pf <- file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$fig)
B10  <- (!is.na(mat[rowMeans(!is.na(mat)) >= PROC$marker_min_det, ])) * 1L   # proteins detected in >= 10% of cells
## column (cell) annotation: raw loading Log(SumRI), detection %, and NA cell-cluster (§5.2)
ann_col <- data.frame(`Detected %` = 100 * colMeans(B10),
                      `Log(SumRI)` = .cd[colnames(B10), "log_sumsRI"],
                      NA_cluster   = .cd[colnames(B10), "NA_CellCluster"], check.names = FALSE)
rownames(ann_col) <- colnames(B10)
## row (protein) annotation: the missingness-based protein modules (§5.2, k = na_k_prot).
## rowData$NA_Cluster is cutree(hc_prot, k) on the SAME detected-10% proteins with the SAME
## euclidean/ward.D2 recipe, so its blocks align with this heatmap's row dendrogram.
.pmod   <- sub("^NA_C", "M", rowData(scp[["Protein.Group"]])[rownames(B10), "NA_Cluster"])
ann_row <- data.frame(`Protein module` = .pmod, check.names = FALSE)
rownames(ann_row) <- rownames(B10)
acol <- list(`Detected %`     = c("#f7fbff", "#08306b"),
             `Log(SumRI)`     = c("#fff5eb", "#7f2704"),
             NA_cluster       = c(NA_C1 = "#1B9E77", NA_C2 = "#D95F02", NA_C3 = "#7570B3"),
             `Protein module` = c(M1 = "#D55E00", M2 = "#F0E442", M3 = "#CC79A7", M4 = "#009E73", M5 = "#56B4E9"))
ph10 <- pheatmap(B10, color = c("#f0f0f0", "#2166AC"), legend_breaks = c(0.25, 0.75), legend_labels = c("missing", "detected"),
  cluster_rows = TRUE, cluster_cols = TRUE, clustering_distance_rows = "euclidean",
  clustering_distance_cols = "euclidean", clustering_method = "ward.D2",
  show_rownames = FALSE, show_colnames = FALSE, treeheight_row = 40, treeheight_col = 30,
  annotation_col = ann_col, annotation_row = ann_row, annotation_colors = acol, border_color = NA, silent = TRUE,
  main = sprintf("Missing-value structure, proteins detected >=%.0f%% of cells — %d proteins x %d cells",
                 100 * PROC$marker_min_det, nrow(B10), ncol(B10)))
## export PNG + PDF + TIFF (all 300 dpi), then render inline
grDevices::png(file.path(.pf, "S5_missing_heatmap_det10.png"), width = 9, height = 8.5, units = "in", res = 300, type = "cairo"); grid::grid.newpage(); grid::grid.draw(ph10$gtable); grDevices::dev.off()
grDevices::cairo_pdf(file.path(.pf, "S5_missing_heatmap_det10.pdf"), width = 9, height = 8.5); grid::grid.newpage(); grid::grid.draw(ph10$gtable); grDevices::dev.off()
grDevices::tiff(file.path(.pf, "S5_missing_heatmap_det10.tiff"), width = 9, height = 8.5, units = "in", res = 300, compression = "lzw", type = "cairo"); grid::grid.newpage(); grid::grid.draw(ph10$gtable); grDevices::dev.off()
grid::grid.newpage(); grid::grid.draw(ph10$gtable)
```

## 5.2c Export missingness-cluster assignments

The two missingness clusterings visualised above — the **NA cell-clusters**
(`k = na_k_cell`) and the **protein NA-modules** (`k = na_k_prot`) — are written out
as flat tables (plus a re-cuttable object) so they can be reused downstream.

```{r na-cluster-export, message=FALSE}
.cdx <- as.data.frame(colData(scp))
.rdx <- as.data.frame(rowData(scp[["Protein.Group"]]))
## cells: NA cell-cluster + detection / loading / QC metadata (one row per cell)
.cell_tab <- data.frame(
  cell              = colnames(mat),
  NA_CellCluster    = .cdx[colnames(mat), "NA_CellCluster"],
  n_proteins        = colSums(!is.na(mat)),
  detected_pct      = round(100 * colMeans(!is.na(mat)), 2),
  count             = .cdx[colnames(mat), "count"],
  log_sumsRI        = round(.cdx[colnames(mat), "log_sumsRI"], 3),
  log_sumsRI_NoCRAP = round(.cdx[colnames(mat), "log_sumsRI_NoCRAP"], 3),
  Trans_Diameter    = .cdx[colnames(mat), "Trans_Diameter"],
  contam_percent    = round(.cdx[colnames(mat), "contam_percent"], 2),
  check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
save_tab(.cell_tab, "S5_NA_cell_clusters.csv")
## proteins: NA module (M1..M<k> for detected >=10% proteins, else unclustered) + detection
.pmodx <- sub("^NA_C", "M", .rdx[rownames(mat), "NA_Cluster"]); .pmodx[.pmodx == "MNA"] <- "unclustered(<10%)"
.prot_tab <- data.frame(
  protein      = rownames(mat),
  gene         = .rdx[rownames(mat), "Genes"],
  NA_module    = .pmodx,
  detected_pct = round(100 * rowMeans(!is.na(mat)), 2),
  na_frac      = round(rowMeans(is.na(mat)), 3),
  mean_log_int = round(rowMeans(mat, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
  check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
save_tab(.prot_tab, "S5_NA_protein_modules.csv")
## re-cuttable clustering object: the two dendrograms + the assignments at the chosen k
saveRDS(list(hc_cell = hc_cell, hc_prot = hc_prot,
             NA_CellCluster = setNames(.cell_tab$NA_CellCluster, .cell_tab$cell),
             protein_module = setNames(.prot_tab$NA_module, .prot_tab$protein),
             k_cell = PROC$na_k_cell, k_prot = PROC$na_k_prot),
        file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$obj, "S5_NA_clustering.rds"))
cat(sprintf("exported cells: %s | protein modules: %s (+%d unclustered)\n",
    paste(names(table(.cell_tab$NA_CellCluster)), table(.cell_tab$NA_CellCluster), sep = "=", collapse = ", "),
    paste(names(table(.prot_tab$NA_module[.prot_tab$NA_module != "unclustered(<10%)"])),
          table(.prot_tab$NA_module[.prot_tab$NA_module != "unclustered(<10%)"]), sep = "=", collapse = ", "),
    sum(.prot_tab$NA_module == "unclustered(<10%)")))
```

## 5.3 NA_C3 — quality vs biology
<!-- CR9: NA_C3 is enriched for trajectory-bad cells (OR 7.4) but entangled with
     low input (smaller, shallower). Treat as a FLAG / biology question, not a
     hard filter. Size-matched test of the C5-absence signature. -->

```{r na-c3-qc, fig.width=10, fig.height=4}
## Characterize the NA cell clusters. The 'absence' cluster (NA_C3 in the
## original) is the one with the lowest overall detection / module score.
cd <- as.data.frame(colData(scp))
cd$overall_det <- colMeans(!is.na(mat))[rownames(cd)]

na_summary <- cd |>
  dplyr::group_by(NA_CellCluster) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n         = dplyr::n(),
                   diameter  = median(Trans_Diameter, na.rm = TRUE),
                   count     = median(count,          na.rm = TRUE),
                   detection = median(overall_det,    na.rm = TRUE),
                   .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::arrange(detection)
print(na_summary)
absence <- na_summary$NA_CellCluster[1]
cat(sprintf("Absence cluster (lowest detection) = %s\n", absence))
save_tab(na_summary, "S5_NA_cluster_summary.csv")

p1 <- ggplot(cd, aes(NA_CellCluster, Trans_Diameter, fill = NA_CellCluster)) +
  geom_violin(alpha = .7) + geom_boxplot(width = .15, outlier.size = .4) +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "none") + labs(title = "Cell size by NA cluster")
p2 <- ggplot(cd, aes(NA_CellCluster, count, fill = NA_CellCluster)) +
  geom_violin(alpha = .7) + geom_boxplot(width = .15, outlier.size = .4) +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "none") + labs(title = "Depth (count) by NA cluster")
print(p1 + p2); save_fig(p1 + p2, "S5_NA_cluster_size_depth.png", w = 10, h = 4)
```

**Interpretation (CR9).** The absence cluster (`r` the one printed above; `NA_C3`
in the original) is **enriched for the trajectory-bad cells** (odds ratio ≈ 7.4
vs the rest) — but it is also **smaller and shallower**, i.e. entangled with the
low-input axis rather than orthogonal to it. So missingness clustering is a
useful *flag* (and a biology question — the structured nuclear-module loss), but
**not a clean QC filter**: hard-rejecting it removes nearly as many good cells as
bad. We therefore keep it as an annotation and rely on the Session 3 gate +
Session 10 compositional check for actual filtering.

## 5.3b NA_C3 absence signature — a coordinated, module-specific protein loss

The `absence` cell-cluster is defined by a **protein module that is detected everywhere
except in these cells**. We characterise that module: (i) its GO-BP function, (ii) whether
its functional coherence exceeds chance (1000× permutation), and (iii) whether the loss is
biological rather than a technical artifact of cell size, proteome depth, or subcellular
compartment. The heavy analysis (incl. the permutation) is **cached** to
`S5_absence_results.rds` — delete it to recompute.

```{r absence-analysis, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(GO.db); library(AnnotationDbi); library(parallel)})
.absres <- file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$obj, "S5_absence_results.rds")
if (file.exists(.absres)) { ABS <- readRDS(.absres) } else {
  set.seed(101)
  .m   <- as.matrix(assay(scp[["Protein.Group"]])); .ab <- as.matrix(assay(scp[["Protein.Group_abund"]]))
  .cdA <- as.data.frame(colData(scp)); .fg <- function(x) sub(";.*$", "", x)
  .cl  <- setNames(as.character(.cdA$NA_CellCluster), rownames(.cdA))
  .c3  <- names(.cl)[.cl == absence]; .rest <- setdiff(colnames(.m), .c3)
  ## protein modules from §5.2; the absence module = largest C3-vs-rest detection gap
  .pmod <- setNames(as.character(rowData(scp[["Protein.Group"]])$NA_Cluster), rownames(.m))
  .mods <- sort(unique(.pmod[grepl("^NA_C[0-9]+$", .pmod)]))
  .gap  <- sapply(.mods, function(m){ g <- names(.pmod)[.pmod == m]; mean(!is.na(.m[g, .rest])) - mean(!is.na(.m[g, .c3])) })
  .absmod <- names(.gap)[which.max(.gap)]; .absprot <- names(.pmod)[.pmod == .absmod]
  .detC3 <- rowMeans(!is.na(.m[, .c3]))*100; .detR <- rowMeans(!is.na(.m[, .rest]))*100
  ## ---- GO BP: real enrichment + 1000x permutation ----
  .univ <- unique(.fg(rownames(.m))); .univ <- .univ[.univ %in% keys(org.Hs.eg.db, "SYMBOL")]
  .gbp  <- suppressMessages(AnnotationDbi::select(org.Hs.eg.db, keys = .univ, columns = c("GOALL","ONTOLOGYALL"), keytype = "SYMBOL"))
  .t2g  <- unique(.gbp[!is.na(.gbp$GOALL) & .gbp$ONTOLOGYALL == "BP", c("GOALL","SYMBOL")])
  .t2n  <- suppressMessages(AnnotationDbi::select(GO.db, keys = unique(.t2g$GOALL), columns = "TERM", keytype = "GOID"))[, c("GOID","TERM")]
  .qg <- intersect(unique(.fg(.absprot)), .univ); .nq <- length(.qg)
  .real <- clusterProfiler::enricher(.qg, universe = .univ, TERM2GENE = .t2g, TERM2NAME = .t2n,
             pAdjustMethod = "BH", pvalueCutoff = 1, qvalueCutoff = 1, minGSSize = 10, maxGSSize = 500)@result
  .gr <- do.call(rbind, lapply(strsplit(.real$GeneRatio, "/"), as.numeric)); .brr <- do.call(rbind, lapply(strsplit(.real$BgRatio, "/"), as.numeric))
  .real$Fold <- (.gr[,1]/.gr[,2]) / (.brr[,1]/.brr[,2]); .Nobs <- sum(.real$p.adjust < 0.05)
  .run1 <- function(i){ set.seed(10000+i); er <- clusterProfiler::enricher(sample(.univ, .nq), universe = .univ, TERM2GENE = .t2g,
             pAdjustMethod = "BH", pvalueCutoff = 1, qvalueCutoff = 1, minGSSize = 10, maxGSSize = 500); if (is.null(er)) 0L else sum(er@result$p.adjust < 0.05) }
  .NP <- 1000
  .null <- tryCatch({ cl <- makeCluster(max(1L, detectCores()-2L)); on.exit(stopCluster(cl), add = TRUE)
      clusterEvalQ(cl, suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(clusterProfiler))); clusterExport(cl, c(".t2g",".univ",".nq"), envir = environment())
      unlist(parLapply(cl, seq_len(.NP), .run1)) }, error = function(e) unlist(lapply(seq_len(.NP), .run1)))
  .empp <- (1 + sum(.null >= .Nobs)) / (.NP + 1)
  ## ---- size + diameter matching (<=1um) + paired detection ----
  .diam <- setNames(.cdA$Trans_Diameter, rownames(.cdA))
  .wall <- wilcox.test(.diam[.c3], .diam[colnames(.m)])$p.value; .wrest <- wilcox.test(.diam[.c3], .diam[.rest])$p.value
  .oc <- .c3[order(.diam[.c3])]; .used <- character(0); .mp <- list()
  for (cc in .oc){ av <- setdiff(.rest, .used); dd <- abs(.diam[av] - .diam[cc]); j <- which.min(dd); if (length(j) && dd[j] <= 1){ .mp[[cc]] <- av[j]; .used <- c(.used, av[j]) } }
  .matched <- data.frame(c3 = names(.mp), ctrl = unlist(.mp), row.names = NULL)
  .dcell <- colMeans(!is.na(.m[.absprot, ]))*100
  .matched$det_c3 <- .dcell[.matched$c3]; .matched$det_ctrl <- .dcell[.matched$ctrl]
  .matched$count_c3 <- .cdA[.matched$c3,"count"]; .matched$count_ctrl <- .cdA[.matched$ctrl,"count"]
  .matched$d_c3 <- .diam[.matched$c3]; .matched$d_ctrl <- .diam[.matched$ctrl]
  .wpair <- wilcox.test(.matched$det_c3, .matched$det_ctrl, paired = TRUE)$p.value
  .wcount <- wilcox.test(.matched$count_c3, .matched$count_ctrl, paired = TRUE)$p.value
  ## ---- module specificity (within-cell) ----
  .detmod <- sapply(.mods, function(m) colMeans(!is.na(.m[names(.pmod)[.pmod == m], ]))*100); rownames(.detmod) <- colnames(.m)
  .reldef <- .detmod[, .absmod] - rowMeans(.detmod[, setdiff(.mods, .absmod), drop = FALSE])
  .wint <- wilcox.test(.reldef[.c3], .reldef[.rest])$p.value
  ## ---- ranked intensity (are absence proteins just the dimmest?) ----
  .mint <- rowMeans(.m, na.rm = TRUE)
  .rankdf <- data.frame(rank = rank(.mint, ties.method = "first"), mint = .mint, is_abs = rownames(.m) %in% .absprot)
  ## ---- compartment (GO CC) + within-nuclear + size proxy ----
  .cc <- .gbp; .cc <- suppressMessages(AnnotationDbi::select(org.Hs.eg.db, keys = .univ, columns = c("GOALL","ONTOLOGYALL"), keytype = "SYMBOL"))
  .cc <- .cc[!is.na(.cc$GOALL) & .cc$ONTOLOGYALL == "CC", c("SYMBOL","GOALL")]
  COMP <- c(Nucleus="GO:0005634", Spliceosome="GO:0005681", Cytosol="GO:0005829", Mitochondrion="GO:0005739", `Plasma membrane`="GO:0005886")
  .psym <- .fg(rownames(.m)); .flag <- sapply(COMP, function(go) .psym %in% unique(.cc$SYMBOL[.cc$GOALL == go])); rownames(.flag) <- rownames(.m)
  .comptab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(.mods, function(m){ g <- names(.pmod)[.pmod == m]; data.frame(module = m, compartment = names(COMP), pct = round(100*colMeans(.flag[g, , drop = FALSE]), 1)) }))
  .d10 <- rownames(.m)[rowMeans(!is.na(.m)) >= 0.10]; .wd <- rownames(.m)[rowMeans(!is.na(.m)) >= 0.50]
  .nuc <- intersect(rownames(.m)[.flag[,"Nucleus"]], .d10)
  .nucA <- intersect(intersect(.nuc, .absprot), .wd); .nucN <- intersect(setdiff(.nuc, .absprot), .wd)
  .wnuc <- wilcox.test(.detC3[.nucN], .detC3[.nucA])$p.value
  .pep <- tryCatch({ .pa <- intersect(c("peptides","peptides_log_noNorm"), names(scp))[1]
      .rp <- as.data.frame(rowData(scp[[.pa]])); .npp <- tapply(.rp$Stripped.Sequence, .rp$Genes, function(x) length(unique(x)))
      setNames(as.integer(.npp[.fg(rownames(.m))]), rownames(.m)) }, error = function(e) NULL)
  ## ---- heatmap red-box coords (M5 rows x C3 cols in the §5.2 dendrogram order) ----
  .ro <- rownames(nb)[hc_prot$order]; .co <- colnames(nb)[hc_cell$order]
  .ri <- which(.pmod[.ro] == .absmod); .ci <- which(.cl[.co] == absence)
  .box <- list(r1 = min(.ri), r2 = max(.ri), nr = length(.ro), c1 = min(.ci), c2 = max(.ci), nc = length(.co))
  ABS <- list(absmod = .absmod, absML = sub("NA_C","M",.absmod), absprot = .absprot, absence = absence,
    c3 = .c3, rest = .rest, cl = .cl, pmod = .pmod, mods = .mods, detC3 = .detC3, detR = .detR,
    real = .real[order(-.real$Fold), ], Nobs = .Nobs, null = .null, empp = .empp, nperm = .NP,
    diam = .diam, wall = .wall, wrest = .wrest, matched = .matched, wpair = .wpair, wcount = .wcount,
    detmod = .detmod, reldef = .reldef, wint = .wint, rankdf = .rankdf, comptab = .comptab, COMP = COMP,
    nucA = .nucA, nucN = .nucN, wnuc = .wnuc, pep = .pep, box = .box, det10 = .d10,
    hc_cell = hc_cell, hc_prot = hc_prot, mat = .m)
  saveRDS(ABS, .absres)
}
cat(sprintf("absence module %s (%d proteins): C3 detection %.1f%% vs rest %.1f%% | GO sig terms %d, perm p<%.3g | matched %d cells, det %.1f%% vs %.1f%% (paired p=%.1g) | within-nuclear non-M5 %.0f%% vs M5 %.0f%% (p=%.1g)\n",
    ABS$absML, length(ABS$absprot), mean(ABS$detC3[ABS$absprot]), mean(ABS$detR[ABS$absprot]),
    ABS$Nobs, 1/(ABS$nperm+1), nrow(ABS$matched), mean(ABS$matched$det_c3), mean(ABS$matched$det_ctrl), ABS$wpair,
    median(ABS$detC3[ABS$nucN]), median(ABS$detC3[ABS$nucA]), ABS$wnuc))
```

**Interpretation.** The `absence` cluster is defined by a **coordinated, module-specific loss
of splicing / RNA-processing machinery** (module `r ABS$absML` — detected in ~10 % of NA_C3
cells vs ~90 % elsewhere). The loss is **not technical**: NA_C3 cells are not smaller, and even
matched on size (and at balanced depth) module-`r ABS$absML` detection stays ~10 % vs ~90 % in
controls; within the same C3 cells other modules (esp. M3) stay ~84 % detected, and C3 recovers
non-module-`r ABS$absML` **nuclear** proteins at ~80 % — so it is not a nuclear-compartment
recovery failure. The functional coherence far exceeds chance (permutation p < 0.001).

# Session 6 — Modeling & dimensionality reduction (scplainer)

## 6.1 Minimal model (~ 1 + log_sumsRI_NoCRAP)
<!-- scpModelWorkflow(minimal), filter NP ratio, variance analysis, APCA
     component analysis, residual biplots (cluster / markers / GLUD1 / TUBB3 /
     C5 overlay). This residual space feeds clustering AND the trajectory. -->

```{r scplainer-minimal, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
## Session 6 is CACHED AS A WHOLE: sce_minimal.rds holds the fitted scplainer
## model + APCA reducedDims (residuals/unmodelled/APCA_log_sumsRI) + the shared
## compPCA + the biplot loadings. Loading it skips the in-knit
## scpComponentAnalysis(APCA), which can hard-crash a single-process knit via heap
## fragmentation. Delete sce_minimal.rds to force full recomputation.
## Compositional PCA, factored out so BOTH the fresh branch and the cache self-heal
## below can build it. Same recipe as the Session-10 trajectory's compPCA but on ALL
## 131 cells (no 22% drop): regress out log_sumsRI per protein + per-cell centre ->
## scaled PCA. prcomp computes the protein loadings anyway; we now KEEP them (they
## used to be discarded, which left the §8.5 biplot with no arrows to draw).
.compPCA_fit <- function(scp) {
  cpg  <- assay(scp[["Protein.Group"]]); ccd <- as.data.frame(colData(scp))
  cpg  <- cpg[rowMeans(!is.na(cpg)) >= 0.30, ]          # >=30%-detected proteins
  czls <- with(ccd, (log_sumsRI_NoCRAP - mean(log_sumsRI_NoCRAP, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(log_sumsRI_NoCRAP, na.rm = TRUE))
  cres <- t(apply(cpg, 1, function(y) { ok <- !is.na(y); r <- rep(NA_real_, length(y))
    b <- coef(stats::lm(y[ok] ~ czls[ok])); r[ok] <- y[ok] - (b[1] + b[2] * czls[ok]); r }))
  dimnames(cres) <- dimnames(cpg)
  cres <- sweep(cres, 2, colMeans(cres, na.rm = TRUE), "-")
  cres0 <- cres; cres0[is.na(cres0)] <- 0; cres0 <- cres0[apply(cres0, 1, var) > 0, ]
  pc <- prcomp(t(cres0), center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE, rank. = min(30, ncol(cres0) - 1))
  list(x = pc$x, rotation = pc$rotation,
       pctVar = 100 * pc$sdev^2 / sum(pc$sdev^2),               # REAL percentVar
       det    = rowMeans(!is.na(cpg))[rownames(pc$rotation)])   # per-protein detection
}

.s6_done <- file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$obj, "sce_minimal.rds")
if (file.exists(.s6_done)) {
  sce <- readRDS(.s6_done)
  scp <- removeAssay(scp, intersect(c("peptides", "peptides_log_noNorm"), names(scp)))
  invisible(gc())
  print(scpModelFilterPlot(sce))
  cat("Session 6 loaded from cache. reducedDims:",
      paste(reducedDimNames(sce), collapse = ", "), "\n")
} else {
## SCE for scplainer = minimal-processing (un-normalized) log peptides
sce <- scp[["peptides_log_noNorm"]]
colData(sce) <- colData(scp)

## scp's peptide-level assays are not used past this point (Sessions 7-10 use
## `sce` and scp[["Protein.Group"]]); drop them so the model fit + APCA below
## have headroom on low-RAM machines. Protein.Group is kept for Sessions 8/10.
scp <- removeAssay(scp, intersect(c("peptides", "peptides_log_noNorm"), names(scp)))
invisible(gc())

## minimal model: peptide ~ 1 + log_sumsRI  (removes library-size variance only,
## so differentiation signal is preserved -- this residual space feeds both
## clustering (Session 7) and the trajectory (Session 10)).
## CACHE the ~12-min fit to disk: a re-knit then skips the refit AND avoids the
## heap fragmentation it causes, which otherwise crashes the APCA step below on
## low-RAM machines. Delete sce_S6_postfit.rds to force a refit.
.s6_fit <- file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$obj, "sce_S6_postfit.rds")
if (file.exists(.s6_fit)) {
  sce <- readRDS(.s6_fit)
} else {
  sce <- scpModelWorkflow(sce, formula = PROC$minimal_form)
  scpModelFilterThreshold(sce) <- 1
  saveRDS(sce, .s6_fit)
}
print(scpModelFilterPlot(sce))

## (variance analysis of this fit is done once, for both cache branches, in §8.4)

## APCA on residuals -> component scores added as the 'residuals' reducedDim.
## APCA transiently allocates ~4 GB (verified: max-used Vcells ~3.9 GB on this
## 14.5k-peptide x 131-cell set), so free memory first for low-RAM safety.
invisible(gc())
caRes      <- scpComponentAnalysis(sce, ncomp = 10, method = "APCA")
sce$cell   <- colnames(sce)
caResCells <- scpAnnotateResults(caRes$bySample,  colData(sce), by = "cell")
caResPeps  <- scpAnnotateResults(caRes$byFeature, rowData(sce),
                                 by = "feature", by2 = "Genes")
sce <- addReducedDims(sce, caResCells)
cat("reducedDims:", paste(reducedDimNames(sce), collapse = ", "), "\n")
## NOTE: downstream uses the residual embedding name 'residuals' (verify above).

## store residual-APCA peptide loadings (Gene-annotated) on the object so the
## Session 8.6 biplot can use them once clustering/identity are available.
.lo <- data.frame(caRes$byFeature[["residuals"]])
.lo$Genes <- rowData(sce)$Genes[match(.lo$feature, rowData(sce)$Stripped.Sequence)]
metadata(sce)$apca_loadings <- .lo

print(scpComponentPlot(caResCells, pointParams = list(aes())))

## --- shared COMPOSITIONAL embedding for clustering/UMAP (Session 7) ----------
## This unifies the clustering/UMAP space with the trajectory space. (The
## scplainer residual APCA above is retained for the Session-8.6 biplot; the
## loadings kept here feed the Session-8.5 compPCA biplot.)
.cp <- .compPCA_fit(scp)
reducedDim(sce, "compPCA") <- .cp$x[colnames(sce), seq_len(min(15, ncol(.cp$x))), drop = FALSE]
metadata(sce)$compPCA_loadings  <- .cp$rotation[, seq_len(min(15, ncol(.cp$rotation))), drop = FALSE]
metadata(sce)$compPCA_pctVar    <- .cp$pctVar
metadata(sce)$compPCA_detection <- .cp$det
cat("compPCA (shared clustering/UMAP/trajectory embedding):",
    paste(dim(reducedDim(sce, "compPCA")), collapse = " x "),
    sprintf("| PC1 %.1f%% PC2 %.1f%% | %d protein loadings kept\n", .cp$pctVar[1], .cp$pctVar[2], nrow(.cp$rotation)))
rm(.cp); invisible(gc())

saveRDS(sce, .s6_done)
}

## --- compPCA loadings self-heal ------------------------------------------------
## Caches written before the §8.5 biplot existed hold compPCA scores but no loadings,
## so the cache-hit branch above would leave §8.5 with no arrows. Rebuild them once
## and refresh the cache (deterministic: same recipe + same data -> same rotation).
if (is.null(metadata(sce)$compPCA_loadings)) {
  .cp <- .compPCA_fit(scp)
  metadata(sce)$compPCA_loadings  <- .cp$rotation[, seq_len(min(15, ncol(.cp$rotation))), drop = FALSE]
  metadata(sce)$compPCA_pctVar    <- .cp$pctVar
  metadata(sce)$compPCA_detection <- .cp$det
  saveRDS(sce, .s6_done); rm(.cp); invisible(gc())
  cat("Session 6: compPCA loadings absent from cache -> computed and re-saved\n")
}

## --- END OF SESSION 6: propagate the current §5.2 NA-clustering to `sce` --------
## Runs in EVERY branch (whole-session cache / fit-only cache / fresh fit). The two
## cache paths can carry an OLDER missingness clustering baked into the cached colData,
## so overwrite all NA_* columns on the end-of-Session-6 object from the freshly
## recomputed `scp` (§5.2, aligned to the §5.2b heatmap). This is the single point that
## guarantees Session 7's NA_CellCluster UMAP/ARI — and any later reader of
## sce_minimal.rds — see the CURRENT clustering. Re-save the cache only when it actually
## held a different clustering, so a stale cache self-heals without needless large I/O.
.nacols   <- grep("^NA_", colnames(colData(scp)), value = TRUE)
.na_cur   <- as.data.frame(colData(scp))[colnames(sce), .nacols, drop = FALSE]   # fresh (§5.2)
.na_old   <- tryCatch(as.data.frame(colData(sce))[, .nacols, drop = FALSE],      # cached (NULL if a col is absent)
                      error = function(e) NULL)
.na_stale <- is.null(.na_old) || !isTRUE(all.equal(.na_old, .na_cur, check.attributes = FALSE))
for (.c in .nacols) colData(sce)[[.c]] <- colData(scp)[colnames(sce), .c]
if (.na_stale) {
  saveRDS(sce, .s6_done)
  cat("Session 6: NA-clustering changed -> refreshed sce NA_* colData + re-saved sce_minimal.rds\n")
}
cat("end-of-Session-6 NA_CellCluster:",
    paste(names(table(colData(sce)$NA_CellCluster)), table(colData(sce)$NA_CellCluster),
          sep = "=", collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

## 6.2 Cluster model (~ 1 + log_sumsRI_NoCRAP + Cluster) — deferred to Session 9

The cluster-aware model `~ 1 + log_sumsRI_NoCRAP + Cluster` requires the cluster labels
produced in **Session 7**, so it is fit in **Session 9** (Differential
expression), where it is the basis for the cluster contrasts. Keeping it there
avoids a forward dependency in the linear knit order.

---

# Session 7 — Clustering & embedding

<!-- scran clusterCells(NNGraph k=clust_k=10, louvain) on the shared compPCA
     (minimal-model residuals); UMAP/t-SNE; coloured by cluster and NA_CellCluster.
     §7.1 fixes the neighbourhood k (silhouette + stability) BEFORE §7.2 clusters at it. -->

Graph-based clustering runs on the shared `compPCA` embedding: an SNN graph is built on
each cell's *k* nearest neighbours and partitioned by **Louvain** (the number of clusters is
*emergent*, not preset — there is no *k*-means here). The neighbourhood size *k* is the one
free knob, so we fix it first with a sweep (§7.1) and only then cluster (§7.2).

## 7.1 Choosing k — silhouette + stability sweep

To make the **k = 10** choice explicit, we sweep the SNN neighbourhood size (k = 4–30 on the
131-cell `compPCA`) and judge each resulting Louvain partition on two internal criteria only:
how well-separated the clusters are (**silhouette**, higher = better) and how reproducible the
partition is across 10 random Louvain seeds (**stability** = mean pairwise ARI, higher =
better). No external cell-type labels are used — this is purely how strongly the *data*
supports each granularity.

```{r cluster-ksweep, fig.width=10, fig.height=4.5}
.rd <- reducedDim(sce, "compPCA")
## adjusted Rand index — used only for the seed-to-seed stability metric
.ari <- function(a, b) { a <- as.integer(factor(a)); b <- as.integer(factor(b)); ok <- !is.na(a) & !is.na(b)
  a <- a[ok]; b <- b[ok]; tb <- table(a, b); n <- sum(tb); if (n < 2) return(NA); ai <- rowSums(tb); bj <- colSums(tb)
  idx <- sum(choose(tb, 2)); ex <- sum(choose(ai, 2)) * sum(choose(bj, 2)) / choose(n, 2)
  m <- 0.5 * (sum(choose(ai, 2)) + sum(choose(bj, 2))); if (m == ex) 1 else (idx - ex) / (m - ex) }
.sw <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 15, 20, 25, 30), function(k) {
  parts <- lapply(1:10, function(s) { set.seed(s)
    as.integer(clusterCells(sce, use.dimred = "compPCA", BLUSPARAM = NNGraphParam(k = k, cluster.fun = "louvain"))) })
  set.seed(101); cl <- clusterCells(sce, use.dimred = "compPCA", BLUSPARAM = NNGraphParam(k = k, cluster.fun = "louvain"))
  data.frame(k = k, nClust = nlevels(cl),
             silhouette = round(mean(bluster::approxSilhouette(.rd, cl)$width), 3),
             stability  = round(mean(combn(10, 2, function(ij) .ari(parts[[ij[1]]], parts[[ij[2]]]))), 2)) }))
print(.sw, row.names = FALSE); save_tab(.sw, "S7_ksweep.csv")

.long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("silhouette", "stability"), function(m)
  data.frame(k = .sw$k, nClust = .sw$nClust, metric = m, value = .sw[[m]])))
.lab <- c(silhouette = "Silhouette (internal separation, higher = better)",
          stability  = "Stability across Louvain seeds (higher = better)")
.long$metric <- factor(.lab[.long$metric], levels = .lab)
p_kd <- ggplot(.long, aes(k, value)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 10, colour = "#B2182B", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_line(colour = "grey55") + geom_point(aes(colour = nClust == 4), size = 2.4) +
  geom_text(data = .sw, aes(x = k, y = Inf, label = paste0(nClust, "c")), vjust = 1.4, size = 2.7, colour = "grey40", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey55", `TRUE` = "#B2182B"), guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "k (SNN neighbours) — red dashed = chosen k = 10 (4 clusters); top labels = n clusters", y = NULL,
       title = "Cluster-number k-sweep: silhouette + stability") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11), strip.text = element_text(size = 8.5))
print(p_kd); save_fig(p_kd, "S7_ksweep.png", 10, 4.5)
```

Silhouette **peaks sharply at k = 10 → 4 clusters** (≈ 0.18) — the best-separated partition,
clearly above even the coarse 2-cluster plateau (≈ 0.16) — so 4 clusters is the granularity
the `compPCA` structure most supports, and the k carried into §7.2. That partition is also
**reproducible across seeds** (stability ≈ 0.90), only marginally below the coarser 2-cluster
cut. The one intrinsic caveat is that the cells lie on a **developmental continuum**, so any
hard partition is a simplification. **The trajectory / pseudotime is therefore the primary
model of this data; the 4 clusters are a defensible, silhouette-optimal overlay for marker /
enrichment analysis — not a claim of 4 discrete cell types.** (Cluster reproducibility is
re-checked with Leiden in §9.3.)

## 7.2 Clustering at k = 10

The chosen **k = `clust_k` = 10** SNN graph is partitioned by **Louvain** into **4
clusters**, and the cells are laid out with UMAP and t-SNE (both on `compPCA`). (The finer
**k = `nn_k` = 6** is used *only* for the Session 10 trajectory graph, where more granular
clusters help slingshot resolve lineages; `umap_nn = 20` / t-SNE `perplexity = 20` shape the
2-D layout only and do not affect the clustering.)

```{r clustering, fig.width=7, fig.height=6}
## graph-based clustering on the minimal-model residual embedding
set.seed(101)   # Louvain community detection is stochastic -> fix for reproducibility
nn.clusters <- clusterCells(sce, use.dimred = "compPCA",
                            BLUSPARAM = NNGraphParam(k = PROC$clust_k,
                                                     cluster.fun = PROC$clust_fun))
colLabels(sce) <- nn.clusters
print(table(colLabels(sce)))

## embeddings (seed for reproducibility)
set.seed(101); sce <- runUMAP(sce, dimred = "compPCA", n_neighbors = PROC$umap_nn)
set.seed(101); sce <- runTSNE(sce, dimred = "compPCA", perplexity = 20)

p_umap <- plotUMAP(sce, colour_by = "label", text_by = "label",
                   point_size = 3, point_alpha = 1) +
  ggtitle(sprintf("UMAP (compPCA, %s k = %d)", PROC$clust_fun, PROC$clust_k))
print(p_umap); save_fig(p_umap, "S7_UMAP_clusters.png", w = 7, h = 6)

print(plotUMAP(sce, colour_by = "NA_CellCluster", point_size = 3, point_alpha = 1) +
        ggtitle("UMAP — NA cell cluster"))

## carry cluster labels to scp colData (used by the cluster model in Session 9)
colData(scp)$Cluster <- as.character(colLabels(sce))
saveRDS(sce, file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$obj, "sce_clustered.rds"))
```
