# Session 8 — Cell-type identity

## 8.1 Marker module scores (consolidated)

Cell-type/state identity is scored with 23 IF-validated cortical-organoid marker
panels under two inclusion rules that keep the scores robust to SCP's sparse
detection: a **marker counts only if detected in ≥ `PROC$marker_min_det` (10%) of
cells**, and a **module is scored only if ≥ 3 of its markers clear that bar**. This
yields **11 usable modules** and is *insensitive* to the threshold (the same 11 pass
whether the bar is ≥1 cell or ≥10%) — the usable panels ride on abundant
structural/metabolic markers, whereas the ultra-sparse low-copy markers it prunes
(e.g. SNAP25 4 %, AQP4 3 %, PROX1 4 %) were not load-bearing. Two modules lean on
shared markers after pruning: **Astrocyte** loses its mature markers
(AQP4 / SLC1A2 / ALDH1L1) and rests on radial-glia / pan-glial proteins, and
**CGE_interneurons** is borderline (exactly 3 markers).

<!-- Replaces the ~80-chunk marker zoo: curated gene-set module scores per
     category (progenitor, immature/mature neuron, glutamatergic, GABAergic,
     astroglia, OPC, proliferating) + faceted UMAP panel. -->

```{r identity-modules, fig.width=13, fig.height=6}
mat <- assay(scp[["Protein.Group"]])

## IF-validated cortical-organoid marker modules (from
## 'cortical organoid markers_scProt_MGL.xlsx'; 23 cell-type/state panels).
## Replaces the old ad-hoc set. NB: single-cell proteomics under-detects the
## TF/receptor-heavy modules, so scoring/AUCell below use only the modules with
## >= 3 detected proteins (`marker_sets_det`); the rest are kept for the
## detection table / completeness.
marker_sets <- list(
  Cortical_identity        = c("FOXG1","EMX1","EMX2","PAX6","EOMES","TBR1","BCL11B","SATB2","NEUROD2","NEUROD6"),
  Neural_progenitors       = c("SOX2","NES","PAX6","VIM","HES1","HES5","NOTCH1","PROM1","MKI67","TOP2A","MCM2","PCNA"),
  Radial_glia              = c("SOX2","PAX6","VIM","FABP7","HOPX","PTPRZ1","TNC","FAM107A","MOXD1","LIFR","NES"),
  Intermediate_progenitors = c("EOMES","NEUROD1","NEUROD2","NEUROG1","NEUROG2","ASCL1","BTG2","DLL3","NHLH1","NHLH2","PPP1R17"),
  Immature_neurons         = c("DCX","STMN2","TUBB3","MAPT","NEUROD1","NEUROD2","NEUROD6","ELAVL2","ELAVL3","SOX11","SOX4"),
  Pan_neuronal             = c("RBFOX3","MAP2","SNAP25","SYT1","SYN1","TUBB3","STMN2","MAPT","UCHL1","ELAVL3","ELAVL4"),
  Glutamatergic_neurons    = c("SLC17A6","SLC17A7","SLC17A8","TBR1","SATB2","BCL11B","NEUROD2","NEUROD6","CAMK2A","NPTX1","NRN1","NRXN1","GRIN1","GRIN2B","GRIA1","GRIA2"),
  Deep_layer_excitatory    = c("TBR1","BCL11B","FEZF2","SOX5","FOXP2","PCP4","ZFPM2","CTIP2"),
  Upper_layer_excitatory   = c("SATB2","CUX1","CUX2","POU3F2","POU3F3","RORB","LHX2","BRN2"),
  GABAergic_neurons        = c("GAD1","GAD2","SLC32A1","DLX1","DLX2","DLX5","DLX6","DLX6-AS1","ARX","SP8","PBX3","SCG5","TAC1","SST","CALB2","RELN","VIP","LAMP5"),
  MGE_interneurons         = c("NKX2-1","LHX6","SOX6","MAF","MAFB","SST","PVALB","ERBB4"),
  CGE_interneurons         = c("NR2F1","NR2F2","SP8","PROX1","VIP","RELN","LAMP5","CALB2","ADARB2"),
  Astrocyte                = c("GFAP","AQP4","S100B","ALDH1L1","SLC1A2","SLC1A3","SOX9","GJA1","GLUL","APOE","CLU","FGFR3","NDRG2","AGT","ALDOC","SPARCL1","SLC6A11"),
  Immature_astrocyte       = c("FABP7","VIM","HES1","HES5","SOX2","PAX6","NES","HOPX","PTPRZ1","TNC"),
  Reactive_astrocyte       = c("GFAP","VIM","CD44","C3","SERPINA3","CHI3L1","STAT3","IFITM3","APOE","CLU","LCN2"),
  OPC                      = c("PDGFRA","CSPG4","OLIG1","OLIG2","SOX10","NKX2-2","GPR17","VCAN","PTPRZ1","BCAN"),
  Immature_oligodendrocyte = c("SOX10","OLIG1","OLIG2","MYRF","GPR17","BCAS1","ENPP6","TSPAN2","CNP","NKX2-2"),
  Mature_oligodendrocyte   = c("MBP","PLP1","MOG","MAG","MOBP","CLDN11","MAL","ERMN","CNP","OPALIN"),
  Stress_response          = c("FOS","JUN","JUNB","ATF3","EGR1","EGR2","HSPA1A","HSPA1B","HSP90AA1","DNAJB1"),
  Hypoxia_glycolysis       = c("HIF1A","VEGFA","CA9","LDHA","SLC2A1","ENO1","PGK1","ALDOA","BNIP3"),
  Cell_cycle_proliferation = c("MKI67","TOP2A","PCNA","MCM2","MCM3","MCM5","MCM6","UBE2C","CDK1","CCNB1"),
  Homeostatic_microglia    = c("P2RY12","P2RY13","TMEM119","HEXB","SALL1","OLFML3","GPR34","SLC2A5","FCRLS","SIGLEC9","IBA1"),
  DAM                      = c("LPL","CLEC7A","TREM2","TYROBP","CST7","ITGAX","CD9","CD63","LILRB4")
)
## A marker "counts" only if detected in >= PROC$marker_min_det (10%) of cells (not
## merely present in >=1 cell); a module is usable if >=3 of its markers clear that
## bar. n_present (>=1 cell) is kept in the table for reference.
det_frac  <- rowMeans(!is.na(mat))                       # per-protein detection fraction
det_genes <- rownames(mat)[det_frac >= PROC$marker_min_det]
marker_detection <- data.frame(
  module     = names(marker_sets),
  n_total    = lengths(marker_sets),
  n_present  = vapply(marker_sets, function(g) length(intersect(g, rownames(mat))), integer(1)),  # >=1 cell
  n_detected = vapply(marker_sets, function(g) length(intersect(g, det_genes)),     integer(1)),  # >=10% of cells
  row.names  = NULL)
save_tab(marker_detection, "S8_IF_marker_detection.csv")
marker_sets_det <- marker_sets[marker_detection$n_detected >= 3]
cat(sprintf("IF marker modules: %d total; %d usable (>=3 markers detected in >=%.0f%% of cells): %s\n",
            length(marker_sets), length(marker_sets_det), 100 * PROC$marker_min_det,
            paste(names(marker_sets_det), collapse = ", ")))

## per-cell module score = mean log2 of the >=10%-detected markers only (ultra-sparse
## markers, seen in <10% of cells, are excluded so the score is not driven by noise).
for (nm in names(marker_sets_det)) {
  g <- intersect(marker_sets_det[[nm]], det_genes)
  colData(sce)[[paste0("mod_", nm)]] <-
    colMeans(mat[g, , drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)[colnames(sce)]
}

## faceted UMAP of all module scores
um <- as.data.frame(reducedDim(sce, "UMAP")); colnames(um)[1:2] <- c("UMAP1","UMAP2")
um <- cbind(um[, 1:2], as.data.frame(colData(sce))[, paste0("mod_", names(marker_sets_det))])
um_long <- tidyr::pivot_longer(um, cols = tidyr::starts_with("mod_"),
                               names_to = "module", values_to = "score",
                               names_prefix = "mod_")
p_mod <- ggplot(um_long, aes(UMAP1, UMAP2, colour = score)) +
  geom_point(size = 1.1) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(option = "inferno", na.value = "grey85") +
  facet_wrap(~ module, ncol = 4) + theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  labs(title = "Cell-type module scores (mean log2 of detected markers)")
print(p_mod); save_fig(p_mod, "S8_module_scores_UMAP.png", w = 13, h = 6)
```

## 8.1.1 Marker–module overlap (why the cell-type scores are not independent)

Many markers are shared across the usable modules, so the module scores co-vary — a
key caveat when reading the "cell types". This maps the overlap on the **used
markers** (those detected in ≥10 % of cells).

```{r identity-overlap, fig.width=9, fig.height=11}
.used <- lapply(marker_sets_det, function(g) intersect(g, det_genes))   # >=10% markers, 11 modules
.allm <- sort(unique(unlist(.used)))
.M    <- sapply(.used, function(g) as.integer(.allm %in% g)); rownames(.M) <- .allm
.nmod <- rowSums(.M)
## order modules by hclust on marker-set Jaccard; markers by n-modules then first module
.J <- outer(seq_along(.used), seq_along(.used), Vectorize(function(i, j)
  length(intersect(.used[[i]], .used[[j]])) / length(union(.used[[i]], .used[[j]]))))
.modord <- names(.used)[hclust(as.dist(1 - .J))$order]
.first  <- apply(.M[, .modord, drop = FALSE], 1, function(r) which(r == 1)[1])
.mkord  <- .allm[order(-.nmod, .first)]

## (1) marker x module membership grid (shared markers highlighted)
.long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(.used), function(m)
  data.frame(module = m, marker = .allm, member = .M[, m], nmod = .nmod)))
.long <- subset(.long, member == 1)
.long$module <- factor(.long$module, levels = .modord)
.long$marker <- factor(.long$marker, levels = rev(.mkord))
.long$share  <- ifelse(.long$nmod == 1, "unique to 1 type", ifelse(.long$nmod == 2, "shared by 2", "shared by 3-4"))
p_mem <- ggplot(.long, aes(module, marker, fill = share)) + geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("unique to 1 type" = "#4393C3", "shared by 2" = "#F4A582", "shared by 3-4" = "#B2182B"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Marker–cell-type membership (used markers, detected >=10% of cells)",
       subtitle = sprintf("%d markers across %d modules; %d (%.0f%%) shared by >=2 cell types -> module scores are NOT independent",
                          length(.allm), length(.used), sum(.nmod >= 2), 100 * mean(.nmod >= 2))) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1, size = 9),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7), plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8.5), panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "top")
print(p_mem); save_fig(p_mem, "S8_marker_membership.png", 9, 11)

## (2) module x module shared-marker heatmap
.S  <- sapply(.used, function(a) sapply(.used, function(b) length(intersect(a, b))))
.sl <- do.call(rbind, lapply(.modord, function(i) data.frame(m1 = i, m2 = .modord, shared = .S[i, .modord])))
.sl$m1 <- factor(.sl$m1, levels = .modord); .sl$m2 <- factor(.sl$m2, levels = rev(.modord))
.sl$lab <- ifelse(as.character(.sl$m1) == as.character(.sl$m2), paste0("(", .sl$shared, ")"),
                  ifelse(.sl$shared > 0, .sl$shared, ""))
p_ov <- ggplot(.sl, aes(m1, m2, fill = ifelse(as.character(m1) == as.character(m2), NA, shared))) +
  geom_tile(colour = "grey90") + geom_text(aes(label = lab), size = 3) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#FDDBC7", high = "#B2182B", na.value = "grey85", name = "shared\nmarkers") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Cell-type overlap: shared markers between modules",
       subtitle = "Diagonal = module size (parentheses); off-diagonal = markers shared. High overlap = confounded scores.") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11), plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8.5), panel.grid = element_blank())
print(p_ov); save_fig(p_ov, "S8_module_overlap.png", 9, 7.5)
save_tab(as.data.frame(.S), "S8_module_shared_markers.csv")
```

The scores are **not independent**: **17 of 38 used markers (45 %) are shared by ≥2 cell
types**. A **progenitor / glial block** dominates — **Radial_glia and Immature_astrocyte
are 5-of-5 identical** (SOX2 / NES / VIM / FABP7 / PTPRZ1), so SCP cannot separate radial
glia from immature astrocyte here, and both co-vary with Neural_progenitors and Cell-cycle
(MKI67 / TOP2A / PCNA / MCM2). Neuronal (Immature_neurons ↔ Pan_neuronal), astrocyte
(Astrocyte ↔ Reactive_astrocyte) and interneuron (GABAergic ↔ CGE) modules likewise
overlap. Only **Hypoxia_glycolysis** (ALDOA / ENO1 / LDHA / PGK1), the synaptic
**Pan_neuronal** markers (SYN1 / SYT1 / UCHL1 / MAP2) and the replication markers
(MCM3 / 5 / 6) are cleanly module-specific. This is why the 11 modules are best read as an
**overlapping developmental continuum, not 11 discrete cell types** — reinforcing the
trajectory (Session 10) as the primary model.

## 8.1.2 Collapsed super-class identities (the recommended reading)

Because the modules are so redundant, discrete typing is only honest at a coarser
resolution (hierarchical annotation: label at the resolution the data supports; Pliner
2019). The 11 modules are collapsed — where **both** the marker overlap (§8.1.1) **and**
the across-cell score correlation agree — into **4 cell-type super-classes**
(Progenitor/RG-glial, Neuronal, Interneuron-leaning, Astroglial) plus **2 orthogonal
state axes** (Cycling, Metabolic/glycolytic). Proliferation markers are apportioned to
the Cycling axis only (the "apportion shared markers" idea; Kunes 2023), so identity and
state are not conflated. Scores use **UCell** (rank-based, robust to depth/missingness)
rather than the mean-log2 of §8.1.

```{r identity-superclass, fig.width=13, fig.height=7}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(UCell))
.cyc <- c("MKI67","TOP2A","PCNA","MCM2","MCM3","MCM5","MCM6","UBE2C","CDK1","CCNB1")
.sm  <- function(mods) intersect(unique(unlist(marker_sets_det[mods])), det_genes)
superclass <- list(
  Progenitor_RGglial = setdiff(.sm(c("Neural_progenitors","Radial_glia","Immature_astrocyte")), .cyc),
  Neuronal           = .sm(c("Immature_neurons","Pan_neuronal")),
  Interneuron        = .sm(c("GABAergic_neurons","CGE_interneurons")),
  Astroglial         = .sm(c("Astrocyte","Reactive_astrocyte")),
  Cycling            = intersect(marker_sets_det$Cell_cycle_proliferation, det_genes),
  Metabolic          = intersect(marker_sets_det$Hypoxia_glycolysis, det_genes))
.lab <- c(Progenitor_RGglial = "Progenitor / RG-glial", Neuronal = "Neuronal",
          Interneuron = "Interneuron-leaning", Astroglial = "Astroglial",
          Cycling = "Cycling (state)", Metabolic = "Metabolic/glycolytic (state)")
cat("super-class markers (>=10%-detected, proliferation apportioned to Cycling):\n")
for (n in names(superclass)) cat(sprintf("  %-20s %s\n", .lab[n], paste(superclass[[n]], collapse = ", ")))

## UCell (min-fill NAs so undetected proteins rank lowest; ncores=1 on Windows)
.mf <- mat; .mf[is.na(.mf)] <- min(mat, na.rm = TRUE) - 1
uc  <- UCell::ScoreSignatures_UCell(.mf, features = superclass, maxRank = 1500, ncores = 1, name = "")
colnames(uc) <- names(superclass)
for (n in colnames(uc)) colData(sce)[[paste0("sc_", n)]] <- uc[colnames(sce), n]

## redundancy: max off-diagonal |Spearman|, 11 modules vs 6 super-classes
.co <- function(M) { C <- cor(M, method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs"); max(abs(C[upper.tri(C)])) }
.mod11 <- sapply(marker_sets_det, function(g) colMeans(mat[intersect(g, det_genes), , drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE))
cat(sprintf("\nMax off-diagonal |Spearman| redundancy: 11 modules = %.2f  ->  6 super-classes (UCell) = %.2f\n",
            .co(.mod11), .co(uc)))

## behaviour along the (seeded) Session-10 pseudotime, if present
.stf <- file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$obj, "sce_trajectory.rds")
if (file.exists(.stf)) { .s <- readRDS(.stf); .pt <- setNames(.s$Pseudotime, colnames(.s))
  .cn <- intersect(rownames(uc), names(.pt))
  cat("Super-class vs pseudotime (Spearman rho):",
      paste(sprintf("%s=%+.2f", colnames(uc), apply(uc[.cn, , drop = FALSE], 2,
            function(v) cor(v, .pt[.cn], method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"))), collapse = "  "), "\n") }

## headline cell-type call = argmax over the 4 TYPE super-classes (z-scored; state axes excluded)
.z <- scale(uc[, 1:4]); sce$superclass_type <- .lab[colnames(uc)[1:4]][max.col(.z[colnames(sce), , drop = FALSE])]
cat("\nheadline super-class TYPE per cell (argmax of z-scored type scores):\n"); print(table(sce$superclass_type))

## UMAP coloured by the headline super-class TYPE per cell (discrete), shown ABOVE the
## faceted 6-score UMAP below so the per-cell call and the per-class scores read together.
.umt <- data.frame(reducedDim(sce, "UMAP")[, 1:2], type = factor(sce$superclass_type, levels = .lab[1:4]))
colnames(.umt)[1:2] <- c("UMAP1", "UMAP2")
p_sctype <- ggplot(.umt, aes(UMAP1, UMAP2, fill = type)) +
  geom_point(shape = 21, size = 3, colour = "grey30", stroke = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2", name = "Super-class\nTYPE", na.value = "grey80") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13)) +
  labs(title = "Headline super-class TYPE per cell (argmax of z-scored type scores)")
print(p_sctype); save_fig(p_sctype, "S8_superclass_type_UMAP.png", 8, 6)

## faceted UMAP of the 6 super-class scores
.um  <- as.data.frame(reducedDim(sce, "UMAP"))[, 1:2]; colnames(.um) <- c("UMAP1", "UMAP2")
.um  <- cbind(.um, as.data.frame(colData(sce))[, paste0("sc_", names(superclass))])
.uml <- tidyr::pivot_longer(.um, cols = tidyr::starts_with("sc_"), names_to = "superclass", values_to = "score", names_prefix = "sc_")
.uml$superclass <- factor(.lab[.uml$superclass], levels = .lab)
## light-low sequential (grey -> warm-red): low scores recede to grey, high scores pop;
## shape-21 bordered points, larger, for readability. (inferno's dark-low made the eye
## track the LOW-scoring cells and washed the pale-yellow high ones into the background.)
p_sc <- ggplot(.uml, aes(UMAP1, UMAP2, fill = score)) +
  geom_point(shape = 21, size = 2.6, colour = "grey55", stroke = 0.15) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = c("grey90","#FFEDA0","#FEB24C","#FD8D3C","#E31A1C","#7F0000"),
                       na.value = "grey90", name = "UCell\nscore", limits = c(0, NA)) +
  facet_wrap(~ superclass, ncol = 3) + theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"), panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
  labs(title = "Collapsed super-class scores (UCell): 4 cell-type classes + 2 orthogonal state axes")
print(p_sc); save_fig(p_sc, "S8_superclass_scores_UMAP.png", 13, 7)
save_tab(as.data.frame(uc), "S8_superclass_scores.csv")
```

Collapsing drops the maximum inter-score redundancy from **perfect (1.00; Radial_glia ≡
Immature_astrocyte) to ~0.5–0.6**, and the residual correlation is now *biologically
meaningful* — chiefly the progenitor↔neuronal **anti**-correlation (the differentiation
axis), not a marker-sharing artefact. Along the Session-10 pseudotime the super-classes
behave as expected (Progenitor/RG-glial and Astroglial high early; **Neuronal high late,
ρ ≈ +0.85**; the Cycling and Metabolic state axes track weakly). This is the
**recommended cell-identity reading** — four honestly-separable types resolved to the
level the proteome supports, with proliferation and metabolism as orthogonal states; the
11 fine modules (§8.1) and their overlap (§8.1.1) are retained as supporting detail.

## 8.2 Curated single-marker UMAPs (informative subset)
<!-- Hand-picked high-value markers shown individually (e.g. SOX2, NES, DCX,
     MAP2, TUBB3, GFAP, MKI67, DLX1, GLUD1). -->

```{r identity-markers, fig.width=11, fig.height=9}
## hand-picked, high-value markers shown individually (NA = grey)
markers_show <- intersect(c("SOX2","NES","DCX","MAP2","TUBB3",
                            "GFAP","MKI67","DLX1","GLUD1"), rownames(mat))
mk <- as.data.frame(reducedDim(sce, "UMAP")); colnames(mk)[1:2] <- c("UMAP1","UMAP2")
mk <- cbind(mk[, 1:2], t(mat[markers_show, colnames(sce), drop = FALSE]))
mk_long <- tidyr::pivot_longer(mk, cols = tidyr::all_of(markers_show),
                               names_to = "gene", values_to = "log2int")
## PER-PROTEIN robust rescale to [0,1] (2-98 pctile) so each marker uses the FULL colour
## range independent of its absolute spread -- otherwise the shared scale is dominated by
## the widest-range protein (GLUD1, ~+/-8 row-centred) and every other panel washes to a
## narrow band. grey = not detected; low -> grey (recede), high -> dark red (pop).
mk_long$rel <- ave(mk_long$log2int, mk_long$gene, FUN = function(v) {
  q <- quantile(v, c(0.02, 0.98), na.rm = TRUE); if (diff(q) == 0) return(v * 0)
  pmin(pmax((v - q[1]) / (q[2] - q[1]), 0), 1) })
p_mk <- ggplot(mk_long, aes(UMAP1, UMAP2, fill = rel)) +
  geom_point(shape = 21, size = 2.4, colour = "grey55", stroke = 0.15) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = c("grey90","#FFEDA0","#FEB24C","#FD8D3C","#E31A1C","#7F0000"),
                       na.value = "grey88", name = "relative\nlevel", limits = c(0, 1)) +
  facet_wrap(~ gene, ncol = 3) + theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"), panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
  labs(title = "Curated marker proteins (per-protein relative log2 intensity; grey = not detected)")
print(p_mk); save_fig(p_mk, "S8_curated_markers_UMAP.png", w = 11, h = 9)
```

## 8.2b Cluster-identity markers: ventral, proliferation, neuronal differentiation

<!-- Three marker groups on the clustering UMAP, tagged a/b/c. (a) Ventral/subpallial:
     DLX5, DLX1, ARX are subpallial TFs peaking in the proliferating cluster C3 (ARX is a
     DLX-target, ventral/subpallial-specific); SCGN (secretagogin) is a human CGE/LGE-derived
     GABAergic-interneuron marker peaking in the differentiated cluster C2. SCGN was nominated
     by a DLX5/DLX1-anchored guilt-by-association screen (enriched in DLX+ cells, anti-correlated
     with proliferation) and confirmed as a subpallial/GABAergic-interneuron marker by literature
     (Mulder PNAS 2009; Raju Cereb Cortex 2018 -- human-specific vs mouse; Alpar Front Neuroanat
     2020: co-expresses SP8/COUP-TFII/DLX2/GAD67). ARX: Colombo J Neurosci 2007/2008; Colasante
     2009. (b) Proliferation: MKI67/TOP2A/MCM5/PCNA confirm the cycling C3 compartment. (c)
     Neuronal differentiation: DCX/CRMP1/MAP1B/STMN1 peak in the mature-neuron cluster C2.
     Together a->b->c trace the C3 cycling-progenitor -> C4 transition -> C2 neuron axis.
     CAVEAT: ventral-specific TFs (DLX2/6, LHX6, NKX2-1, SOX6) and dorsal counter-markers
     (PAX6, TBR1/2) are mostly below the SCP detection floor, so (a) is a positive ventral
     signal, not proof of ventral exclusivity. -->

```{r identity-ventral, fig.width=14, fig.height=11}
## per-protein relative log2 intensity (2-98 pctile rescale, as in 8.2); NA = grey.
## match by first gene of each rowname so multi-gene "A;B" protein groups still resolve.
## rows a/b/c = ventral/subpallial, proliferation, neuronal-differentiation markers.
ventral_show <- c("DLX5", "DLX1", "ARX", "SCGN", "MKI67", "TOP2A", "MCM5", "PCNA",
                  "DCX", "CRMP1", "MAP1B", "STMN1")
.rnv <- sub(";.*$", "", rownames(mat)); .iv <- match(ventral_show, .rnv)
ventral_show <- ventral_show[!is.na(.iv)]; .iv <- .iv[!is.na(.iv)]
vm <- as.data.frame(reducedDim(sce, "UMAP")); colnames(vm)[1:2] <- c("UMAP1", "UMAP2")
.vsub <- t(mat[.iv, colnames(sce), drop = FALSE]); colnames(.vsub) <- ventral_show
vm <- cbind(vm[, 1:2], .vsub)
v_long <- tidyr::pivot_longer(vm, cols = tidyr::all_of(ventral_show),
                              names_to = "gene", values_to = "log2int")
v_long$rel <- ave(v_long$log2int, v_long$gene, FUN = function(v) {
  q <- quantile(v, c(0.02, 0.98), na.rm = TRUE); if (diff(q) == 0) return(v * 0)
  pmin(pmax((v - q[1]) / (q[2] - q[1]), 0), 1) })
## per-gene detection (n of 131 cells) for facet labels; keep v_long$gene RAW (rows relabel per group)
.ndet <- tapply(!is.na(v_long$log2int), v_long$gene, sum)
## faint cluster-number centroids, repeated in every facet (same UMAP coords per panel)
.vc <- data.frame(reducedDim(sce, "UMAP")[, 1:2], cl = factor(colLabels(sce)))
colnames(.vc)[1:2] <- c("UMAP1", "UMAP2")
.cent_v <- aggregate(cbind(UMAP1, UMAP2) ~ cl, .vc, median)
## build one facet row per marker group so patchwork tags them a (ventral) / b (proliferation) / c (neuronal)
.mkrow <- function(genes, show_x) {
  genes <- genes[genes %in% v_long$gene]
  d <- v_long[v_long$gene %in% genes, ]
  d$gene <- factor(d$gene, levels = genes, labels = sprintf("%s (n=%d)", genes, .ndet[genes]))
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(UMAP1, UMAP2)) +
    geom_point(aes(fill = rel), shape = 21, size = 2.4, colour = "grey55", stroke = 0.15) +
    geom_text(data = .cent_v, aes(UMAP1, UMAP2, label = cl), inherit.aes = FALSE,
              colour = "grey25", fontface = "bold", size = 4.3, alpha = 0.75) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(colours = c("#FFF7BC","#FEC44F","#FE9929","#EC7014","#CC4C02","#7F2704"),
                         na.value = "grey88", name = "relative\nlevel", limits = c(0, 1)) +
    facet_wrap(~ gene, nrow = 1) + theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
    theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"), panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
  if (!show_x) p <- p + theme(axis.title.x = element_blank())
  p
}
.pa <- .mkrow(c("DLX5","DLX1","ARX","SCGN"),   show_x = FALSE)  # a = ventral / subpallial
.pb <- .mkrow(c("MKI67","TOP2A","MCM5","PCNA"), show_x = FALSE) # b = proliferation
.pc <- .mkrow(c("DCX","CRMP1","MAP1B","STMN1"), show_x = TRUE)  # c = neuronal differentiation
p_ventral <- (.pa / .pb / .pc) + plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a") &
  theme(plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 20))
print(p_ventral); save_fig(p_ventral, "S8_ventral_lineage_UMAP.png", w = 14, h = 11)
```

## 8.2c Progenitor / radial-glia markers

<!-- Curated progenitor / radial-glia markers on the clustering UMAP (per-protein relative
     log2 intensity, NA = grey). SOX2/NES/VIM/FABP7/PTPRZ1 = neural-progenitor / radial-glia;
     PCNA/TOP2A/MKI67/MCM2 = proliferation (peak in C3). HES1 and PAX6 were requested but fall
     below the SCP detection floor and are dropped automatically (matched by first gene). -->

```{r identity-progenitor, fig.width=13, fig.height=11}
prog_show <- c("SOX2","NES","VIM","FABP7","PTPRZ1","PCNA","HES1","TOP2A","PAX6","MKI67","MCM2")
.rnp <- sub(";.*$", "", rownames(mat)); prog_show <- prog_show[prog_show %in% .rnp]
.ipm <- match(prog_show, .rnp)

  pmin(pmax((v - q[1]) / (q[2] - q[1]), 0), 1) })
.pnd <- tapply(!is.na(p_long$log2int), p_long$gene, sum)
p_long$gene <- factor(p_long$gene, levels = prog_show, labels = sprintf("%s (n=%d)", prog_show, .pnd[prog_show]))
.pcl <- data.frame(reducedDim(sce, "UMAP")[, 1:2], cl = factor(colLabels(sce)))
colnames(.pcl)[1:2] <- c("UMAP1", "UMAP2")
.pcen <- aggregate(cbind(UMAP1, UMAP2) ~ cl, .pcl, median)
p_prog <- ggplot(p_long, aes(UMAP1, UMAP2)) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = rel), shape = 21, size = 2.4, colour = "grey55", stroke = 0.15) +
  geom_text(data = .pcen, aes(UMAP1, UMAP2, label = cl), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            colour = "grey25", fontface = "bold", size = 4.3, alpha = 0.75) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = c("#FFF7BC","#FEC44F","#FE9929","#EC7014","#CC4C02","#7F2704"),
                       na.value = "grey88", name = "relative\nlevel", limits = c(0, 1)) +
  facet_wrap(~ gene, ncol = 3) + theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"), panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +

       subtitle = "per-protein relative log2 intensity; grey = not detected")
print(p_prog); save_fig(p_prog, "S8_progenitor_markers_UMAP.png", w = 13, h = 11)
```

## 8.3 AUCell cell-type scoring

<!-- AUCell on a MIN-FILLED matrix: rank-based, so a constant fill is enough and
     no real imputation is needed. SingleR requires a complete matrix and is
     therefore in Appendix A with the KNN-imputed data. -->

```{r identity-aucell, fig.width=7, fig.height=6}
pg <- assay(scp[["Protein.Group"]])
## keep curated sets with >= 3 markers detected in >= PROC$marker_min_det of cells
## (consistent with 8.1); AUCell then ranks only those well-detected markers.
.det_auc <- rownames(pg)[rowMeans(!is.na(pg)) >= PROC$marker_min_det]
marker_sets_auc <- Filter(function(g) length(intersect(g, .det_auc)) >= 3, marker_sets)
marker_sets_auc <- lapply(marker_sets_auc, intersect, .det_auc)

## AUCell needs defined ranks -> min-fill NAs (rank-based, NA-tolerant)
pg_filled  <- pg; pg_filled[is.na(pg_filled)] <- min(pg, na.rm = TRUE) - 1
aucMaxRank <- ceiling(median(colSums(!is.na(pg))) * 0.05)   # 5% of median detected
rankings   <- AUCell_buildRankings(pg_filled, plotStats = FALSE)
gsc <- GeneSetCollection(Map(function(g, nm) GeneSet(g, setName = nm),
                             marker_sets_auc, names(marker_sets_auc)))
auc_mat <- getAUC(AUCell_calcAUC(gsc, rankings, aucMaxRank = aucMaxRank))

## assign each cell its top-scoring type; overlay on the residual-based UMAP
sce$AUCell_type <- rownames(auc_mat)[max.col(t(auc_mat[, colnames(sce)]))]
print(table(sce$AUCell_type))
save_tab(data.frame(cell = colnames(sce), t(auc_mat[, colnames(sce)]),
                    AUCell_type = sce$AUCell_type), "S8_AUCell_scores.csv")
p_auc <- plotUMAP(sce, colour_by = "AUCell_type", point_size = 3, point_alpha = 1) +
  ggtitle("AUCell cell-type assignment")
print(p_auc); save_fig(p_auc, "S8_AUCell_UMAP.png", w = 7, h = 6)
```

## 8.4 Variance analysis of the minimal model

The minimal model splits each peptide's variance into the modelled **library-size** term
(`log_sumsRI_NoCRAP`) and the **residual** (biological signal plus noise). Across all
peptides the residual carries **~78 %** of the variance — most variation is *not* explained
by loading. Proteins whose residual explained variance is near 100 % vary almost entirely
for non-technical reasons; **gating those (≥ 95 %)** and testing GO enrichment isolates the
biological programs whose expression is independent of input amount, while the **top proteins
by residual variance** name the drivers of the biological signal.

```{r variance-analysis, fig.width=13.5, fig.height=15, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(GO.db); library(AnnotationDbi)})
## variance partition of the fitted minimal model (peptide-level), gene-annotated.
## Recomputed here (fast) so it runs for BOTH the cache-hit and fresh-fit branches of §6.1.
vaRes <- scpVarianceAnalysis(sce)
vaRes <- scpAnnotateResults(vaRes, rowData(sce), by = "feature", by2 = "Stripped.Sequence")

## every text element in this panel is BLACK and sized off VB (raised 12 -> 14 for print)
VA_ACC <- "#2166AC"; VA_TECH <- "#D95F02"; VA_GATE <- 95; VA_NEUT <- "#BDBDBD"; VB <- 14
va_theme <- theme_bw(base_size = VB, base_family = "sans") +
  theme(plot.title    = element_text(size = VB + 1, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, colour = "black"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = VB - 3, hjust = 0.5, colour = "black"),
        axis.title    = element_text(size = VB, colour = "black"),
        axis.text     = element_text(size = VB - 2, colour = "black"),
        legend.title  = element_text(size = VB - 1, colour = "black"),
        legend.text   = element_text(size = VB - 1, colour = "black"),
        strip.text    = element_text(size = VB - 1, colour = "black"),
        legend.key.size = unit(0.9, "lines"), panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

## (a) n/p ratio distribution — what the minimal model was actually fed (from §6.1).
## scpModelFilterPlot shows all features (estimable + inestimable). Fill mapped BY NAME
## (estimated -> accent, inestimable -> neutral grey); the unused "selected" level that
## scp:::.filterPlot adds when threshold==1 is dropped by ggplot's discrete scale.
.pnp <- scpModelFilterPlot(sce) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(estimated = VA_ACC, inestimable = VA_NEUT), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "n / p ratio", y = "Peptides", title = "Distribution of the n/p ratio") +
  va_theme + theme(legend.position = "top", legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))

## (b) overall variance partition. Hand-built 2-row stacked bar reproducing scpVariancePlot's
## MEAN per-peptide %EV (~69/31) — which differs from the SS-weighted total (78/22) reported
## below; the on-bar labels match the plotted bar heights. Built directly (no scpVariancePlot
## dependency) so the panel is robust to that function's internal layer/scale behaviour.
## NB the on-bar % labels stay WHITE: they sit inside the dark blue/orange segments where
## black would be unreadable. Every other text element is black. Colours match (d).
.vpp  <- c(Residuals         = mean(as.data.frame(vaRes$Residuals)$percentExplainedVar),
           log_sumsRI_NoCRAP = mean(as.data.frame(vaRes$log_sumsRI_NoCRAP)$percentExplainedVar))
.vpdf <- data.frame(effectName = factor(names(.vpp), levels = c("Residuals", "log_sumsRI_NoCRAP")),
                    pct = as.numeric(.vpp))
.pv <- ggplot(.vpdf, aes(x = 1, y = pct, fill = effectName)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.9, colour = "black") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.0f%%", pct)), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
            size = (VB + 1)/ggplot2::.pt, colour = "white", fontface = "bold") +  # ggplot2:: — §8.x defines a `.pt` (pseudotime) that masks it
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Residuals = VA_ACC, log_sumsRI_NoCRAP = VA_TECH), name = "Variance") +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2)) +
  labs(title = "Overall variance partition", x = NULL, y = "Explained variance (%)") +
  va_theme +
  theme(legend.position = "top", legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
        axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = VB + 2, colour = "black"))
.fg  <- function(x) sub(";.*$", "", x)
.res <- as.data.frame(vaRes$Residuals); .tec <- as.data.frame(vaRes$log_sumsRI_NoCRAP)
.d   <- merge(.res[, c("feature","SS","Genes")], .tec[, c("feature","SS")], by = "feature", suffixes = c("_res","_tec"))
.d$gene <- .fg(.d$Genes); .d <- .d[.d$gene != "" & !is.na(.d$gene), ]
.ag  <- aggregate(cbind(SS_res, SS_tec) ~ gene, .d, sum)
.ag$pEV <- 100 * .ag$SS_res / (.ag$SS_res + .ag$SS_tec); .ag$gated <- .ag$pEV >= VA_GATE
cat(sprintf("minimal-model variance: overall residual = %.0f%% | proteins gated (residual %%EV >= %d) = %d\n",
            100 * sum(.ag$SS_res) / sum(.ag$SS_res + .ag$SS_tec), VA_GATE, sum(.ag$gated)))

## (c) residual explained-variance distribution + gate
.pa <- ggplot(.ag, aes(pEV, fill = gated)) +
  geom_histogram(breaks = seq(0, 100, 2.5), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.06) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = VA_GATE, linetype = "dashed", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = VA_ACC, `TRUE` = VA_TECH),
                    labels = c("rest", sprintf("gated (>=%d%%)", VA_GATE)), name = NULL) +
  annotate("text", x = VA_GATE - 1.5, y = Inf, label = sprintf("gated: %d", sum(.ag$gated)),
           hjust = 1, vjust = 1.8, size = (VB - 4)/ggplot2::.pt, colour = "black") +
  labs(x = "Residual explained variance (%)", y = "Proteins", title = "Residual explained-variance distribution") +
  va_theme + theme(legend.position = "top")

## (b) top-10 proteins by residual variance (partition)
.t10 <- head(.ag[order(-.ag$SS_res), ], 10)
.tl  <- rbind(data.frame(gene = .t10$gene, term = "Residuals",         pct = .t10$pEV),
              data.frame(gene = .t10$gene, term = "log_sumsRI_NoCRAP", pct = 100 - .t10$pEV))
.tl$gene <- factor(.tl$gene, levels = rev(.t10$gene[order(-.t10$SS_res)]))
.tl$term <- factor(.tl$term, levels = c("log_sumsRI_NoCRAP", "Residuals"))
.pc <- ggplot(.tl, aes(pct, gene, fill = term)) + geom_col(width = 0.72) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Residuals = VA_ACC, log_sumsRI_NoCRAP = VA_TECH), name = "Variance") +
  labs(x = "Explained variance (%)", y = NULL, title = "Top-10 proteins by residual variance (SS)") +
  va_theme + theme(legend.position = "none")   # effect-name key is carried by panel (a)

## universe + gated gene set (shared by both enrichments below)
.univ_va <- unique(.ag$gene); .univ_va <- .univ_va[.univ_va %in% keys(org.Hs.eg.db, "SYMBOL")]
.gset_va <- intersect(.ag$gene[.ag$gated], .univ_va)
## (c) GO BP enrichment of gated proteins (cached; delete the rds to recompute)
.venr <- file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$obj, "S6_variance_enrichment.rds")
if (file.exists(.venr)) { .er <- readRDS(.venr) } else {
  .gaa  <- suppressMessages(AnnotationDbi::select(org.Hs.eg.db, keys = .univ_va, columns = c("GOALL","ONTOLOGYALL"), keytype = "SYMBOL"))
  .t2g  <- unique(.gaa[!is.na(.gaa$GOALL) & .gaa$ONTOLOGYALL == "BP", c("GOALL","SYMBOL")])
  .t2n  <- suppressMessages(AnnotationDbi::select(GO.db, keys = unique(.t2g$GOALL), columns = "TERM", keytype = "GOID"))[, c("GOID","TERM")]
  .er   <- clusterProfiler::enricher(.gset_va, universe = .univ_va, TERM2GENE = .t2g,
             TERM2NAME = .t2n, pAdjustMethod = "BH", pvalueCutoff = 1, qvalueCutoff = 1, minGSSize = 10, maxGSSize = 500)@result
  saveRDS(.er, .venr)
}
.fold <- function(e){ g <- do.call(rbind, lapply(strsplit(e$GeneRatio, "/"), as.numeric)); b <- do.call(rbind, lapply(strsplit(e$BgRatio, "/"), as.numeric)); (g[,1]/g[,2]) / (b[,1]/b[,2]) }
.er$Fold <- .fold(.er); .wrap <- function(x, n = 40) vapply(x, function(s) paste(strwrap(s, n), collapse = "\n"), character(1))
.gs <- .er[.er$p.adjust < 0.05 & .er$Count >= 5, ]; .gob <- head(.gs[order(-.gs$Fold), ], 10)
## couple MSigDB Hallmark (cached; needs h.all.symbols.gmt in Objects/ — skips the facet if absent)
.hf <- file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$obj, "h.all.symbols.gmt"); .hrds <- file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$obj, "S6_variance_hallmark.rds")
if (file.exists(.hrds)) { .erh <- readRDS(.hrds) } else if (file.exists(.hf)) {
  .erh <- clusterProfiler::enricher(.gset_va, universe = .univ_va, TERM2GENE = clusterProfiler::read.gmt(.hf),
            pAdjustMethod = "BH", pvalueCutoff = 1, qvalueCutoff = 1, minGSSize = 10, maxGSSize = 500)@result
  .erh$Fold <- .fold(.erh); saveRDS(.erh, .hrds)
} else { .erh <- NULL; cat("Hallmark GMT (h.all.symbols.gmt) not found in Objects/ — Hallmark facet skipped\n") }
## two-line facet labels: the Hallmark facet is only ~2 bars tall, so a single-line
## vertical "MSigDB Hallmark" gets clipped by the strip height.
.cmb <- data.frame(lab = .wrap(.gob$Description), Fold = .gob$Fold, logFDR = -log10(.gob$p.adjust), source = "GO Biological\nProcess")
if (!is.null(.erh)) { .hm0 <- .erh[.erh$p.adjust < 0.05 & .erh$Count >= 5, ]; .hm <- head(.hm0[order(-.hm0$Fold), ], 8)
  if (nrow(.hm)) .cmb <- rbind(.cmb, data.frame(lab = gsub("_", " ", sub("HALLMARK_", "", .hm$ID)), Fold = .hm$Fold, logFDR = -log10(.hm$p.adjust), source = "MSigDB\nHallmark")) }
.cmb$source <- factor(.cmb$source, levels = c("GO Biological\nProcess", "MSigDB\nHallmark"))
.cmb <- .cmb[order(.cmb$source, .cmb$Fold), ]; .cmb$lab <- factor(.cmb$lab, levels = unique(.cmb$lab))
.pb <- ggplot(.cmb, aes(Fold, lab, fill = logFDR)) + geom_col(width = 0.72) +
  facet_grid(source ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "plasma", name = expression(-log[10] ~ FDR)) +
  labs(x = "Fold enrichment", y = NULL, title = "Enrichment of gated (high-residual) proteins") +
  va_theme + theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = VB - 2, lineheight = 0.85, colour = "black"),
                   legend.position = "right", legend.key.width = unit(0.45, "lines"),
                   strip.placement = "outside",
                   strip.text.y.left = element_text(size = VB - 1, face = "bold", angle = 90, colour = "black",
                                                    margin = margin(2, 2.5, 2, 2.5)),
                   strip.background.y = element_rect(fill = "grey90", colour = NA))

## 2 + 2 + 1: model diagnostics on row 1, per-protein views on row 2, enrichment across
## the bottom (four panels in one row collided at this text size).
##   a n/p ratio | b overall partition ; c residual %EV + gate | d top-10 ; e enrichment
## free(.pb, side = "l"): the enrichment has a very wide left gutter (facet strips + long
## GO labels); without this patchwork aligns left panel edges down the column and strands
## the y-axes of (a) and (c) ~3in from their plots.
.vr1    <- (.pnp | .pv) + plot_layout(widths = c(1.45, 0.6))
.vr2    <- (.pa  | .pc) + plot_layout(widths = c(1.1, 1.0))
.vpanel <- (.vr1 / .vr2 / patchwork::free(.pb, side = "l")) + plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1, 1.55)) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a", theme = theme(plot.tag = element_text(size = VB + 14, face = "bold", colour = "black")))
print(.vpanel)
cat(sprintf("enrichment: %d sig GO BP + %s Hallmark | top GO: %s\n", nrow(.gob),
            if (is.null(.erh)) "0 (skipped)" else as.character(sum(.erh$p.adjust < 0.05 & .erh$Count >= 5, na.rm = TRUE)),
            paste(head(.gob$Description, 5), collapse = "; ")))
## export the composite (PNG/PDF/TIFF, 300 dpi)
.vpf <- file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$fig, "Panels"); dir.create(.vpf, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
.vst <- file.path(.vpf, "Panel6_variance_analysis")
try(ggplot2::ggsave(paste0(.vst, ".png"),  .vpanel, width = 13.5, height = 15, dpi = 300, device = grDevices::png,  type = "cairo"), silent = TRUE)
try(ggplot2::ggsave(paste0(.vst, ".pdf"),  .vpanel, width = 13.5, height = 15, device = grDevices::cairo_pdf), silent = TRUE)
try(ggplot2::ggsave(paste0(.vst, ".tiff"), .vpanel, width = 13.5, height = 15, dpi = 300, device = grDevices::tiff, type = "cairo", compression = "lzw"), silent = TRUE)
```

## 8.5 Residual-structure biplot — compPCA space (primary)

**This is the primary biplot.** It shows the **compositional PCA** — the *same* embedding the
Session-7 clusters, the UMAP and the Session-10 trajectory are built on — so its arrows explain
the structure those analyses actually use, not a neighbouring decomposition. That coherence is
the reason it leads: a biplot's job is "which proteins drive *these* clusters / *this*
trajectory?", and only the space the clusters were defined in answers it. Three further
advantages over the residual-APCA view (§8.6): it is **protein-level** (no per-gene peptide
selection at all), its axes carry a **real `percentVar`** (`sdev^2`, not a proxy), and because
its protein pool is already ≥ 30 %-detected, its arrows are the best-measured of any biplot
here (median detection ≈ 98 %, vs ≈ 82 % for the floored APCA).

The read-out: both a neuronal-cytoskeleton axis and a **VIM + mitochondrial-metabolism**
(GLUD1/HADHA/B) axis separate the clusters, and a histone/`PTMA` direction gives the
proliferative cluster its identity — converging independently with the chromatin + G2M/E2F
signature gated in §8.4. The **caveat** of this space is the mirror of APCA's: compPCA is
zero-imputed, so it *attenuates* (rather than inflates) sparse proteins and is blind to the
≥ 70 %-missing proteome — a conservative failure mode, harmless for an embedding, but it means
neither biplot is assumption-free. That §8.6 recovers the same split by a method whose bias
runs the *opposite* way is what makes the result robust (see there).

```{r identity-biplot-compPCA, fig.width=9, fig.height=6.5}
## Scores AND protein loadings come from the SAME prcomp (kept in §6.1), so the biplot
## geometry is internally consistent; `rotation` is computed by prcomp regardless.
.cs   <- as.matrix(reducedDim(sce, "compPCA"))[, 1:2]
.cl   <- metadata(sce)$compPCA_loadings
.cv   <- metadata(sce)$compPCA_pctVar
.cdet <- metadata(sce)$compPCA_detection
stopifnot(!is.null(.cl), !is.null(.cv))
## unity scaling (scplainer's convention, scp:::.scaleComponentsToUnity); defined locally
## so this chunk stands alone. Scores and arrows each scaled so the longest vector = 1.
.unit <- function(m) m / max(sqrt(rowSums(m^2)), na.rm = TRUE)
.L <- .unit(as.matrix(.cl[, 1:2])); .S <- .unit(.cs)
.tp <- head(order(sqrt(.L[, 1]^2 + .L[, 2]^2), decreasing = TRUE), 10)
.ld <- data.frame(gene = sub(";.*$", "", rownames(.L)[.tp]), PC1 = .L[.tp, 1], PC2 = .L[.tp, 2],
                  det = round(100 * .cdet[rownames(.L)[.tp]], 1), row.names = NULL)
.sd <- data.frame(PC1 = .S[, 1], PC2 = .S[, 2],
                  Cluster = factor(colLabels(sce)), AUCell = factor(sce$AUCell_type))
cat(sprintf("compPCA biplot: %d proteins | PC1 %.1f%% PC2 %.1f%% of TOTAL variance | arrows median detection %.0f%%\n  %s\n",
            nrow(.cl), .cv[1], .cv[2], median(.ld$det), paste(.ld$gene, collapse = ", ")))
.cbp <- function(col, title) ggplot(.sd, aes(PC1, PC2)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = .data[[col]]), size = 2.6, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_segment(data = .ld, aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = PC1, yend = PC2), inherit.aes = FALSE,
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm"), type = "closed"), linewidth = 0.4, colour = "grey30") +
  geom_text_repel(data = .ld, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, label = gene), inherit.aes = FALSE,
                  size = 4.5, colour = "grey20", max.overlaps = 20, box.padding = 0.5, segment.size = 0.3) +
  labs(x = sprintf("PC1 (%.1f%%)", .cv[1]), y = sprintf("PC2 (%.1f%%)", .cv[2]),
       title = title, colour = col) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 15) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
.pcb <- .cbp("Cluster", "compPCA — by cluster")
print(.pcb); save_fig(.pcb, "S8_biplot_compPCA_cluster.png", 9, 6.5)
print(.cbp("AUCell", "compPCA — by AUCell type"))
```

Per-top-loading-protein expression panels: the same 10 arrows, now shown as where each
driver is expressed. Cells sit at their compPCA scores, coloured by that protein's
row-centred log2 abundance (grey = not detected in that cell). This reads the arrows
concretely — e.g. the neuronal-cytoskeleton drivers light up one pole, the mitochondrial /
VIM drivers the other — and is the compPCA analogue of the residual-APCA panel in §8.6.

```{r identity-biplot-compPCA-loadings, fig.width=14, fig.height=8}
## Protein.Group log2 (row-centred, the same assay §8.6's panel uses); NA = grey.
.cpg <- assay(scp[["Protein.Group"]])
.crn <- rownames(.cl)[.tp]                       # full Protein.Group rownames of the top-10 loadings
.crn <- .crn[.crn %in% rownames(.cpg)]           # guard (compPCA is built from this assay, so all present)
.cdf <- data.frame(PC1 = .sd$PC1, PC2 = .sd$PC2, cell = rownames(.cs))   # cells at their compPCA scores
.cpanels <- lapply(.crn, function(rn) {
  .cdf$.expr <- .cpg[rn, .cdf$cell]
  det <- .cdf[!is.na(.cdf$.expr), ]; mis <- .cdf[is.na(.cdf$.expr), ]
  ggplot() +
    geom_point(data = mis, aes(PC1, PC2), size = 1.6, colour = "grey85", alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_point(data = det, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = .expr), size = 1.6, alpha = 0.9) +
    scale_colour_gradientn(colours = c("#2C5F8A", "#F0E442", "#D93F3F"), name = "log2") +
    labs(x = "compPCA PC1", y = "compPCA PC2", title = sub(";.*$", "", rn)) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
})
.cpall <- patchwork::wrap_plots(.cpanels, ncol = 4) +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(title = "compPCA — top loading proteins")
print(.cpall)
save_fig(.cpall, "S8_biplot_compPCA_top_loadings.png",
         w = 5.5 * min(4, length(.cpanels)), h = 4.5 * ceiling(length(.cpanels) / 4))
```

## 8.6 Residual-APCA biplot (supplementary — replication in the model's residual space)

This is a **supplementary cross-check**, not the primary read-out. It biplots the scplainer
**residual APCA** — the biological component left after the minimal model removes the loading
term — rather than the compPCA space the clusters live in. Its value is not a *new* result but
a **replication**: it recovers the same split as §8.5 — neuronal cytoskeleton
(TUBB3/STMN1/MAP1B/CRMP1/DPYSL5) vs **VIM + mitochondrial metabolism** (GLUD1) — from an
*independent* decomposition. Because compPCA (zero-fill) and residual APCA (NIPALS, no
imputation) carry missingness bias in **opposite directions** — attenuation vs variance
inflation — a signal an artifact of one would not reproduce in the other. That the two agree
is the robustness argument the pair is here to make.

<!-- The floor + aggregation below are what make this replication trustworthy: scplainer's
     stock top-by-vector-length rule, unfiltered, selects peptides seen in only 3-5 of 131
     cells (the old CDK1/RRM2 "proliferation" read rested on 4-cell peptides). Peptide loadings
     were stored on the object in Session 6.1. -->

```{r identity-biplot, fig.width=9, fig.height=6.5}
## cell scores (residual embedding) + current annotations
rd_res  <- as.matrix(reducedDim(sce, "residuals"))
cell_df <- data.frame(PC1 = rd_res[, 1], PC2 = rd_res[, 2], cell = colnames(sce),
                      Cluster = factor(colLabels(sce)),
                      AUCell  = factor(sce$AUCell_type),
                      Trans_Diameter = as.numeric(colData(sce)$Trans_Diameter))

## Arrow selection. Two deliberate departures from the stock scplainer recipe:
##  (1) DETECTION FLOOR. scplainer picks arrows purely by loading vector length
##      (scp:::.formatEigenVectors). On sparse DIA data that selects near-unobserved
##      peptides: unfiltered, 8/10 arrows came from peptides seen in 3-5 of 131 cells,
##      and max |loading| in the LEAST-detected decile is ~2x the most-detected one
##      (low-n variance inflation, not biology). The floor is what fixes this.
##  (2) per-gene AGGREGATION via scpComponentAggregate's recipe (median of the PCs over
##      the gene's surviving peptides) rather than cherry-picking each gene's most
##      extreme (= noisiest) peptide. NB aggregation ALONE makes things worse (it
##      shrinks multi-peptide genes while single-peptide noise passes through
##      untouched), so it is only ever applied on top of the floor.
BP_FLOOR <- 30                                   # peptide must be seen in >= this % of cells
lo <- metadata(sce)$apca_loadings
lo$det <- 100 * rowMeans(!is.na(assay(sce)))[match(lo$feature, rowData(sce)$Stripped.Sequence)]
lo <- lo[!is.na(lo$Genes) & lo$Genes != "" & !is.na(lo$det) & lo$det >= BP_FLOOR, ]
agg_lo <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(lo, lo$Genes), function(g)
  data.frame(Genes = g$Genes[1], PC1 = median(g$PC1), PC2 = median(g$PC2),
             det = median(g$det), n_pep = nrow(g), row.names = NULL)))

## scplainer's own scaling (scp:::.scaleComponentsToUnity): scale scores and loadings
## each so the longest vector = 1, making the two directly comparable. Replaces the
## ad-hoc `* 0.6` arrow fudge that used to live here.
.unit <- function(m) m / max(sqrt(rowSums(m^2)), na.rm = TRUE)
agg_lo[, c("PC1", "PC2")]  <- .unit(as.matrix(agg_lo[, c("PC1", "PC2")]))
cell_df[, c("PC1", "PC2")] <- .unit(as.matrix(cell_df[, c("PC1", "PC2")]))
top_peps <- head(agg_lo[order(-sqrt(agg_lo$PC1^2 + agg_lo$PC2^2)), ], 10)
cat(sprintf("biplot arrows: %d genes pass the >=%d%% detection floor | top-10 median detection %.0f%%\n  %s\n",
            nrow(agg_lo), BP_FLOOR, median(top_peps$det),
            paste(sub(";.*$", "", top_peps$Genes), collapse = ", ")))

## APCA carries no percentVar, and the old "% of captured var" proxy was misleading
## (a share of the RETAINED components, not of total variance) -> report no % at all.
xlab <- "Residual APCA PC1 (scaled)"; ylab <- "Residual APCA PC2 (scaled)"

loadings_layer <- list(
  geom_segment(data = top_peps, aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = PC1, yend = PC2),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm"), type = "closed"),
               linewidth = 0.4, colour = "grey30"),
  geom_text_repel(data = top_peps, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, label = sub(";.*$", "", Genes)),
                  inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 4.5, colour = "grey20",
                  max.overlaps = 20, box.padding = 0.5, segment.size = 0.3))
biplot_by <- function(col, title, continuous = FALSE) {
  p <- ggplot(cell_df, aes(PC1, PC2)) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = .data[[col]]), size = 2.6, alpha = 0.85) +
    loadings_layer + labs(x = xlab, y = ylab, title = title, colour = col) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 15) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
  if (continuous) p <- p + scale_colour_viridis_c(na.value = "grey85")
  p
}
p_bp <- biplot_by("Cluster", "Residual APCA — by cluster")
print(p_bp); save_fig(p_bp, "S8_biplot_residualAPCA_cluster.png", 9, 6.5)
print(biplot_by("AUCell", "Residual APCA — by AUCell type"))
p_bd <- biplot_by("Trans_Diameter", "Residual APCA — by cell diameter", TRUE)
print(p_bd); save_fig(p_bd, "S8_biplot_residualAPCA_diameter.png", 9, 6.5)
```

```{r identity-biplot-loadings, fig.width=14, fig.height=8}
## per-top-loading-protein expression panels (Protein.Group log2; NA = grey)
pg_mat    <- assay(scp[["Protein.Group"]])
top_genes <- intersect(unique(top_peps$Genes), rownames(pg_mat))
apca_panels <- lapply(top_genes, function(mk) {
  cell_df$.expr <- pg_mat[mk, cell_df$cell]
  det <- cell_df[!is.na(cell_df$.expr), ]; mis <- cell_df[is.na(cell_df$.expr), ]
  ggplot() +
    geom_point(data = mis, aes(PC1, PC2), size = 1.6, colour = "grey85", alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_point(data = det, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = .expr), size = 1.6, alpha = 0.9) +
    scale_colour_gradientn(colours = c("#2C5F8A", "#F0E442", "#D93F3F"), name = "log2") +
    labs(x = xlab, y = ylab, title = mk) + theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
})
p_all <- patchwork::wrap_plots(apca_panels, ncol = 4) +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(title = "Residual APCA — top loading proteins")
print(p_all)
save_fig(p_all, "S8_biplot_residualAPCA_top_loadings.png",
         w = 5.5 * min(4, length(apca_panels)), h = 4.5 * ceiling(length(apca_panels) / 4))
```

## 8.7 Biplot arrow robustness — the detection floor across both spaces

A supplementary check on *why* §8.6's arrows are detection-floored and why the compPCA biplot
(§8.5) is primary. Each panel biplots the top-10 loadings with **arrows coloured by protein-level
detection** — the % of cells with a non-missing `Protein.Group` value, read off the NA-containing
assay, **not** the zero-filled matrix that feeds the compPCA SVD. The floor is a different lever
in each space: compPCA's ≥ 30 % filter defines the *embedding* (removing it rebuilds the SVD on
all proteins), whereas APCA's floor only restricts which peptides may be *selected* as arrows
(the embedding is unchanged).

```{r biplot-floor-compare, fig.width=14, fig.height=12.5, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## top-10 loading biplots, arrows coloured by PROTEIN-level detection (NA-based on the raw
## Protein.Group assay, NOT the zero-filled compPCA matrix). compPCA reuses the floored §6.1
## embedding and rebuilds a no-floor variant on all proteins; APCA reuses the residual
## embedding with the arrow pool floored / unfloored.
.first  <- function(x) sub(";.*$", "", x)
.uscale <- function(m) m / max(sqrt(rowSums(m^2)), na.rm = TRUE)
.bcl    <- factor(colLabels(sce)); names(.bcl) <- colnames(sce)
.pgm    <- as.matrix(assay(scp[["Protein.Group"]]))                 # NA = undetected (zeroIsNA, §1)
.pgv    <- 100 * rowMeans(!is.na(.pgm)); names(.pgv) <- .first(rownames(.pgm))
.pgv    <- tapply(.pgv, names(.pgv), max)
.gdet   <- function(g, fb = NA_real_) { d <- as.numeric(.pgv[g]); d[is.na(d)] <- fb[is.na(d)]; round(d) }
.comppca <- function(floor) {          # >=30% = embedding filter; no-floor = all proteins (>=3 obs for the per-protein lm)
  m <- .pgm; det <- rowMeans(!is.na(m)); m <- m[if (floor) det >= 0.30 else rowSums(!is.na(m)) >= 3, , drop = FALSE]
  z <- with(as.data.frame(colData(scp)), (log_sumsRI_NoCRAP - mean(log_sumsRI_NoCRAP, na.rm=TRUE)) / sd(log_sumsRI_NoCRAP, na.rm=TRUE))
  r <- t(apply(m, 1, function(y){ ok <- !is.na(y); o <- rep(NA_real_, length(y)); b <- coef(stats::lm(y[ok] ~ z[ok])); o[ok] <- y[ok] - (b[1] + b[2]*z[ok]); o }))
  dimnames(r) <- dimnames(m); r <- sweep(r, 2, colMeans(r, na.rm=TRUE), "-")
  r0 <- r; r0[is.na(r0)] <- 0; r0 <- r0[apply(r0, 1, var) > 0, ]
  pc <- prcomp(t(r0), center=TRUE, scale.=TRUE, rank.=2)
  list(x = pc$x[, 1:2], rot = pc$rotation[, 1:2], det = det[rownames(pc$rotation)], n = nrow(r0))
}
.mkbp <- function(scores, cells, ld, title, sub) {
  .S <- .uscale(scores); .L <- .uscale(as.matrix(ld[, c("PC1","PC2")]))
  .s <- data.frame(PC1 = .S[,1], PC2 = .S[,2], Cluster = .bcl[cells])
  .a <- data.frame(gene = ld$gene, PC1 = .L[,1], PC2 = .L[,2], det = ld$det)
  ggplot(.s, aes(PC1, PC2)) +
    geom_point(aes(fill = Cluster), shape = 21, colour = "grey45", stroke = 0.15, size = 2.4, alpha = 0.9) +
    geom_segment(data = .a, aes(0, 0, xend = PC1, yend = PC2, colour = det), inherit.aes = FALSE,
                 arrow = grid::arrow(length = grid::unit(0.16, "cm"), type = "closed"), linewidth = 0.8) +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = .a, aes(PC1, PC2, label = gene), inherit.aes = FALSE,
                 size = 5.2, fontface = "bold", colour = "grey10", max.overlaps = 20, box.padding = 0.5, segment.size = 0.25) +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2", name = "Cluster") +
    scale_colour_viridis_c(name = "Protein detection\n(% of cells)", limits = c(0, 100)) +
    labs(x = "PC1 (scaled)", y = "PC2 (scaled)", title = title, subtitle = sub) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 12) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey35"), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "top")
}
.top <- function(rot, det) { i <- head(order(-sqrt(rot[,1]^2 + rot[,2]^2)), 10); nm <- rownames(rot)[i]; g <- .first(nm)
  data.frame(gene = g, PC1 = rot[i,1], PC2 = rot[i,2], det = .gdet(g, fb = round(100 * as.numeric(det[nm])))) }
## compPCA: floored embedding straight from §6.1 metadata; no-floor rebuilt on all proteins
.cnf  <- .comppca(FALSE); .cflr <- as.matrix(metadata(sce)$compPCA_loadings[, 1:2])
.bnf  <- .top(.cnf$rot, .cnf$det); .bfl <- .top(.cflr, metadata(sce)$compPCA_detection)
.pA <- .mkbp(.cnf$x, rownames(.cnf$x), .bnf, "compPCA (SVD) — no floor (all proteins)",
             sprintf("%d proteins in embedding | arrows median detection %d%%", .cnf$n, round(median(.bnf$det))))
.pB <- .mkbp(as.matrix(reducedDim(sce, "compPCA"))[, 1:2], colnames(sce), .bfl, "compPCA (SVD) — >=30% floor (§8.5, primary)",
             sprintf("%d proteins in embedding | arrows median detection %d%%", nrow(.cflr), round(median(.bfl$det))))
## APCA: one residual embedding, arrow pool unfloored / floored (per-gene median loading, scp recipe)
.rdm <- as.matrix(reducedDim(sce, "residuals"))[, 1:2]
.lom <- metadata(sce)$apca_loadings
.lom$det <- 100 * rowMeans(!is.na(assay(sce)))[match(.lom$feature, rowData(sce)$Stripped.Sequence)]
.lom <- .lom[!is.na(.lom$Genes) & .lom$Genes != "" & !is.na(.lom$det), ]
.aggl <- function(d) do.call(rbind, lapply(split(d, d$Genes), function(g)
  data.frame(gene = .first(g$Genes[1]), PC1 = median(g$PC1), PC2 = median(g$PC2), pepdet = median(g$det), row.names = NULL)))
.atop <- function(a) { a <- head(a[order(-sqrt(a$PC1^2 + a$PC2^2)), ], 10); a$det <- .gdet(a$gene, fb = a$pepdet); a }
.anf <- .atop(.aggl(.lom)); .afl <- .atop(.aggl(.lom[.lom$det >= 30, ]))
.pC <- .mkbp(.rdm, rownames(.rdm), .anf, "APCA (NIPALS residuals) — no floor (all peptides)",
             sprintf("arrows median detection %d%%", round(median(.anf$det))))
.pD <- .mkbp(.rdm, rownames(.rdm), .afl, "APCA (NIPALS residuals) — >=30% floor (§8.6)",
             sprintf("arrows median detection %d%%", round(median(.afl$det))))
.bgrid <- (.pA | .pB) / (.pC | .pD) + plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a", theme = theme(plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18), legend.position = "top"))
print(.bgrid)
save_fig(.bgrid, "S8_biplot_floor_comparison.png", w = 14, h = 12.5)
cat(sprintf("arrow median detection — APCA no-floor %d%% -> floored %d%% | compPCA no-floor %d%% -> floored %d%%\n",
            round(median(.anf$det)), round(median(.afl$det)), round(median(.bnf$det)), round(median(.bfl$det))))
```

The comparison is decisive. **APCA without a floor selects near-unobserved peptides** (panel c):
most arrows are proteins seen in only 2–4 of 131 cells (dark), because NIPALS applies no
shrinkage and top-by-loading-length lands on the noisy tail — flooring (panel d, = §8.6) removes
them. **compPCA arrows stay well-detected either way** (panels a/b, uniformly bright) — zero-fill
*attenuates* sparse proteins so they cannot dominate loadings — but dropping compPCA's floor
degrades the *cell* geometry (panel a: the extra ~1500 mostly-missing proteins inject zero-fill
noise that collapses the layout). So the floor protects the **APCA arrows** and the **compPCA
embedding**; both floored versions (b, d) recover the same neuronal-cytoskeleton-vs-metabolic
split — the convergence across two opposite-bias methods that makes the reading robust.

## 8.8 Loading concordance between the two DR spaces

§8.5–8.7 argue *visually* that the compPCA (SVD) and residual-APCA (NIPALS) biplots recover the
same biology. This quantifies it: a direct correlation of the two decompositions' **loadings**,
matched per gene (APCA's peptide loadings aggregated to gene by median), over the genes both
spaces share. Because PCA axes are rotated and signed arbitrarily between methods, alignment is
read from the full **cross-correlation matrix** and from **canonical correlations** (rotation-
and sign-invariant), not a naive PC1-vs-PC1 comparison.

```{r loading-concordance, fig.width=15, fig.height=5, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
.fg  <- function(x) sub(";.*$", "", x)
## compPCA loadings (protein-level) -> gene: keep the max-importance protein per first gene
.clm <- as.matrix(metadata(sce)$compPCA_loadings)
.cgn <- .fg(rownames(.clm)); .ordc <- order(-(.clm[,1]^2 + .clm[,2]^2))
.clg <- .clm[.ordc, , drop = FALSE][!duplicated(.cgn[.ordc]), , drop = FALSE]
rownames(.clg) <- .cgn[.ordc][!duplicated(.cgn[.ordc])]
## APCA loadings (peptide-level) -> gene: per-gene median of each PC (scp aggregation recipe)
.alm <- metadata(sce)$apca_loadings; .alm$gene <- .fg(.alm$Genes)
.alm <- .alm[!is.na(.alm$gene) & .alm$gene != "", ]; .apc <- paste0("PC", 1:10)
.agg <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(.alm[, .apc], .alm$gene), function(d) apply(as.matrix(d), 2, median)))
## match by gene; compare the top 5 PCs of each
.sh  <- intersect(rownames(.clg), rownames(.agg)); .K <- 5
.cc  <- .clg[.sh, 1:.K]; .ac <- .agg[.sh, 1:.K]
.mx  <- cor(.cc, .ac); dimnames(.mx) <- list(paste0("compPCA PC", 1:.K), paste0("APCA PC", 1:.K))
.can2 <- cancor(.cc[,1:2], .ac[,1:2])$cor                          # rotation/sign-invariant subspace alignment
.can3 <- cancor(.cc[,1:3], .ac[,1:3])$cor
.impc <- sqrt(.cc[,1]^2 + .cc[,2]^2); .impa <- sqrt(.ac[,1]^2 + .ac[,2]^2)
.spm  <- cor(.impc, .impa, method = "spearman")
.bmx  <- which(abs(.mx) == max(abs(.mx)), arr.ind = TRUE); .sgn <- sign(.mx[.bmx]); .ci <- .bmx[1]; .aj <- .bmx[2]
cat(sprintf("shared genes: %d | canonical cor PC1-2: %s | PC1-3: %s | importance Spearman %+.2f | best axis compPCA PC%d ~ APCA PC%d r=%+.2f\n",
            length(.sh), paste(round(.can2,2), collapse="/"), paste(round(.can3,2), collapse="/"), .spm, .ci, .aj, .mx[.bmx]))

.thc <- theme_bw(base_size = 12) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12), panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
.hdf <- expand.grid(comp = rownames(.mx), apca = colnames(.mx)); .hdf$r <- as.vector(.mx)
.hdf$comp <- factor(.hdf$comp, levels = rev(rownames(.mx)))
.lc_a <- ggplot(.hdf, aes(apca, comp, fill = r)) + geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", r)), size = 3.4) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B", midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1), name = "Pearson r") +
  labs(x = "APCA (NIPALS)", y = "compPCA (SVD)", title = "a  Loading cross-correlation (per gene)") +
  .thc + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
.scd <- data.frame(gene = .sh, x = .cc[, .ci], y = .ac[, .aj] * .sgn, imp = .impc)
.lcl <- .scd[order(-.scd$imp)[1:12], ]
.lc_b <- ggplot(.scd, aes(x, y)) + geom_point(aes(colour = imp), size = 1.6, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.6) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = .lcl, aes(label = gene), size = 3.6, fontface = "bold", max.overlaps = 20, box.padding = 0.4) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(name = "compPCA\n|loading|", option = "plasma") +
  labs(x = sprintf("compPCA PC%d loading", .ci), y = sprintf("APCA PC%d loading (sign-aligned)", .aj),
       title = sprintf("b  Best-aligned axis: r = %+.2f", .mx[.bmx])) + .thc
.imdf <- data.frame(impc = .impc, impa = .impa)
.lc_c <- ggplot(.imdf, aes(impc, impa)) + geom_point(size = 1.4, alpha = 0.5, colour = "#2166AC") +
  labs(x = "compPCA |PC1:2 loading|", y = "APCA |PC1:2 loading|",
       title = sprintf("c  Driver importance: Spearman %+.2f", .spm)) + .thc
.lcfig <- (.lc_a | .lc_b | .lc_c) + plot_layout(widths = c(1.1, 1, 0.9))
print(.lcfig)
save_fig(.lcfig, "S8_loading_concordance.png", w = 15, h = 5)
```

The leading driver subspace is **strongly shared**: the top compPCA axis maps onto APCA space at
canonical correlation **≈ 0.86** (its single best match, compPCA PC1 ~ APCA PC2, is r ≈ **0.78**),
and the same neuronal-cytoskeleton (STMN1 / CRMP1 / DYNC1H1) vs mitochondrial-metabolic
(GLUD1 / HADHA/B / ALDH9A1) genes anchor its two ends. Driver *importance* agrees more modestly
(Spearman ≈ **0.45**), as expected from methods differing in level (protein vs peptide), centring
(per-cell vs per-feature) and missing-handling (zero-fill vs NIPALS). That an **0.86** canonical
correlation holds between two decompositions whose missing-data biases run *opposite* ways is the
quantitative form of the §8.5–8.7 robustness argument; note only the top **two** directions are
common (PC1–3 canonical cor 0.86 / 0.72 / **0.06**), the third being method-specific.
