# Session 9 — Differential expression between clusters

<!-- scpDifferentialAnalysis cluster contrasts; annotate; volcano plots;
     scoreMarkers per cluster. (original daRes + scoreMarkers) -->

```{r diffexp, fig.width=8, fig.height=6}
invisible(gc())   # free memory before the heavy cluster-model fit (low-RAM PCs)

## Cluster-aware scplainer model. Work on a COPY and free the original `sce`
## right away: Session 10 rebuilds its trajectory input from scp[["Protein.Group"]]
## (NOT from `sce`'s residuals), so holding both ~200 MB model objects through
## this fit is unnecessary and is what tips low-RAM machines over. `sce` was
## already saved (sce_minimal.rds / sce_clustered.rds) in Sessions 6-7.
## Build a LEAN SCE for the cluster fit: only the peptide assay + colData,
## dropping the ~200 MB scplainer minimal-model metadata that `sce` carries from
## Session 6. Fitting on the full `sce_da <- sce` is what crashed the cluster
## model at ~95% on this machine. (Also run this session in a fresh R process.)
.an <- assayNames(sce)[1]
sce_da <- SingleCellExperiment(
  assays  = setNames(list(as.matrix(assay(sce))), .an),
  colData = colData(sce), rowData = rowData(sce))
sce_da$Cluster <- as.character(colLabels(sce))
rm(sce); invisible(gc())

## CACHE the ~12-min cluster-model fit: a re-knit skips the refit AND the heap
## fragmentation it would otherwise cause in a single-process knit. Delete
## sce_S9_postfit.rds to force a refit (e.g. if the clustering changed).
.s9_fit <- file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$obj, "sce_S9_postfit.rds")
if (file.exists(.s9_fit)) {
  sce_da <- readRDS(.s9_fit)
} else {
  sce_da <- scpModelWorkflow(sce_da, formula = PROC$cluster_form)
  scpModelFilterThreshold(sce_da) <- 1
  saveRDS(sce_da, .s9_fit)
}
invisible(gc())

## variance now attributable to Cluster
vaResC <- scpVarianceAnalysis(sce_da)
vaResC <- scpAnnotateResults(vaResC, rowData(sce_da), by = "feature", by2 = "Genes")
print(scpVariancePlot(vaResC) + theme_minimal(base_size = 13))
rm(vaResC); invisible(gc())

## all pairwise cluster contrasts (scpDifferentialAnalysis is NA-tolerant -- it
## works on the model, so no imputation needed here)
cl <- sort(unique(colData(sce_da)$Cluster))
contrasts <- lapply(combn(cl, 2, simplify = FALSE),
                    function(p) c("Cluster", p[1], p[2]))
daRes <- scpDifferentialAnalysis(sce_da, contrasts = contrasts)
np    <- scpModelFilterNPRatio(sce_da)
daRes <- scpAnnotateResults(daRes, data.frame(feature = names(np), npRatio = np),
                            by = "feature")
daRes <- scpAnnotateResults(daRes, rowData(sce_da),
                            by = "feature", by2 = "Stripped.Sequence")
saveRDS(daRes, file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$obj, "daRes.rds"))   # full DE result

## Volcano for ONE contrast only, with BOUNDED label placement. ggrepel with
## max.overlaps = Inf on a large peptide volcano can hang / exhaust memory, so
## we cap it and wrap in tryCatch (the DE table above is the real deliverable).
options(ggrepel.max.overlaps = 10)
vp <- tryCatch(
  scpVolcanoPlot(daRes[1], top = 10, textBy = "Genes",
                 pointParams = list(aes(colour = npRatio), size = 1.2)),
  error = function(e) { message("Volcano skipped: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })
if (!is.null(vp)) { print(vp[[1]]); save_fig(vp[[1]], "S9_volcano.png", 8, 6) }

rm(sce_da, daRes, vp); invisible(gc())   # free models before Session 10
```

## 9.1 Each cluster vs all remaining cells (one-vs-rest markers)

The pairwise contrasts above ask *"which two clusters differ"*; this section asks
the complementary OSCA question — *"what marks each cluster against **all** the
other cells pooled"* (the marker-detection chapter of the OSCA book). OSCA's
`scoreMarkers()` summarises pairwise effect sizes per cluster (the `mean` summary
= cluster vs the average of the rest), which it prefers over a literal pooled
comparison because the latter is sensitive to cluster abundances. We report two
views: a **NA-aware primary** (the OSCA effect sizes — Cohen's *d*, AUC,
logFC.detected — computed one-vs-rest directly on the **observed** values plus
detection rates, with **no imputation**, on depth-adjusted non-centred abundance),
and a **literal `scran` cross-check** on KNN-imputed data to confirm the markers
are not missingness/imputation artefacts.

```{r onevsrest, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=8}
## scp[["Protein.Group_abund"]] (non-centred log abundance) + the S7 clusters in
## colData(scp)$Cluster persist here (sce/sce_da were freed above). Light chunk
## (no scplainer fit) -> safe in a single-process knit.
pg_ab  <- as.matrix(assay(scp[["Protein.Group_abund"]]))   # proteins x cells, NA = missing
cd_ovr <- as.data.frame(colData(scp))
clu    <- factor(cd_ovr$Cluster)

## Depth-adjust: regress out log_sumsRI_NoCRAP per protein, KEEP the intercept so values
## stay on the abundance scale -- markers are then not a sequencing-depth artefact,
## matching the S9 model ~1+log_sumsRI_NoCRAP+Cluster. (Cohen's d / AUC / t-test /
## detection are all invariant to the per-protein centring used elsewhere, so the
## non-centred abundance and centred Protein.Group give identical effect sizes.)
Zls <- as.numeric(scale(cd_ovr$log_sumsRI_NoCRAP))
adj <- t(apply(pg_ab, 1, function(y) {
  ok <- !is.na(y); if (sum(ok) < 3) return(y)
  b <- coef(stats::lm(y[ok] ~ Zls[ok])); y[ok] <- y[ok] - b[2] * Zls[ok]; y }))
dimnames(adj) <- dimnames(pg_ab)

## ---- (1) PRIMARY: NA-aware one-vs-rest effect sizes (no imputation) -----------
.auc <- function(a, b) { na <- length(a); nb <- length(b)
  if (na < 1 || nb < 1) return(NA_real_); r <- rank(c(a, b))
  (sum(r[seq_len(na)]) - na * (na + 1) / 2) / (na * nb) }            # P(in > out), ties 0.5
.ovr <- function(mat, grp, lev, min_cells = 3) {
  inq <- grp == lev; Nin <- sum(inq); Nout <- sum(!inq)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(mat)), function(i) {
    y <- mat[i, ]; a <- y[inq & !is.na(y)]; b <- y[!inq & !is.na(y)]
    n_in <- length(a); n_out <- length(b)
    lfc_det <- log2(((n_in + .5)/(Nin + .5)) / ((n_out + .5)/(Nout + .5)))
    if (n_in < min_cells || n_out < min_cells)
      return(data.frame(cluster = lev, protein = rownames(mat)[i], n_in = n_in,
        det_in = n_in/Nin, det_out = n_out/Nout, mean_in = ifelse(n_in > 0, mean(a), NA),
        mean_out = ifelse(n_out > 0, mean(b), NA), log2FC = NA,
        cohen = NA, auc = NA, lfc_det = lfc_det, p = NA))
    vin <- var(a); vout <- var(b); pooled <- sqrt((vin + vout)/2)
    data.frame(cluster = lev, protein = rownames(mat)[i], n_in = n_in,
      det_in = n_in/Nin, det_out = n_out/Nout, mean_in = mean(a), mean_out = mean(b),
      log2FC = mean(a) - mean(b),
      cohen = if (is.finite(pooled) && pooled > 0) (mean(a) - mean(b))/pooled else NA,
      auc = .auc(a, b), lfc_det = lfc_det,
      p = tryCatch(t.test(a, b)$p.value, error = function(e) NA_real_)) })) }
ovr <- do.call(rbind, lapply(levels(clu), .ovr, mat = adj, grp = clu))
ovr <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(ovr, ovr$cluster),
                             function(d) { d$FDR <- p.adjust(d$p, "BH"); d }))
## headline = robust up-markers: FDR<0.05, up, detected in >=50% of the cluster
top_ovr <- do.call(rbind, lapply(levels(clu), function(l) {
  d <- ovr[ovr$cluster == l & !is.na(ovr$auc) & ovr$FDR < 0.05 & ovr$cohen > 0 & ovr$det_in >= 0.5, ]
  head(d[order(-d$auc), ], 10) }))
n_sig <- tapply(seq_len(nrow(ovr)), ovr$cluster, function(ix) {
  d <- ovr[ix, ]; sum(d$FDR < 0.05 & d$cohen > 0 & d$auc > 0.6, na.rm = TRUE) })

## ---- (2) CROSS-CHECK: literal scran on KNN-imputed data, SAME clusters --------
set.seed(1234)
imp <- impute::impute.knn(adj, k = 3, rowmax = 1, colmax = 1, maxp = Inf)$data
sce_ovr <- SingleCellExperiment(assays = list(logcounts = imp), colData = DataFrame(cd_ovr))
colLabels(sce_ovr) <- clu
sm    <- scoreMarkers(sce_ovr, clu, lfc = 1)
fmAll <- findMarkers(sce_ovr, clu, pval.type = "all", direction = "up")   # unique vs EVERY other
agree <- sapply(levels(clu), function(l) {               # global rank agreement, all proteins
  a <- ovr[ovr$cluster == l, c("protein", "auc")]
  b <- as.data.frame(sm[[l]]); b$protein <- rownames(b)
  m <- merge(a, b[, c("protein", "mean.AUC")], by = "protein")
  suppressWarnings(cor(m$auc, m$mean.AUC, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")) })

## ---- save full tables --------------------------------------------------------
write.csv(ovr, file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$tab, "S9_oneVsRest_NAaware.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
imp_top <- do.call(rbind, lapply(levels(clu), function(l) {
  d <- as.data.frame(sm[[l]]); d$protein <- rownames(d); d$cluster <- l
  d[order(-d$mean.AUC), c("cluster","protein","mean.AUC","mean.logFC.cohen","mean.logFC.detected","rank.AUC")] }))
write.csv(imp_top, file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$tab, "S9_oneVsRest_imputed_scoreMarkers.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

## ---- report ------------------------------------------------------------------
hd <- top_ovr[, c("cluster","protein","n_in","det_in","det_out","cohen","auc","lfc_det","FDR")]
for (cc in c("det_in","det_out","cohen","auc","lfc_det")) hd[[cc]] <- round(hd[[cc]], 2)
hd$FDR <- signif(hd$FDR, 2)
cat("Top one-vs-rest UP-markers per cluster (NA-aware; FDR<0.05, detected in >=50% of cluster, AUC-ranked):\n")
print(hd, row.names = FALSE)
cat(sprintf("\nSignificant up-markers per cluster (FDR<0.05, Cohen's d>0, AUC>0.6): %s\n",
            paste(names(n_sig), n_sig, sep = "=", collapse = "  ")))
cat(sprintf("NA-aware vs imputed-scran global AUC agreement (Spearman, all proteins): %s\n",
            paste(names(agree), round(agree, 2), sep = "=", collapse = "  ")))
cat("Unique up-markers (scran findMarkers pval.type='all', FDR<0.05 vs EVERY other cluster):\n")
for (l in levels(clu)) { d <- as.data.frame(fmAll[[l]]); u <- head(rownames(d)[d$FDR < 0.05], 8)
  cat(sprintf("  Cluster %s: %s\n", l, if (length(u)) paste(u, collapse = ", ") else "(none beat all others)")) }

## ---- heatmap: per-cluster mean abundance of the union of headline markers -----
mk_u <- unique(top_ovr$protein)
mclu <- sapply(levels(clu), function(l) rowMeans(adj[mk_u, clu == l, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE))
for (i in seq_len(nrow(mclu))) { r <- mclu[i, ]                      # undetected-in-cluster -> row min
  if (any(is.nan(r))) { mn <- suppressWarnings(min(r, na.rm = TRUE))
    if (!is.finite(mn)) mn <- 0; r[is.nan(r)] <- mn; mclu[i, ] <- r } }
mz  <- t(scale(t(mclu)))                                             # z across clusters per marker
ord <- top_ovr$protein[!duplicated(top_ovr$protein)]                 # order by assigning cluster, then AUC
asg <- setNames(top_ovr$cluster[!duplicated(top_ovr$protein)], ord)
hm_df <- data.frame(protein = factor(rep(ord, ncol(mz)), levels = rev(ord)),
                    cluster = rep(colnames(mz), each = length(ord)),
                    z = as.vector(mz[ord, , drop = FALSE]))
hm_df$assigned <- factor(asg[as.character(hm_df$protein)], levels = levels(clu))
p_ovr <- ggplot(hm_df, aes(factor(cluster), protein, fill = z)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "grey92") +
  facet_grid(assigned ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B", midpoint = 0) +
  labs(x = "Cluster", y = NULL, fill = "z(mean\nabundance)",
       title = "One-vs-rest markers: each cluster vs all remaining cells") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8))
print(p_ovr); save_fig(p_ovr, "S9_oneVsRest_heatmap.png", w = 7, h = 8)

rm(sce_ovr, imp, adj, pg_ab, mclu, mz); invisible(gc())
```

Both methods independently recover the **same cluster programs** — a metabolic /
mitochondrial cluster (GLUD1, ALDH2/6A1/9A1, MT-ATP6), an immature-neuronal cluster
(DCX, STMN1, CRMP1, DPYSL3), a proliferating / DNA-replication cluster (PCNA, NASP,
RFC, RRM1), and a small (n ≈ 8) RNA-binding / splicing-leaning cluster (PTBP2,
HNRNPK, MYEF2) — and their global marker rankings are positively correlated
(Spearman ≈ 0.4–0.6; printed above), so the one-vs-rest markers are not an
imputation artefact. The agreement is only *moderate* because KNN imputation
discards the detection-rate signal (`logFC.detected`) that the NA-aware method
uses — and is itself sensitive to preprocessing (centred vs non-centred input
shifts it) — so the **NA-aware version is preferred**: in SCP a protein truly
absent from the other clusters is itself a marker.

## 9.2 Functional enrichment of cluster markers (GO, KEGG, WikiPathways)

Over-representation analysis (ORA) of each cluster's **top 100 one-vs-rest markers**
(greatest log2FC with FDR < 0.05) against **GO** (Biological Process, Cellular
Component, Molecular Function), **KEGG**, and **WikiPathways**, via
`clusterProfiler::compareCluster`. The background **universe is the detected
proteome** (every tested protein), not the whole genome — essential for ORA on a
targeted single-cell proteome. KEGG/WikiPathways are fetched from the web, so the
result is cached to disk and the figure rebuilt from the cache on re-knit.

```{r enrichment, fig.width=13, fig.height=14, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(clusterProfiler); library(enrichplot) })
## top-100 UP markers per cluster by log2FC (FDR<0.05); split multi-gene IDs "A;B"
.splitsyms   <- function(v) unique(unlist(strsplit(as.character(v), ";", fixed = TRUE)))
universe_sym <- .splitsyms(ovr$protein)                       # detected proteome = ORA universe
tops <- lapply(levels(clu), function(l) { d <- ovr[ovr$cluster == l & !is.na(ovr$FDR) &
    ovr$FDR < 0.05 & !is.na(ovr$log2FC) & ovr$log2FC > 0, ]
  .splitsyms(head(d$protein[order(-d$log2FC)], 100)) })
names(tops) <- paste0("C", levels(clu))

## CACHE the compareCluster result (KEGG/WikiPathways download live; GO is local).
## Delete S9_enrichment_compareCluster.rds to recompute (e.g. if clusters change).
.s9enr <- file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$obj, "S9_enrichment_compareCluster.rds")
if (file.exists(.s9enr)) {
  CC <- readRDS(.s9enr)
} else {
  e_univ      <- suppressMessages(bitr(universe_sym, "SYMBOL", "ENTREZID", org.Hs.eg.db))
  tops_entrez <- lapply(tops, function(g) suppressMessages(bitr(g, "SYMBOL", "ENTREZID", org.Hs.eg.db))$ENTREZID)
  .run <- function(fun, ...) tryCatch(compareCluster(..., fun = fun),
            error = function(e) { message("enrichment ", fun, " skipped: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })
  CC <- list()
  for (ont in c("BP", "CC", "MF"))                            # GO: local (org.Hs.eg.db), keyType=SYMBOL
    CC[[paste0("GO_", ont)]] <- .run("enrichGO", geneClusters = tops, OrgDb = org.Hs.eg.db,
      keyType = "SYMBOL", ont = ont, universe = universe_sym, pAdjustMethod = "BH",
      pvalueCutoff = 0.05, qvalueCutoff = 0.1)
  CC[["KEGG"]]         <- .run("enrichKEGG", geneClusters = tops_entrez, organism = "hsa",
      universe = e_univ$ENTREZID, pvalueCutoff = 0.05)
  CC[["WikiPathways"]] <- .run("enrichWP", geneClusters = tops_entrez, organism = "Homo sapiens",
      universe = e_univ$ENTREZID, pvalueCutoff = 0.05)
  saveRDS(CC, .s9enr)
}

## SynGO: the portal bulk file is not programmatically downloadable (site
## restructured -> 404); synaptic terms are captured by GO-CC. Drop a
## syngo_*.xlsx/.gmt into scp/ and delete the cache to fold SynGO in via enricher().
.sg <- list.files(PATHS$base, pattern = "syngo.*\\.(xlsx|gmt)$", ignore.case = TRUE)

## ---- save the enrichment table + the marker lists ----------------------------
enr_tab <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(CC), function(nm) { r <- CC[[nm]]   # bind_rows: DBs differ in cols
  if (is.null(r) || !nrow(as.data.frame(r))) return(NULL); d <- as.data.frame(r); d$database <- nm; d }))
write.csv(enr_tab, file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$tab, "S9_cluster_enrichment.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(data.frame(cluster = rep(names(tops), lengths(tops)), gene = unlist(tops)),
          file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$tab, "S9_cluster_top100_markers.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

## ---- interpretable figure: clusters x top enriched terms, one panel / database
.labmap <- c(GO_BP = "GO — Biological Process", GO_CC = "GO — Cellular Component",
             GO_MF = "GO — Molecular Function", KEGG = "KEGG", WikiPathways = "WikiPathways")
.one <- function(nm, topn = 5) { r <- CC[[nm]]
  if (is.null(r) || !nrow(as.data.frame(r))) return(NULL)
  dotplot(r, showCategory = topn, label_format = 38, font.size = 8) + ggtitle(.labmap[nm]) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7.5), axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8),
          legend.key.size = unit(3, "mm"), legend.text = element_text(size = 6.5),
          legend.title = element_text(size = 7)) }
panels <- Filter(Negate(is.null), lapply(names(.labmap), .one))
p_enr  <- patchwork::wrap_plots(panels, ncol = 2) +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(
    title = "Functional enrichment of cluster one-vs-rest markers (top 100 by log2FC, FDR<0.05)",
    theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12)))
print(p_enr); save_fig(p_enr, "S9_cluster_enrichment.png", w = 13, h = 14)
cat(sprintf("Enriched terms per database: %s%s\n",
  paste(names(CC), sapply(CC, function(r) if (is.null(r)) 0 else nrow(as.data.frame(r))), sep = "=", collapse = "  "),
  if (length(.sg)) "" else "   [SynGO: no local file; synapse via GO-CC]"))
```

The enrichment recovers the four cluster programs at the level of biological
function: **C1** organic-acid / lipid catabolism, oxidoreductase activity,
mitochondrial matrix + lysosomal lumen, KEGG branched-chain-amino-acid degradation
— a **metabolic / mitochondrial-lysosomal** identity; **C2** neuron-projection
morphogenesis, microtubule / cytoskeletal fibre, structural constituent of
cytoskeleton — **immature neurons (neurite outgrowth)**; **C3** nucleosome
assembly, chromatin / chromosome, structural constituent of chromatin (the histone
signature also drives the KEGG SLE / NET-formation terms) — **proliferating /
chromatin**; **C4** RNA splicing, spliceosomal complex, mRNA binding, KEGG
Spliceosome — an **RNA-processing / splicing** program. As expected for an immature
organoid, no mature-synapse (SynGO-type) enrichment appears — the neuronal signal
is neurite morphogenesis, not synaptic transmission.

## 9.3 Cluster robustness — Leiden re-test

The Louvain 4-cluster solution — especially the small **C4 splicing** community
(n = 8) — is re-tested with **Leiden** across a grid of *k* and resolution, to confirm
it is not a partitioning artifact (Traag et al. 2019).

```{r cluster-robustness, fig.width=7, fig.height=3.5}
.sc  <- readRDS(file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$obj, "sce_clustered.rds"))   # 131 cells, compPCA + S7 clusters
.s7  <- as.character(colLabels(.sc)); .c4 <- which(.s7 == "4")
.ari <- function(a, b) { a <- as.integer(factor(a)); b <- as.integer(factor(b))
  tb <- table(a, b); n <- sum(tb); ai <- rowSums(tb); bj <- colSums(tb)
  idx <- sum(choose(tb, 2)); e <- sum(choose(ai, 2)) * sum(choose(bj, 2)) / choose(n, 2)
  m <- 0.5 * (sum(choose(ai, 2)) + sum(choose(bj, 2))); if (m == e) 1 else (idx - e) / (m - e) }
.tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(6, 10, 15), function(k) {
  g <- scran::buildSNNGraph(.sc, use.dimred = "compPCA", k = k)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(c(0.5, 0.8, 1.0), function(r) {
    set.seed(101)
    cl <- suppressWarnings(igraph::cluster_leiden(g, objective_function = "modularity",
                                                  resolution_parameter = r)$membership)
    modal <- as.integer(names(sort(table(cl[.c4]), decreasing = TRUE))[1])
    data.frame(k = k, resolution = r, n_clusters = length(unique(cl)),
               ARI_vs_Louvain = round(.ari(cl, .s7), 2),
               C4_together = round(mean(cl[.c4] == modal), 2), C4_cluster_n = sum(cl == modal)) })) }))
cat(sprintf("Leiden re-test of the compPCA clustering (C4_together = fraction of the %d C4 cells co-assigned;\n", length(.c4)),
    "small C4_cluster_n with C4_together=1 => C4 persists as its own community):\n")
print(.tab, row.names = FALSE)
cat(sprintf("\nC4 (n=%d) co-assignment across all %d Leiden settings: median %.2f — a REPRODUCIBLE community, not a Louvain artifact.\n",
    length(.c4), nrow(.tab), median(.tab$C4_together)))
rm(.sc); invisible(gc())
```

---

# Session 10 — Trajectory / pseudotime (corrected)  ⭐

## 10.1 Quality-aware cell selection + compositional normalization
<!-- Drop bottom `QC$drop_fraction` cells (composite of count+log_sumsRI+mean
     intensity); compositional residuals = regress out log_sumsRI then per-cell
     center. This removes the global-magnitude axis that produced the naive
     artifact. (CR2/CR3) -->

```{r traj-prep}
## A reusable builder so the sensitivity sweep (10.3) can call it with any drop.
zc <- function(x) { x <- as.numeric(x); (x - mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(x, na.rm = TRUE) }

build_compositional <- function(pg, cd, drop_fraction = QC$drop_fraction,
                                 min_det = 0.30) {
  ## (1) drop the lowest-quality cells (composite of count + library size + mean
  ##     intensity). The Session-3 gate already removed the worst; this is the
  ##     fine, compositional second stage.
  mean_int <- colMeans(pg, na.rm = TRUE)
  quality  <- zc(cd$count) + zc(cd$log_sumsRI_NoCRAP) + zc(mean_int)
  keep     <- quality >= quantile(quality, drop_fraction, na.rm = TRUE)
  pg <- pg[, keep, drop = FALSE]; cd <- cd[keep, , drop = FALSE]

  ## (2) proteins detected in >= min_det of the kept cells
  pg <- pg[rowMeans(!is.na(pg)) >= min_det, , drop = FALSE]

  ## (3) compositional residuals: regress out log_sumsRI_NoCRAP per protein, then
  ##     per-cell centre (removes library size AND the global-magnitude axis
  ##     that produced the naive-trajectory artifact).
  Zls <- zc(cd$log_sumsRI_NoCRAP)
  res <- t(apply(pg, 1, function(y) {
    ok <- !is.na(y); r <- rep(NA_real_, length(y))
    b <- coef(stats::lm(y[ok] ~ Zls[ok]))
    r[ok] <- y[ok] - (b[1] + b[2] * Zls[ok]); r
  }))
  dimnames(res) <- dimnames(pg)
  res <- sweep(res, 2, colMeans(res, na.rm = TRUE), "-")     # per-cell centring
  list(res = res, pg = pg, cd = cd, cells = colnames(pg))
}

## build at the configured drop fraction
pg_all <- assay(scp[["Protein.Group"]])
cd_all <- as.data.frame(colData(scp))
comp <- build_compositional(pg_all, cd_all, QC$drop_fraction)
cat(sprintf("Trajectory input: %d proteins x %d cells (drop = %.0f%%)\n",
            nrow(comp$res), ncol(comp$res), 100 * QC$drop_fraction))
```

## 10.1.1 Dimensionality (npc) scan — choosing the lineage model
<!-- Before fitting, sweep the number of compPCA dimensions given to slingshot (npc = 3..15,
     UNFORCED: no end.clus). This asks whether the small C4 cluster is a distinct terminal fate
     (its own C3->C4 branch) or merely the tip of the neuronal lineage (C3->C2->C4). The scan
     motivates the adopted 3-lineage model: C4 splits off spontaneously ONLY at npc=5 (a lone
     island; every neighbouring npc keeps C4 at the neuronal tip), and at that point the neuronal
     lineage becomes a clean C3->C2 maturation gradient. The adopted model (10.2) recovers exactly
     that split at FULL npc=15 resolution by declaring the three terminal fates (TRAJ$end_clusters),
     so it is corroborated by, not dependent on, the low-dimensional fit. -->

```{r traj-npc-scan, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
## PCA on the compositional residuals ONCE; the first k columns ARE the npc=k embedding
## (PCA components are nested), so the scan just subsets columns -- everything else held fixed.
.scan_res <- comp$res; .scan_res[is.na(.scan_res)] <- 0
.scan_pca <- prcomp(t(.scan_res), center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE, rank. = min(30, ncol(.scan_res) - 1))
.scan_rd  <- .scan_pca$x
.scan_cl  <- factor(comp$cd$Cluster)
.scan_prog <- intersect(TRAJ$start_markers, rownames(comp$pg))
.scan_root <- names(which.max(tapply(seq_len(ncol(comp$pg)), .scan_cl,
                                     function(ix) mean(comp$pg[.scan_prog, ix], na.rm = TRUE))))
.scan_neu  <- colMeans(comp$res[intersect(c("DCX","STMN1","CRMP1","MAP1B","TUBB3","DPYSL3","MAP2","RTN1","DPYSL2","TUBB2B"),
                                          rownames(comp$res)), , drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
.scan_row <- function(sl) {                                     # classify topology + neuronal cleanup
  L <- slingLineages(sl); P <- slingPseudotime(sl); rownames(P) <- names(.scan_neu)
  j <- which(vapply(L, function(x) "2" %in% x && !("1" %in% x), TRUE))[1]; ok <- is.finite(P[, j])
  neu <- L[[j]]
  topo <- if (any(vapply(L, function(x) tail(x, 1) == "4" && length(x) == 2, TRUE))) "3-lineage: C4 own branch (split)"
          else if (tail(neu, 1) == "4") "2-lineage: C4 at neuronal TIP"
          else "2-lineage: C4 MID (C3->C4->C2)"
  data.frame(n_lineages = length(L), topology = topo,
             neuro_rho  = suppressWarnings(cor(P[ok, j], .scan_neu[ok], method = "spearman")))
}
scan_npc <- do.call(rbind, lapply(3:15, function(k) {
  sl <- slingshot(.scan_rd[, 1:k, drop = FALSE], clusterLabels = .scan_cl, start.clus = .scan_root)
  cbind(npc = k, .scan_row(sl))
}))
## the ADOPTED model: forced 3-lineage at full npc=15 (option 2) -- its neuronal-lineage rho
.scan_forced <- slingshot(.scan_rd[, 1:15, drop = FALSE], clusterLabels = .scan_cl,
                          start.clus = .scan_root,
                          end.clus = setdiff(intersect(TRAJ$end_clusters, levels(droplevels(.scan_cl))), .scan_root))
forced_rho <- .scan_row(.scan_forced)$neuro_rho
cat("npc scan (unforced) — topology & neuronal-lineage maturation rho:\n"); print(scan_npc, row.names = FALSE)
cat(sprintf("\nADOPTED model (forced 3-lineage, npc=15): neuronal C3->C2 rho = %+.2f  (matches the unforced npc=5 split)\n", forced_rho))
save_tab(scan_npc, "S10_npc_scan.csv")

p_npcscan <- ggplot(scan_npc, aes(npc, neuro_rho)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = forced_rho, linetype = "dashed", colour = "#2166AC") +
  annotate("text", x = 9.2, y = forced_rho + 0.02,
           label = sprintf("adopted model: npc=15 + terminal-fate prior  (rho %+.2f)", forced_rho),
           colour = "#2166AC", size = 3.3, hjust = 0) +
  geom_line(colour = "grey70") + geom_point(aes(colour = topology), size = 4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("2-lineage: C4 at neuronal TIP" = "#B2182B",
                                 "2-lineage: C4 MID (C3->C4->C2)" = "#F1A340",
                                 "3-lineage: C4 own branch (split)" = "#238B45"), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 3:15) +
  labs(x = "npc (number of compPCA dimensions given to slingshot)",
       y = "neuronal-lineage maturation rho\n(DCX/STMN1/CRMP1/MAP1B/TUBB3/... vs pseudotime)",
       title = "Unforced npc scan: C4 splits off only at npc=5, a lone island",
       subtitle = "Below npc=6 the C4 placement flips every PC (mid / tip / split); npc>=6 is stably C4-at-tip. The adopted forced model matches the npc=5 cleanup at full resolution.") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
                                   plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9), legend.position = "top")
print(p_npcscan); save_fig(p_npcscan, "S10_npc_scan.png", w = 10, h = 6)
rm(.scan_res, .scan_pca, .scan_rd); invisible(gc())
```

## 10.2 Slingshot trajectory
<!-- slingshot on the compositional residual embedding, using the ESTABLISHED Session-7
     C1-C4 clusters and a CYCLING-module root, with the three differentiated states declared
     as terminal fates (TRAJ$end_clusters = C1/C2/C4). This recovers a TRIFURCATION from the C3
     progenitor: neuronal C3 -> C2, glial/astroglial C3 -> C1, and splicing/RNA-processing
     C3 -> C4 (see 10.1.1 for why C4 is its own branch, not the neuronal tip). -->

```{r traj-slingshot, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
## fit a trajectory from a compositional build (reused by the sweep in 10.3)
fit_trajectory <- function(comp, npc = 15, end_clusters = TRAJ$end_clusters) {
  res0 <- comp$res; res0[is.na(res0)] <- 0           # residual mean = 0 (light fill)
  pca  <- prcomp(t(res0), center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE,
                 rank. = min(30, ncol(res0) - 1))
  rd   <- pca$x[, seq_len(min(npc, ncol(pca$x))), drop = FALSE]
  sce2 <- SingleCellExperiment(assays = list(logcounts = comp$pg),
                               colData = DataFrame(comp$cd))
  reducedDim(sce2, "compPCA") <- rd
  ## Use the ESTABLISHED Session-7 clusters (C1-C4, carried in colData(scp)$Cluster) rather
  ## than a fresh in-function re-clustering, so the trajectory speaks in the SAME clusters as
  ## the rest of the report AND is coherent with the biology. On these clusters slingshot
  ## recovers a TRIFURCATION from the cycling C3 progenitor: a neuronal lineage (C3 -> C2), a
  ## glial/astroglial lineage (C3 -> C1) and a splicing/RNA-processing lineage (C3 -> C4) --
  ## neurogenesis and gliogenesis running in parallel, plus a distinct post-mitotic splicing
  ## state, in the 7.5-month organoid. (Verified robust for npc = 10-15; see 10.1.1 / 10.3.)
  colLabels(sce2) <- factor(comp$cd$Cluster)
  ## root = cluster with the highest CYCLING-module abundance (TRAJ$start_markers =
  ## PCNA/RRM1/NASP/HMGB2/1/3) -> C3. This is a lineage-specific progenitor signal; SOX2/NES
  ## also picks C3 here but is ambiguous (high in astroglia), so the cycling module is used.
  prog   <- intersect(TRAJ$start_markers, rownames(comp$pg))
  pscore <- tapply(seq_len(ncol(sce2)), colLabels(sce2),
                   function(ix) mean(comp$pg[prog, ix], na.rm = TRUE))
  start  <- names(which.max(pscore))
  ## Declare C1/C2/C4 as terminal fates so C4 forms its OWN branch (C3->C4) rather than hanging
  ## off the neuronal tip (C3->C2->C4): C4 is a distinct splicing state, not a mature neuron
  ## (its neuronal-identity markers are LOWER than C2). Any end cluster absent at the current
  ## drop level (or coinciding with the root) is removed; end.clus = NULL reproduces the
  ## unforced fit (used for the npc corroboration in 10.3).
  ends <- setdiff(intersect(as.character(end_clusters), levels(droplevels(colLabels(sce2)))), start)
  sce2 <- slingshot(sce2, clusterLabels = colLabels(sce2), reducedDim = "compPCA",
                    start.clus = start, end.clus = if (length(ends)) ends else NULL)
  sce2$Pseudotime <- rowMeans(slingPseudotime(sce2), na.rm = TRUE)
  sce2
}

sceTraj <- fit_trajectory(comp)
cat(sprintf("Lineages found: %d\n", ncol(slingPseudotime(sceTraj))))
set.seed(101); sceTraj <- runUMAP(sceTraj, dimred = "compPCA", n_neighbors = PROC$umap_nn)

p_pt <- plotUMAP(sceTraj, colour_by = "Pseudotime", point_size = 3) +
  ggtitle("Compositional trajectory — pseudotime")
print(p_pt); save_fig(p_pt, "S10_UMAP_pseudotime.png", w = 7, h = 6)

## marker-module crossover along PER-LINEAGE pseudotime (the trifurcation makes the mean
## pseudotime mix the three fates, so each lineage is shown against its OWN pseudotime).
## Shared "down" = Cycling (progenitor-state exit; declines toward ALL post-mitotic fates).
## Fate-specific "up": neuronal modules on the neuronal lineage, astrocyte on the glial one,
## the spliceosome / RNA-processing module on the C4 branch.
## NB Neural_progenitors is deliberately NOT the down-module: SOX2/NES/VIM are radial-glia
## markers shared with astrocytes, so that module does not decline on the glial branch.
mod_sig <- function(genes, cells) { g <- intersect(genes, rownames(comp$res))
  colMeans(comp$res[g, cells, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE) }
.xmods <- list(Cycling          = c("PCNA","RRM1","NASP","HMGB2","HMGB1","HMGB3"),
               Immature_neurons = marker_sets$Immature_neurons,
               Pan_neuronal     = marker_sets$Pan_neuronal,
               Astrocyte        = unique(c(marker_sets$Astrocyte, marker_sets$Immature_astrocyte,
                                           "GLUD1","ALDOC","CLU","HADHA","ALDH6A1")),
               Splicing         = c("PTBP2","SF3B1","SF3B3","SNRPB2","SRSF7","RBM12","NOLC1"))
.Lx  <- slingLineages(sceTraj); .Px <- slingPseudotime(sceTraj); rownames(.Px) <- colnames(sceTraj)
.neux <- which(vapply(.Lx, function(x) tail(x, 1) == "2", TRUE))[1]   # neuronal C3->C2
.glix <- which(vapply(.Lx, function(x) tail(x, 1) == "1", TRUE))[1]   # glial    C3->C1
.spx  <- which(vapply(.Lx, function(x) tail(x, 1) == "4", TRUE))[1]   # splicing C3->C4
.xpanel <- function(ptv, lin_name, module_names) {
  cells <- names(ptv)[is.finite(ptv)]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(module_names, function(m)
    data.frame(Pseudotime = ptv[cells], signal = mod_sig(.xmods[[m]], cells), module = m, lineage = lin_name))) }
.lv_neu <- "Neuronal lineage (C3->C2)"; .lv_gli <- "Glial lineage (C3->C1)"; .lv_spl <- "Splicing lineage (C3->C4)"
df_cross <- rbind(
  .xpanel(setNames(.Px[, .neux], rownames(.Px)), .lv_neu, c("Cycling","Immature_neurons","Pan_neuronal")),
  .xpanel(setNames(.Px[, .glix], rownames(.Px)), .lv_gli, c("Cycling","Astrocyte")),
  .xpanel(setNames(.Px[, .spx],  rownames(.Px)), .lv_spl, c("Cycling","Splicing")))
df_cross$module  <- factor(df_cross$module,  levels = c("Cycling","Immature_neurons","Pan_neuronal","Astrocyte","Splicing"))
df_cross$lineage <- factor(df_cross$lineage, levels = c(.lv_neu, .lv_gli, .lv_spl))
p_cross <- ggplot(df_cross, aes(Pseudotime, signal, colour = module)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, size = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  facet_wrap(~ lineage, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Cycling = "#6A51A3", Immature_neurons = "#EC7014",
                                 Pan_neuronal = "#B2182B", Astrocyte = "#238B45",
                                 Splicing = "#08519C"), name = "marker module") +
  labs(y = "relative abundance (centred log2)",
       title = "Per-lineage marker-module crossover: cycling-exit, then neuronal / astrocyte / splicing accumulation") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10.5))
print(p_cross); save_fig(p_cross, "S10_marker_crossover.png", w = 15, h = 5)
saveRDS(sceTraj, file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$obj, "sce_trajectory.rds"))
```

## 10.2.1 Trajectory curves on the embedding

<!-- slingshot principal curve(s) overlaid on the compPCA fitting space — where the
     curve is defined and traces smoothly (embedCurves onto UMAP tangles it at this
     n). Coloured by the trajectory's clusters and by pseudotime; per-lineage panels
     are added when >1 lineage (here 3: neuronal C3->C2, glial C3->C1 and splicing C3->C4
     off the C3 root). -->

```{r traj-curves, fig.width=8, fig.height=6.5}
sling_pseudo <- slingPseudotime(sceTraj); n_lin <- ncol(sling_pseudo)
lin <- slingLineages(sceTraj)
for (i in seq_len(n_lin)) {
  colData(sceTraj)[[paste0("Pseudotime_L", i)]] <- sling_pseudo[, i]
  cat(sprintf("Lineage %d: %s (%d cells)\n", i, paste(lin[[i]], collapse = " -> "),
              sum(!is.na(sling_pseudo[, i]))))
}
coords  <- reducedDim(sceTraj, "compPCA")[, 1:2]
curves  <- slingCurves(sceTraj)
plot_df <- data.frame(X = coords[, 1], Y = coords[, 2],
                      Cluster = factor(colLabels(sceTraj)), Pseudotime = sceTraj$Pseudotime)
for (i in seq_len(n_lin)) plot_df[[paste0("PT_L", i)]] <- sling_pseudo[, i]
all_curves <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(curves), function(i) {
  s <- curves[[i]]$s[curves[[i]]$ord, 1:2]
  data.frame(x = s[, 1], y = s[, 2], Lineage = paste0("L", i)) }))

p_tc <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(X, Y)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = Cluster), size = 2, alpha = 0.75) +
  geom_path(data = all_curves, aes(x, y, group = Lineage), linewidth = 1.2, colour = "black") +
  labs(x = "compPCA PC1", y = "compPCA PC2", title = "Trajectory — clusters") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
print(p_tc); save_fig(p_tc, "S10_trajectory_clusters.png", 8, 6.5)

pt_plot <- function(col, title, lin_id = NULL) {
  ok <- plot_df[!is.na(plot_df[[col]]), ]; na <- plot_df[is.na(plot_df[[col]]), ]
  ## per-lineage panel draws ONLY its own principal curve; global draws all
  crv <- if (is.null(lin_id)) all_curves else all_curves[all_curves$Lineage == paste0("L", lin_id), ]
  ggplot(plot_df, aes(X, Y)) +
    geom_point(data = na, size = 1.5, colour = "grey85", alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_point(data = ok, aes(colour = .data[[col]]), size = 2, alpha = 0.85) +
    scale_colour_viridis_c(option = "inferno", name = "Pseudotime") +
    geom_path(data = crv, aes(x, y, group = Lineage), linewidth = 1, colour = "grey30") +
    labs(x = "compPCA PC1", y = "compPCA PC2", title = title) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
}
pt_list <- list(pt_plot("Pseudotime", "Global pseudotime"))
if (n_lin > 1) for (i in seq_len(n_lin))
  pt_list[[length(pt_list) + 1]] <- pt_plot(paste0("PT_L", i), sprintf("Lineage %d", i), lin_id = i)
p_ptraj <- patchwork::wrap_plots(pt_list, ncol = min(3, length(pt_list)))
print(p_ptraj)
save_fig(p_ptraj, "S10_pseudotime_trajectory.png",
         w = 6 * min(3, length(pt_list)), h = 5.5 * ceiling(length(pt_list) / 3))
```

## 10.2.1b Trajectory on the UMAP (embedded curves)

<!-- The same slingshot principal curves EMBEDDED onto the UMAP via embedCurves(), as a
     familiar 2-D companion to the compPCA view above. The curves are FIT in compPCA (where
     Euclidean distances are meaningful); embedCurves projects them into UMAP space. At n=131
     they trace cleanly and show the C3-rooted trifurcation (neuronal C3->C2, glial C3->C1,
     splicing C3->C4); compPCA (10.2.1) remains the space where the curves are defined. -->

```{r traj-curves-umap, fig.width=13, fig.height=10}
.embU <- slingshot::embedCurves(sceTraj, "UMAP"); .ecU <- slingCurves(.embU)
.umU  <- as.data.frame(reducedDim(sceTraj, "UMAP"))[, 1:2]; colnames(.umU) <- c("UMAP1", "UMAP2")
.umU$Cluster <- factor(colLabels(sceTraj)); .umU$Pseudotime <- sceTraj$Pseudotime
.LU <- slingLineages(sceTraj); .PU <- slingPseudotime(sceTraj)
.linU <- vapply(.LU, function(x) { .t <- tail(x, 1)
                if (.t == "2") "L1 neuronal (C3->C2)" else if (.t == "1") "L2 glial (C3->C1)"
                else if (.t == "4") "L3 splicing (C3->C4)" else paste(x, collapse = "-") }, "")
for (i in seq_along(.LU)) .umU[[paste0("PT_L", i)]] <- .PU[, i]
.crvU <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(.ecU), function(i) {
  s <- .ecU[[i]]$s[.ecU[[i]]$ord, 1:2]; data.frame(x = s[, 1], y = s[, 2], Lineage = .linU[i]) }))
.labU <- c("1" = "C1 astroglial", "2" = "C2 neuron", "3" = "C3 progenitor", "4" = "C4 splicing")

p_tcU <- ggplot(.umU, aes(UMAP1, UMAP2)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = Cluster), size = 2.4, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_path(data = .crvU, aes(x, y, group = Lineage, linetype = Lineage), linewidth = 1.1, colour = "black") +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2", labels = .labU) +
  labs(title = "Trajectory on UMAP — clusters + embedded lineage curves") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12))

.ptU <- function(col, ttl, lid = NULL) {
  ok <- .umU[!is.na(.umU[[col]]), ]; na <- .umU[is.na(.umU[[col]]), ]
  cc <- if (is.null(lid)) .crvU else .crvU[.crvU$Lineage == .linU[lid], ]
  ggplot(.umU, aes(UMAP1, UMAP2)) +
    geom_point(data = na, size = 1.4, colour = "grey85", alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_point(data = ok, aes(colour = .data[[col]]), size = 2, alpha = 0.85) +
    scale_colour_viridis_c(option = "inferno", name = "pseudotime") +
    geom_path(data = cc, aes(x, y, group = Lineage), linewidth = 1, colour = "grey20") +
    labs(title = ttl) + theme_bw(base_size = 11) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
}
.panU <- list(.ptU("Pseudotime", "Global (mean)"))
for (i in seq_along(.LU)) .panU[[length(.panU) + 1]] <- .ptU(paste0("PT_L", i), .linU[i], lid = i)
p_ptrajU <- patchwork::wrap_plots(.panU, nrow = 1)
print(p_tcU / p_ptrajU + patchwork::plot_layout(heights = c(1, 0.9)))
save_fig(p_tcU, "S10_UMAP_trajectory_clusters.png", 9, 6.5)
save_fig(p_ptrajU, "S10_UMAP_pseudotime_trajectory.png", w = 6 * length(.panU), h = 5)
```

## 10.2.2 Where each cluster sits along pseudotime

Mapping the clusters onto the trajectory confirms the ordering and, crucially, that
**depth is decoupled from pseudotime** (so the trajectory is not a technical/quality
artifact). The trajectory **trifurcates at the cycling C3 progenitor** (root) into a
**neuronal lineage (C3 → C2)**, a **glial / astroglial lineage (C3 → C1)** and a distinct
**splicing / RNA-processing lineage (C3 → C4)** — neurogenesis and gliogenesis running in
parallel, plus a small post-mitotic splicing state, in this 7.5-month organoid. **C1 is
therefore a late glial *endpoint*, not the early progenitor**: it carries astrocyte
markers (ALDOC, CLU, S100B, GFAP, AQP4), the lowest cycling-module abundance, and one of
the highest pseudotimes — so its oxidative/metabolic-enzyme load is an *astrocyte*
feature, not a progenitor one. (An earlier single-lineage fit that re-clustered internally
and rooted on SOX2/NES placed C1 early; using the validated C1–C4 clusters and a
cycling-specific root corrects this to the trifurcation.)

**Why C4 is its own branch, not the neuronal tip.** C4 is a small (n≈10),
**non-proliferating** cluster defined by peak spliceosome / RNA-processing machinery
(SF3B1/3, SNRPB2, SRSF7, RBM12, NOLC1, PTBP2) — *not* by neuronal maturity: every
neuronal-identity marker (DCX, CRMP1, STMN1, TUBB3, MAP2, DPYSL3) is **lower** in C4 than
in the mature C2 neurons. Left unconstrained at full npc=15, slingshot hangs C4 off the
neuronal tip (C3 → C2 → C4), which incorrectly reads C4 as the *most mature* neuron and
flattens the neuronal-maturation gradient (module rho +0.56). Declaring the three
differentiated states (C1/C2/C4) as terminal fates gives C4 its **own** C3 → C4 branch and
restores a clean C3 → C2 neuronal gradient (rho **+0.91**). This is not an artefact of the
prior: the **unforced npc = 5 fit splits C4 off spontaneously** with the same cleanup
(§10.1.1), so the terminal-fate model recovers real structure at full resolution.

```{r cluster-position, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.2}
.pt  <- setNames(sceTraj$Pseudotime, colnames(sceTraj))
.cd  <- as.data.frame(colData(scp))                    # flatten QFeatures colData (Cluster is a CompressedList)
.s7  <- setNames(as.character(.cd$Cluster), rownames(.cd))
.cm  <- intersect(names(.pt), names(.s7))
.lab <- c("1" = "C1 astroglial", "2" = "C2 neuron", "3" = "C3 progenitor (root)", "4" = "C4 splicing")
.df  <- data.frame(pt = as.numeric(.pt[.cm]), lab = factor(.lab[.s7[.cm]], levels = .lab))
cat("median pseudotime per cluster (root = progenitor):\n")
print(aggregate(pt ~ lab, .df, function(x) round(median(x), 1)), row.names = FALSE)
.kw  <- kruskal.test(pt ~ lab, .df)$p.value
.dp  <- setNames(as.numeric(comp$cd$log_sumsRI_NoCRAP), rownames(comp$cd))
.rd  <- cor(.pt[.cm], .dp[.cm], method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")
cat(sprintf("Kruskal-Wallis (pseudotime ~ cluster) p = %.1e | depth (log_sumsRI_NoCRAP) vs pseudotime rho = %+.2f (decoupled)\n", .kw, .rd))
p_cp <- ggplot(.df, aes(lab, pt, fill = lab)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.85, outlier.size = 0.5) + geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 0.6, alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Pseudotime (root = progenitor)", title = "Cluster positions along the trajectory") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(legend.position = "none", plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1))
print(p_cp); save_fig(p_cp, "S10_cluster_position.png", 7, 4.2)

## pseudotime distribution: shows the continuous ranking (no early/late cutoff) and
## the sparse root gap — a few cycling-high, highest-coverage C3 progenitors at pt~0
## sit isolated from the main body (see 10.5 for the robustness consequence).
.md <- aggregate(pt ~ lab, .df, median)
.sp <- sort(.df$pt); .gp <- c(.sp[which.max(diff(.sp))], .sp[which.max(diff(.sp)) + 1])
p_pd <- ggplot(.df, aes(pt)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = .gp[1], xmax = .gp[2], ymin = 0, ymax = Inf, fill = "grey80", alpha = 0.35) +
  geom_histogram(aes(fill = lab), bins = 28, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_rug(aes(colour = lab), sides = "b", alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(data = .md, aes(xintercept = pt, colour = lab), linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.7, show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Pseudotime (arc-length from cycling-progenitor root — continuous, arbitrary units)", y = "cells",
       fill = NULL, colour = NULL,
       title = sprintf("Pseudotime = a continuous ranking, no early/late cutoff (grey = sparse gap %.0f-%.0f: 3 root cells vs body)", .gp[1], .gp[2])) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9.5), legend.position = "right")
print(p_pd); save_fig(p_pd, "S10_pseudotime_distribution.png", 9, 4.2)
```

## 10.3 Sensitivity to drop threshold
<!-- Sweep 0-50% drop; show the TRIFURCATION (C3 root -> neuronal C2 / glial C1 / splicing C4)
     and all three per-lineage marker programs (neuron up on the neuronal lineage; astrocyte up
     on the glial lineage; spliceosome up on the C4 lineage) are stable across drop thresholds. -->

```{r traj-sensitivity, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
## Re-fit the trajectory across drop thresholds; track the TRIFURCATION (n lineages, root,
## presence of the glial-C1 / neuronal-C2 / splicing-C4 branches) and the per-lineage marker
## directions. Expect: neuronal neuron-up / prog-down; glial astrocyte-up / neuron-down;
## splicing spliceosome-up. (fit_trajectory forces the three terminal fates, so each drop level
## is the adopted 3-lineage model; end clusters absent at a given drop are dropped automatically.)
fracs <- c(0, 0.10, 0.20, 0.30, 0.40, 0.50)
rho_module <- function(res, pt, genes) {
  g <- intersect(genes, rownames(res)); if (!length(g) || all(is.na(pt))) return(NA_real_)
  s <- colMeans(res[g, , drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)
  suppressWarnings(cor(pt, s, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"))
}
.ast_mk <- c("GLUD1", "ALDOC", "CLU", "HADHA", "ALDH6A1")               # astrocyte / astro-metabolic
.spl_mk <- c("PTBP2", "SF3B1", "SF3B3", "SNRPB2", "SRSF7", "RBM12", "NOLC1")  # spliceosome / RNA-processing (C4)
sens <- do.call(rbind, lapply(fracs, function(fr) {
  cmp <- build_compositional(pg_all, cd_all, drop_fraction = fr)
  st  <- tryCatch(fit_trajectory(cmp), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(st)) return(NULL)
  L <- slingLineages(st); P <- slingPseudotime(st); rownames(P) <- colnames(st)
  neu <- which(vapply(L, function(x) tail(x, 1) == "2", TRUE)); gli <- which(vapply(L, function(x) tail(x, 1) == "1", TRUE))
  spl <- which(vapply(L, function(x) tail(x, 1) == "4", TRUE))
  npt <- if (length(neu)) setNames(P[, neu[1]], rownames(P)) else NA_real_
  gpt <- if (length(gli)) setNames(P[, gli[1]], rownames(P)) else NA_real_
  spt <- if (length(spl)) setNames(P[, spl[1]], rownames(P)) else NA_real_
  data.frame(drop = fr, n_cells = ncol(cmp$res), n_lineages = length(L), root = paste0("C", L[[1]][1]),
             glial_C1 = length(gli) > 0, neuronal_C2 = length(neu) > 0, splicing_C4 = length(spl) > 0,
             neu_lin_neuron = rho_module(cmp$res, npt, marker_sets$Immature_neurons),
             neu_lin_prog   = rho_module(cmp$res, npt, marker_sets$Neural_progenitors),
             gli_lin_astro  = rho_module(cmp$res, gpt, .ast_mk),
             gli_lin_neuron = rho_module(cmp$res, gpt, marker_sets$Immature_neurons),
             spl_lin_splice = rho_module(cmp$res, spt, .spl_mk))
}))
print(sens); save_tab(sens, "S10_sensitivity.csv")

p_sens <- sens |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(neu_lin_neuron, neu_lin_prog, gli_lin_astro, gli_lin_neuron, spl_lin_splice),
                      names_to = "track", values_to = "rho") |>
  ggplot(aes(drop * 100, rho, colour = track)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(neu_lin_neuron = "#B2182B", neu_lin_prog = "#F4A582",
                                 gli_lin_astro = "#2166AC", gli_lin_neuron = "#92C5DE",
                                 spl_lin_splice = "#08519C"),
                      labels = c(neu_lin_neuron = "neuronal lineage: neuron", neu_lin_prog = "neuronal lineage: progenitor",
                                 gli_lin_astro = "glial lineage: astrocyte", gli_lin_neuron = "glial lineage: neuron",
                                 spl_lin_splice = "splicing lineage: spliceosome")) +
  labs(x = "% lowest-quality cells dropped", y = "marker-module rho vs per-lineage pseudotime",
       colour = NULL, title = "Trifurcation stability across drop thresholds (all three lineages)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) + theme(legend.position = "right")
print(p_sens); save_fig(p_sens, "S10_sensitivity.png", w = 9, h = 5)

## npc corroboration (#4): the adopted 3-lineage model (forced terminal fates, npc=15) is
## CORROBORATED by an UNFORCED fit (end_clusters = NULL). Refit unforced at npc 5/10/15 and
## report whether C4 splits off spontaneously: the C3->C4 branch appears unforced ONLY at npc=5
## (matching the adopted model), while npc 10-15 leave C4 at the neuronal tip (C3->C2->C4). So
## the terminal-fate prior recovers, at full resolution, structure that is otherwise visible
## only at the npc=5 island (full 3..15 sweep + cleanup rho in 10.1.1). Root stays C3 throughout.
npc_rob <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(5, 10, 15), function(np) {
  st  <- fit_trajectory(comp, npc = np, end_clusters = NULL)          # UNFORCED
  L <- slingLineages(st); ord <- tapply(st$Pseudotime, factor(comp$cd$Cluster), median, na.rm = TRUE)
  c4_split <- any(vapply(L, function(x) tail(x, 1) == "4" && length(x) == 2, TRUE))
  data.frame(npc = np, n_lineages = length(L),
             lineages = paste(vapply(L, function(x) paste0("C", x, collapse = ">"), ""), collapse = " | "),
             C4_own_branch = c4_split, root = paste0("C", names(which.min(ord))),
             C1 = round(ord["1"], 1), C2 = round(ord["2"], 1),
             C3 = round(ord["3"], 1), C4 = round(ord["4"], 1), row.names = NULL)
}))
cat("\nnpc corroboration — UNFORCED fit (C4 splits off spontaneously only at npc=5; median pseudotime per cluster):\n")
print(npc_rob, row.names = FALSE)
save_tab(npc_rob, "S10_npc_robustness.csv")
```

## 10.4 Driver proteins + GO enrichment
<!-- Per-protein association along pseudotime on the compositional residuals,
     via mgcv GAUSSIAN GAMs (NOT tradeSeq's negative-binomial GAMs, which are for
     counts). GO BP enrichment with the detected proteome as background. (CR3/CR4) -->

```{r traj-drivers, fig.width=9, fig.height=6}
## Drivers along the NEURONAL lineage (C3 -> C2). Because the trajectory trifurcates, the mean
## pseudotime mixes the neuronal, glial and splicing fates and cancels opposing signals, so the
## GAM is run on the neuronal-lineage pseudotime only (glial and splicing fates: per-lineage in 10.5).
.Ln  <- slingLineages(sceTraj); .neu <- which(vapply(.Ln, function(x) tail(x, 1) == "2", TRUE))[1]
ptv  <- setNames(slingPseudotime(sceTraj)[, .neu], colnames(sceTraj)); ptv <- ptv[is.finite(ptv)]
tz   <- (ptv - min(ptv)) / diff(range(ptv))
resT <- comp$res[, names(ptv), drop = FALSE]       # proteins x neuronal-lineage cells

driver_one <- function(g) {
  y <- resT[g, ]; ok <- !is.na(y)
  if (sum(ok) < 40 || sd(y[ok]) == 0) return(NULL)
  fit <- tryCatch(mgcv::gam(y ~ s(t, k = TRAJ$spline_df + 1),
                            data = data.frame(y = y[ok], t = tz[ok])),
                  error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(fit)) return(NULL)
  fv <- predict(fit, data.frame(t = seq(0, 1, length.out = 50)))
  data.frame(protein = g, p = summary(fit)$s.table[1, "p-value"],
             swing = diff(range(fv)),
             direction = ifelse(tail(fv, 1) >= fv[1], "up", "down"))
}
drivers <- do.call(rbind, lapply(rownames(resT), driver_one))
drivers$FDR <- p.adjust(drivers$p, "BH")
drivers <- drivers[order(drivers$FDR), ]
sig <- subset(drivers, FDR < 0.05 & swing >= 0.5)
cat(sprintf("Drivers FDR<0.05 & swing>=0.5: %d (up=%d, down=%d)\n",
            nrow(sig), sum(sig$direction == "up"), sum(sig$direction == "down")))
save_tab(drivers, "S10_drivers.csv")

## GO BP enrichment (first gene symbol per protein group; detected = background)
first_sym  <- function(x) sub(";.*", "", x)
up_genes   <- unique(first_sym(sig$protein[sig$direction == "up"]))
down_genes <- unique(first_sym(sig$protein[sig$direction == "down"]))
bg_genes   <- unique(first_sym(rownames(resT)))

go_up <- enrichGO(up_genes,   OrgDb = org.Hs.eg.db, keyType = "SYMBOL", ont = "BP",
                  universe = bg_genes, pAdjustMethod = "BH", qvalueCutoff = 0.1)
go_dn <- enrichGO(down_genes, OrgDb = org.Hs.eg.db, keyType = "SYMBOL", ont = "BP",
                  universe = bg_genes, pAdjustMethod = "BH", qvalueCutoff = 0.1)
if (!is.null(go_up) && nrow(as.data.frame(go_up))) {
  print(dotplot(go_up, showCategory = 12) + ggtitle("UP drivers — toward neurons"))
  save_tab(as.data.frame(go_up), "S10_GO_up.csv") }
if (!is.null(go_dn) && nrow(as.data.frame(go_dn))) {
  print(dotplot(go_dn, showCategory = 12) + ggtitle("DOWN drivers — toward neurons"))
  save_tab(as.data.frame(go_dn), "S10_GO_down.csv") }
```

## 10.5 Absolute-abundance drivers — per lineage (neuronal / glial / splicing fate)

<!-- Genome-wide per-protein Spearman association with per-LINEAGE pseudotime on TRUE
     non-normalised abundance (Protein.Group_abund = peptides_log_noNorm aggregated by gene, S4).
     Computed separately for the neuronal (C3->C2), glial (C3->C1) and splicing (C3->C4) lineages,
     because the trifurcation makes the mean pseudotime cancel opposing signals. Depth is decoupled
     from pseudotime (10.2.2), so these are not a depth artifact. -->

```{r traj-validate, fig.width=11, fig.height=6.5}
## Per-LINEAGE absolute-abundance drivers (Protein.Group_abund = true non-normalised log2).
## The trajectory trifurcates, so drivers are computed SEPARATELY for each lineage: averaging the
## fates into one pseudotime cancels opposing signals (e.g. GLUD1 falls toward neurons but rises
## toward astrocytes). L1 = neuronal (C3->C2), L2 = glial (C3->C1), L3 = splicing (C3->C4).
A <- as.matrix(assay(scp[["Protein.Group_abund"]]))                       # TRUE non-normalised log2
.Ln <- slingLineages(sceTraj); .P <- slingPseudotime(sceTraj); rownames(.P) <- colnames(sceTraj)
lin_lab <- vapply(.Ln, function(x) { .t <- tail(x, 1)
                  if (.t == "2") "neuronal (C3->C2)" else if (.t == "1") "glial (C3->C1)"
                  else if (.t == "4") "splicing (C3->C4)" else paste(x, collapse = "-") }, "")
abs_drivers <- function(ptv) {
  cells <- names(ptv)[is.finite(ptv)]; Ai <- A[, cells, drop = FALSE]; Ai <- Ai[rowSums(!is.na(Ai)) >= 20, , drop = FALSE]
  d <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(Ai)), function(i) { y <- Ai[i, ]; o <- !is.na(y)
    if (sum(o) < 20) return(NULL); ct <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(y[o], ptv[cells][o], method = "spearman"))
    data.frame(gene = rownames(Ai)[i], rho = unname(ct$estimate), p = ct$p.value) }))
  d$FDR <- p.adjust(d$p, "BH"); d
}
drv <- setNames(lapply(seq_len(ncol(.P)), function(i) abs_drivers(setNames(.P[, i], rownames(.P)))), lin_lab)
for (i in seq_along(drv)) { nm <- names(drv)[i]; d <- drv[[i]]
  dn <- sum(d$rho < 0 & d$FDR < 0.05); up <- sum(d$rho > 0 & d$FDR < 0.05)
  cat(sprintf("Lineage %-22s (%d cells): absolute drivers DOWN=%d UP=%d (%.1fx)\n",
              nm, sum(is.finite(.P[, i])), dn, up, dn / max(up, 1)))
  .tag <- if (grepl("neuronal", nm)) "neuronal" else if (grepl("glial", nm)) "glial" else "splicing"
  save_tab(d[order(d$rho), ], sprintf("S10_drivers_absolute_%s.csv", .tag)) }

## multi-fate volcano — the same metabolic enzymes move OPPOSITE ways in the neuronal vs glial
## fates; the splicing fate (C3->C4) is driven up by the spliceosome / RNA-processing program
volc <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(drv), function(nm) { d <- drv[[nm]]; d$lineage <- nm; d }))
.lg <- c("DCX","STMN1","CRMP1","DPYSL3","TUBB3","MAP2","MAP1B","RTN1",
         "GLUD1","HADHA","HADHB","ALDH6A1","PHGDH","DECR1","ALDOC","CLU","S100B","VIM","FABP7",
         "PTBP2","SF3B1","SF3B3","SNRPB2","SRSF7","RBM12","NOLC1")
volc$dir <- ifelse(volc$FDR < 0.05 & volc$rho < 0, "down", ifelse(volc$FDR < 0.05 & volc$rho > 0, "up", "n.s."))
## label BOTH the curated markers AND, per fate, the 5 strongest UP and 5 strongest DOWN drivers
## (largest |rho| among FDR<0.05); the data-driven top hits are drawn in bold to set them apart.
volc$top <- FALSE
for (nm in unique(volc$lineage)) {
  ix <- which(volc$lineage == nm & volc$FDR < 0.05)
  up <- ix[volc$rho[ix] > 0]; up <- up[order(-volc$rho[up])][seq_len(min(5, length(up)))]
  dn <- ix[volc$rho[ix] < 0]; dn <- dn[order( volc$rho[dn])][seq_len(min(5, length(dn)))]
  volc$top[c(up, dn)] <- TRUE
}
volc$lab   <- ifelse(volc$gene %in% .lg | volc$top, volc$gene, "")
volc$fface <- ifelse(volc$top, "bold", "plain")
p_v <- ggplot(volc, aes(rho, -log10(pmax(FDR, 1e-16)), colour = dir)) +
  geom_point(size = 1.1, alpha = 0.7) + facet_wrap(~ lineage) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(down = "#2166AC", up = "#B2182B", n.s. = "grey80")) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = lab, fontface = fface), size = 2.5, max.overlaps = Inf,
                           min.segment.length = 0, segment.size = 0.2, segment.colour = "grey65", show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  labs(x = "Spearman rho vs per-lineage pseudotime (absolute abundance)", y = "-log10 FDR", colour = NULL,
       title = "Per-lineage absolute drivers: neuronal / glial / splicing fate (bold = top-5 up/down per fate)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), legend.position = "top")
print(p_v); save_fig(p_v, "S10_absolute_volcano.png", 13, 6)

## GO:BP of each lineage's UP program (detected proteome = background)
.ss <- function(v) unique(unlist(strsplit(v, ";", fixed = TRUE))); .u <- .ss(volc$gene)
for (nm in names(drv)) { d <- drv[[nm]]; upg <- .ss(d$gene[d$rho > 0 & d$FDR < 0.05])
  g <- tryCatch(enrichGO(upg, org.Hs.eg.db, keyType = "SYMBOL", ont = "BP", universe = .u, qvalueCutoff = 0.1), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(g) && nrow(as.data.frame(g))) {
    print(dotplot(g, showCategory = 10) + ggtitle(sprintf("UP toward the %s endpoint", nm)))
    .gtag <- if (grepl("neuronal", nm)) "neuronal" else if (grepl("glial", nm)) "glial" else "splicing"
    save_tab(as.data.frame(g), sprintf("S10_GO_up_%s.csv", .gtag)) } }
rm(A); invisible(gc())
```

The three fates carry **distinct** absolute-abundance programs, which is why they must be read
per lineage — averaging them cancels the signal. Along the **neuronal lineage (C3 → C2)** a
high-confidence **neuronal-identity** program accumulates (CRMP1 +0.84, MAP1B +0.83, DCX +0.72,
DPYSL3 +0.62, TUBB3 / STMN1 +0.49) while **biosynthetic** machinery (ribosome biogenesis,
translation) and **mitochondrial / metabolic** enzymes (fatty-acid β-oxidation and amino-acid
catabolism — PHGDH −0.74, ALDH6A1 −0.63, GLUD1 −0.50, HADHA −0.40) fall as cells exit the cycle
— the cell-cycle-exit + biosynthetic-shutdown signature (Chau 2018; Telley 2019) at the protein
level. (Splitting C4 off *sharpens* this program: CRMP1 / MAP1B / DCX rise from ~+0.6 on the old
C3→C2→C4 lineage to ~+0.8 on the clean C3→C2 gradient.) Along the **glial lineage (C3 → C1)** the
*same* metabolic enzymes move the **other way** — GLUD1 +0.74, HADHA +0.73, ALDH6A1 +0.65, PHGDH
+0.54 — together with astrocyte markers (VIM +0.44, S100B +0.49, ALDOC) **accumulating toward the
astrocyte endpoint**, while neuronal markers fall (STMN1 −0.71, DCX −0.43). So the
oxidative/metabolic load is an **astrocyte feature of the gliogenic branch**, not a progenitor
feature (the earlier single-lineage reading): rising glutamate metabolism (GLUD1) toward
astrocytes is textbook astroglial biology. The **splicing lineage (C3 → C4)** is dominated in
absolute terms by **cell-cycle exit** (replication machinery down: PCNA −0.78, MCM6 −0.77, RRM1
−0.75, NASP −0.71) toward a small post-mitotic state that gains **synaptic / axonal** proteins
(UCHL1 +0.73, RAB3A +0.64, STXBP1 +0.58, GAP43, ELAVL3); its *defining* **spliceosome /
RNA-processing** signature (PTBP2, SF3B1/3, SNRPB2, SRSF7) is **compositional** — it stands out
after depth-regression (residual crossover, §10.2) rather than as an absolute surge — and its
immature-neuron markers (DCX, CRMP1, MAP1B) stay **below** C2, so C4 is a **distinct post-mitotic
splicing state, not a more mature neuron** (§10.2.2). Depth is decoupled from pseudotime
(§10.2.2) and the trifurcation and all three per-lineage programs are stable across the 0–40 %
drop sweep (§10.3), so none of the fates is a technical artifact.

## 10.6 Residual-APCA biplot — pseudotime overlay

<!-- The Session-8.4 residual-APCA biplot coloured by Session-10 pseudotime. `sce`
     was freed in Session 9, so residual scores + loadings are read back from
     sce_minimal.rds; pseudotime comes from `sceTraj` (NA/grey for the cells the
     quality gate dropped before the trajectory). -->

```{r traj-biplot, fig.width=9, fig.height=6.5}
sce_min <- readRDS(file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$obj, "sce_minimal.rds"))
rd_res  <- as.matrix(reducedDim(sce_min, "residuals"))
bp_df   <- data.frame(PC1 = rd_res[, 1], PC2 = rd_res[, 2], cell = colnames(sce_min))
bp_df$Pseudotime <- sceTraj$Pseudotime[match(bp_df$cell, colnames(sceTraj))]   # NA = dropped

## loadings stored in Session 6.1 (fallback: recompute if absent)
lo <- metadata(sce_min)$apca_loadings
if (is.null(lo)) {
  caR <- scpComponentAnalysis(sce_min, ncomp = 10, method = "APCA")
  lo  <- data.frame(caR$byFeature[["residuals"]])
  lo$Genes <- rowData(sce_min)$Genes[match(lo$feature, rowData(sce_min)$Stripped.Sequence)]
}
lo <- lo[!is.na(lo$Genes) & lo$Genes != "", ]
lo$importance <- sqrt(lo$PC1^2 + lo$PC2^2)
lo <- lo[order(lo$importance, decreasing = TRUE), ]
top_peps <- head(lo[!duplicated(lo$Genes), ], 10)

sf  <- max(abs(c(bp_df$PC1, bp_df$PC2))) /
       max(abs(c(top_peps$PC1, top_peps$PC2))) * 0.6
pcv <- apply(rd_res, 2, var); pct <- 100 * pcv / sum(pcv)

p_ptbi <- ggplot(bp_df, aes(PC1, PC2)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = Pseudotime), size = 2.6, alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(na.value = "grey85") +
  geom_segment(data = top_peps, aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = PC1 * sf, yend = PC2 * sf),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm"), type = "closed"),
               linewidth = 0.4, colour = "grey30") +
  geom_text_repel(data = top_peps, aes(x = PC1 * sf, y = PC2 * sf, label = Genes),
                  inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 4.5, colour = "grey20",
                  max.overlaps = 20, box.padding = 0.5, segment.size = 0.3) +
  labs(x = sprintf("PC1 (%.1f%% of captured var)", pct[1]),
       y = sprintf("PC2 (%.1f%% of captured var)", pct[2]),
       title = "Residual APCA — pseudotime overlay (grey = dropped before trajectory)",
       colour = "Pseudotime") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 15) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
print(p_ptbi); save_fig(p_ptbi, "S10_biplot_residualAPCA_pseudotime.png", 9, 6.5)
```
