# Session 11 — Functional protein covariation (Leduc et al. 2022) ⭐

Leduc *et al.* (Genome Biol 2022, nPOP) infer protein function without imputation
by correlating protein levels **across single cells**: proteins that covary tend to
be functionally coupled ("guilt-by-association"). Their pipeline is specific —
Pearson on **observed values only**, per-protein-normalised log2, restricted to
**well-detected** proteins, computed **within a cell state**, and gated by
**split-half reproducibility** (correlation matrices from two disjoint halves of the
cells must agree at ρ > 0.8). This session tests those implementations on our data
and is explicit about where our regime (n = 131 cells vs their ~1,490; ~75 %
missingness; a single progenitor→neuron continuum) does and does not support them.

Two design choices follow the primary literature. **(i)** Covariation is computed on
the non-imputed, per-protein-referenced `Protein.Group` values (Session 6) — never the
imputed Appendix-A matrix (imputation fabricates covariation). (Pearson centres each
protein internally, so the exact per-protein offset is immaterial; note the observed
row-means are not exactly zero — they sit near −0.4 — because missingness is
not-at-random.) **(ii)** Because `scplainer` *models* the per-cell loading term
the loading term rather than dividing it out, these values still carry a per-cell loading
axis (the per-cell mean of observed values correlates with `log_sumsRI_NoCRAP` at r ≈ −0.90);
Leduc normalise that away before correlating. We therefore report covariation **raw**,
then after regressing out `log_sumsRI_NoCRAP` (the contaminant-free loading — the
`scplainer`-equivalent normalisation step, and a better de-confounder than the raw total),
then additionally the trajectory (compPCA PC1) — the "within-state" view that Khan
*et al.* (2024, EMT continuum) show is the correct treatment for a developmental
trajectory.

## 11.1 Global covariation, the baseline confound, and reproducibility

```{r covariation-core, fig.width=9, fig.height=8, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(SingleCellExperiment); library(ggplot2)})
.s11 <- file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$obj, "S11_covariation.rds")

mat <- as.matrix(assay(scp[["Protein.Group"]]))          # non-imputed, per-protein referenced log2
det <- rowMeans(!is.na(mat))
M   <- mat[det >= 0.5, ]                                  # well-detected proteins

## remove the linear effect of covariate(s) X from every protein's OBSERVED values
regress_out <- function(Mx, X) { R <- Mx
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(Mx))) { y <- Mx[i, ]; ok <- is.finite(y)
    if (sum(ok) < 8) { R[i, ] <- NA; next }
    R[i, ok] <- residuals(lm(y[ok] ~ X[ok, , drop = FALSE])) }; R }

complexes <- list(
  Ribosome    = grep("^RP[LS][0-9]", rownames(M), value = TRUE),
  Proteasome  = grep("^PSM[ABCDEF][0-9]", rownames(M), value = TRUE),
  Chaperonin  = grep("^CCT[0-9]|^TCP1$", rownames(M), value = TRUE),
  OXPHOS      = grep("^NDUF|^UQCR|^COX[0-9]|^SDH[ABCD]$|^ATP5", rownames(M), value = TRUE),
  Spliceosome = grep("^SNRP|^SF3[AB]|^SRSF|^PRPF|^HNRNP", rownames(M), value = TRUE))
glyc <- intersect(c("HK1","HK2","GPI","PFKL","PFKM","PFKP","ALDOA","ALDOC","TPI1",
                    "GAPDH","PGK1","PGAM1","ENO1","ENO2","PKM","LDHA","LDHB"), rownames(M))
mean_within <- function(C, gs){ gs <- intersect(gs, rownames(C)); if (length(gs) < 4) return(NA)
  s <- C[gs, gs]; mean(s[upper.tri(s)], na.rm = TRUE) }

if (file.exists(.s11)) {
  S11 <- readRDS(.s11)
} else {
  set.seed(101)
  ## covariates for the "peel" (only needed when recomputing). NB `sce` is rm()'d in
  ## Session 9 to free memory, so read compPCA from the S6 cache (sce_min, 131 cells).
  lrs <- as.data.frame(colData(scp))[colnames(M), "log_sumsRI_NoCRAP"]        # per-cell loading (contaminant-free)
  if (!exists("sce_min")) sce_min <- readRDS(file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$obj, "sce_minimal.rds"))
  pc1 <- reducedDim(sce_min, "compPCA")[colnames(M), 1]                       # dominant biological axis (trajectory)
  C0 <- cor(t(M), use = "pairwise.complete.obs")                              # raw
  Ci <- cor(t(regress_out(M, cbind(lrs))),        use = "pairwise.complete.obs")   # -log_sumsRI
  Ct <- cor(t(regress_out(M, cbind(lrs, pc1))),   use = "pairwise.complete.obs")   # -log_sumsRI -PC1
  ## split-half reproducibility of the (raw and technically-cleaned) correlation matrices
  reprod <- function(X) sapply(1:8, function(s){ set.seed(s); h <- sample(ncol(X), floor(ncol(X)/2))
    a <- cor(t(X[, h]), use = "pairwise.complete.obs"); b <- cor(t(X[, -h]), use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
    ut <- upper.tri(a); ok <- is.finite(a[ut]) & is.finite(b[ut]); cor(a[ut][ok], b[ut][ok]) })
  rr0 <- reprod(M); rri <- reprod(regress_out(M, cbind(lrs)))
  S11 <- list(C0 = C0, Ci = Ci, Ct = Ct, rr0 = rr0, rri = rri)
  saveRDS(S11, .s11)
}
C0 <- S11$C0; Ci <- S11$Ci; Ct <- S11$Ct

## --- complex covariation vs a random-set null, per pass -----------------------
set.seed(1)
null_r <- function(C, n, B = 3000) replicate(B, { g <- sample(rownames(C), n)
  s <- C[g, g]; mean(s[upper.tri(s)], na.rm = TRUE) })
tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(complexes), function(nm) {
  gs <- intersect(complexes[[nm]], rownames(M)); if (length(gs) < 4) return(NULL)
  n0 <- null_r(Ci, length(gs)); ob <- mean_within(Ci, gs)
  data.frame(Set = nm, n = length(gs),
             r_raw = round(mean_within(C0, gs), 2),
             `r_clean (-log_sumsRI)` = round(ob, 2),
             null_clean = round(mean(n0), 2),
             z = round((ob - mean(n0)) / sd(n0), 1),
             p = signif((sum(n0 >= ob) + 1) / (length(n0) + 1), 2),
             check.names = FALSE) }))
knitr::kable(tab, caption = "Complex covariation (mean within-set Pearson r) vs a size-matched random-set null, after removing the technical cell-loading axis. Every annotated complex covaries far above chance.")

cat(sprintf("Well-detected proteins (>=50%% of %d cells): %d of %d\n", ncol(mat), nrow(M), nrow(mat)))
cat(sprintf("Random-pair null mean r:  raw = %+.2f  ->  -log_sumsRI = %+.2f  ->  -log_sumsRI-PC1 = %+.2f\n",
            mean(null_r(C0, 20)), mean(null_r(Ci, 20)), mean(null_r(Ct, 20))))
cat(sprintf("Split-half reproducibility (median rho over 8 splits):  raw = %.2f | technically-cleaned = %.2f\n",
            median(S11$rr0), median(S11$rri)))
cat(sprintf("OXPHOS<->glycolysis block r:  raw = %+.2f  ->  -log_sumsRI = %+.2f  ->  -log_sumsRI-PC1 = %+.2f  (Leduc report NEGATIVE within a state)\n",
            mean(C0[intersect(complexes$OXPHOS, rownames(C0)), intersect(glyc, rownames(C0)), drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE),
            mean(Ci[intersect(complexes$OXPHOS, rownames(Ci)), intersect(glyc, rownames(Ci)), drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE),
            mean(Ct[intersect(complexes$OXPHOS, rownames(Ct)), intersect(glyc, rownames(Ct)), drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)))

## --- Fig S11a: curated functional covariation heatmap -------------------------
curated <- list(Ribosome = head(complexes$Ribosome, 8), OXPHOS = head(intersect(complexes$OXPHOS, rownames(C0)), 8),
  Glycolysis = head(glyc, 8), Neuronal = intersect(c("TUBB3","STMN2","DCX","CRMP1","MAP1B","DPYSL3"), rownames(C0)),
  Progenitor = intersect(c("SOX2","NES","VIM","FABP7","PTPRZ1"), rownames(C0)))
gsel <- unlist(curated); Csel <- C0[gsel, gsel]
hm <- data.frame(g1 = factor(rep(gsel, length(gsel)), levels = gsel),
                 g2 = factor(rep(gsel, each = length(gsel)), levels = rev(gsel)), r = as.vector(Csel))
pA <- ggplot(hm, aes(g1, g2, fill = r)) + geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B", midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1,1), name = "r") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = sprintf("Curated functional covariation (Pearson r across %d cells)", ncol(mat)),
       subtitle = "diagonal blocks = ribosome / OXPHOS / glycolysis / neuronal / progenitor; note faint neuronal↔VIM anti-correlation") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 8) + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = .5, size = 6),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6), panel.grid = element_blank(), plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
print(pA); save_fig(pA, "S11_functional_covariation_heatmap.png", 9, 8.5)
```

The result splits cleanly into a **robust positive** and a **non-reproduced** finding.

* **Complexes covary strongly and significantly** in every pass (ribosome, proteasome,
  chaperonin, OXPHOS, spliceosome all at *z* ≈ +8 to +16 above their random-set null,
  *p* < 0.001). This is **not** an artefact of complex members being better-detected:
  under a *detection-matched* null (random sets whose per-protein detection distribution
  matches each complex) the range is essentially unchanged (*z* ≈ +6.5 to +17). The
  curated heatmap shows the expected diagonal blocks, and — as a positive biological
  control — the neuronal module (TUBB3/DCX/CRMP1/DPYSL3) shows the only visible
  **negative** tiles, anti-correlating with the progenitor marker VIM along the
  differentiation axis. Guilt-by-association therefore recovers real functional structure.
* **The baseline is confounded.** Random protein pairs correlate at **+0.64** raw —
  proteins are not independent because a single per-cell axis moves them together (the
  per-cell mean of observed values tracks `log_sumsRI_NoCRAP` at r ≈ −0.90, i.e. these
  values are *not* per-cell-normalised). Removing `log_sumsRI_NoCRAP` drops the null to
  **+0.30** (over half the baseline is per-cell loading that `scplainer` models rather
  than divides out); additionally removing the trajectory PC1 barely moves it (**≈ +0.3**),
  meaning the residual floor is coverage/missingness structure, not the trajectory.
* **Individual pairwise correlations fail the paper's gate — because of power, not
  absent signal.** Split-half reproducibility is ρ ≈ 0.72 raw / 0.63 cleaned, below the
  0.8 threshold. That it is *power-limited* is demonstrable: holding the protein set
  fixed and keeping only pairs with ≥40–50 complete observations per half raises the raw
  ρ to **0.80–0.82**, and restricting to higher-detection proteins does the same
  (ρ 0.72→0.82 at ≥90 % detection) — whereas down-sampling to the same *number* of
  random proteins does not (ρ ≈ 0.70). So the *set-level* covariation is reproducible and
  strong; *pair-level* correlations are noise-limited at n = 131 (≈11× fewer cells,
  ~75 % missingness) and are not interpreted individually here.

## 11.2 Within-state covariation and the OXPHOS↔glycolysis test

Leduc's headline metabolic result — glycolytic proteins positively correlating with
each other and **inversely** with OXPHOS — was computed *within one cluster*. Khan
*et al.* (2024) make the same point for a continuum: correlations must be computed
within a state, never pooled across the trajectory. We test this within our clusters
and within pseudotime tertiles.

```{r covariation-state, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=5, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
.cd <- as.data.frame(colData(scp))                       # colnames(scp) is a CompressedList; use rownames of the df
cl  <- setNames(as.character(.cd$Cluster), rownames(.cd))
state_stats <- function(cells) {
  Ms <- mat[, cells, drop = FALSE]; Ms <- Ms[rowMeans(!is.na(Ms)) >= 0.5, , drop = FALSE]
  C  <- suppressWarnings(cor(t(Ms), use = "pairwise.complete.obs"))
  set.seed(1); nul <- mean(replicate(1500, { g <- sample(rownames(C), 20); s <- C[g, g]; mean(s[upper.tri(s)], na.rm = TRUE) }), na.rm = TRUE)
  ox <- intersect(complexes$OXPHOS, rownames(C)); gl <- intersect(glyc, rownames(C))
  data.frame(null = nul,
             Ribosome = mean_within(C, complexes$Ribosome), Proteasome = mean_within(C, complexes$Proteasome),
             OXPHOS = mean_within(C, complexes$OXPHOS), Spliceosome = mean_within(C, complexes$Spliceosome),
             OXPHOS_vs_glyc = mean(C[ox, gl, drop = FALSE], na.rm = TRUE)) }

st_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(sort(unique(na.omit(cl))), function(k) {
  cells <- names(cl)[which(cl == k)]; if (length(cells) < 20) return(NULL)
  cbind(State = sprintf("Cluster %s (n=%d)", k, length(cells)), round(state_stats(cells), 2)) }))
knitr::kable(st_tab, row.names = FALSE, caption = "State-resolved covariation. Complexes stay strongly cohesive within every cluster; OXPHOS↔glycolysis stays POSITIVE (≈ the within-state null) — the Warburg-style anti-correlation is not reproduced.")

## Fig S11b/c: reproducibility scatter + OXPHOS/glyc raw->cleaned->within-state
set.seed(1); h <- sample(ncol(M), floor(ncol(M)/2))
a <- cor(t(M[, h]), use = "pairwise.complete.obs"); b <- cor(t(M[, -h]), use = "pairwise.complete.obs"); ut <- upper.tri(a)
dfr <- data.frame(a = a[ut], b = b[ut]); dfr <- dfr[is.finite(dfr$a) & is.finite(dfr$b), ]
pB <- ggplot(dfr[sample(nrow(dfr), min(3e4, nrow(dfr))), ], aes(a, b)) + geom_point(size = .3, alpha = .12) +
  geom_abline(linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") + geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, formula = y~x, colour = "#B2182B") +
  labs(x = "protein-protein r (cell half 1)", y = "r (cell half 2)",
       title = sprintf("Split-half reproducibility (rho = %.2f; Leduc gate = 0.8)", cor(dfr$a, dfr$b))) + theme_bw(base_size = 12)
print(pB); save_fig(pB, "S11_covariation_reproducibility.png", 6, 5.5)

gs <- c(head(intersect(complexes$OXPHOS, rownames(C0)), 16), head(glyc, 12))
mk_long <- function(C, tag){ Cs <- C[gs, gs]; data.frame(g1 = factor(rep(gs, length(gs)), levels = gs),
  g2 = factor(rep(gs, each = length(gs)), levels = rev(gs)), r = as.vector(Cs), panel = tag) }
d <- rbind(mk_long(C0, "RAW (all cells)"), mk_long(Ci, "-log_sumsRI (technical out)"), mk_long(Ct, "-log_sumsRI -PC1 (within-state)"))
d$panel <- factor(d$panel, levels = c("RAW (all cells)", "-log_sumsRI (technical out)", "-log_sumsRI -PC1 (within-state)"))
pC <- ggplot(d, aes(g1, g2, fill = r)) + geom_tile() + facet_wrap(~panel) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B", midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1,1), name = "r") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "OXPHOS + glycolysis covariation: OXPHOS stays cohesive, cross-block weakens but stays positive (never negative)",
       subtitle = "first 16 rows/cols OXPHOS, rest glycolysis") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 7) + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = .5, size = 4),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 4), panel.grid = element_blank(), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
print(pC); save_fig(pC, "S11_oxphos_glycolysis_residual.png", 13, 5.5)
```

**Interpretation.** Within every cluster and pseudotime tertile the complexes remain
tightly cohesive (ribosome/OXPHOS/spliceosome *r* ≈ 0.75–0.92), confirming that
functional covariation is a within-state property here, not an artefact of pooling
across the trajectory. But **OXPHOS↔glycolysis stays positive** (+0.53 to +0.73 within
clusters, ≈ the within-state null) — after normalisation the cross-block *weakens* but
does **not** turn negative: the block mean settles near **+0.3**, and a stricter test —
the partial correlation of the per-cell OXPHOS and glycolysis mean scores, controlling
for `log_sumsRI_NoCRAP` and compPCA-PC1 — stays firmly positive at **r ≈ +0.5**
(*p* < 10⁻¹⁰), with essentially no negative pairs within the homogeneous clusters. We do
**not** reproduce the Warburg-style antagonism (if anything the modules are *co-regulated*). Two non-exclusive reasons, both literature-grounded:
(i) it is a within-cell-state effect requiring cell numbers and state resolution we lack
(our per-state n ≈ 25–35, vs their hundreds-to-thousands, and the metabolic split-half
reproducibility does not clear 0.8); and (ii) a differentiating cortical organoid need
not run the proliferation-driven glycolysis/OXPHOS trade-off seen in the Slavov lab's
dividing monocyte and cancer-cell systems — here both metabolic modules track the
shared biosynthetic program (consistent with Session 10's biosynthetic/metabolic DOWN
axis dominating absolute abundance).

## 11.3 Robustness of the covariation claims

Three checks close the obvious loopholes: is the complex signal just "well-detected
proteins covary more"? is the sub-0.8 reproducibility power-limited or genuinely absent?
and does the OXPHOS↔glycolysis coupling flip negative under a stricter partial correlation?

```{r covariation-robustness, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
.s11r <- file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$obj, "S11_robustness.rds")
if (!exists("sce_min")) sce_min <- readRDS(file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$obj, "sce_minimal.rds"))
lrs  <- as.data.frame(colData(scp))[colnames(M), "log_sumsRI_NoCRAP"]
pc1v <- reducedDim(sce_min, "compPCA")[colnames(M), 1]

if (file.exists(.s11r)) { R11 <- readRDS(.s11r) } else {
  set.seed(101)
  ## (a) detection-matched null: draw each complex member's replacement from proteins
  ##     of near-identical detection -> controls for "well-detected proteins covary more"
  detM <- rowMeans(!is.na(M)); pool <- rownames(Ci)
  matched_null <- function(gs, B = 2000) { gs <- intersect(gs, pool)
    replicate(B, { pick <- vapply(gs, function(g){ cand <- setdiff(pool[abs(detM[pool] - detM[g]) <= 0.03], gs)
        if (!length(cand)) g else sample(cand, 1) }, character(1))
      s <- Ci[pick, pick]; mean(s[upper.tri(s)], na.rm = TRUE) }) }
  dettab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(complexes), function(nm){ gs <- intersect(complexes[[nm]], pool); if (length(gs) < 4) return(NULL)
    ob <- mean_within(Ci, gs); rn <- replicate(2000, { g <- sample(pool, length(gs)); s <- Ci[g, g]; mean(s[upper.tri(s)], na.rm = TRUE) }); mn <- matched_null(gs)
    data.frame(Set = nm, n = length(gs), r = round(ob, 2), z_random = round((ob - mean(rn))/sd(rn), 1), z_detection_matched = round((ob - mean(mn))/sd(mn), 1)) }))
  ## (b) reproducibility vs detection threshold (raw)
  reprod_thr <- function(thr, S = 6){ Mt <- mat[rowMeans(!is.na(mat)) >= thr, ]; sapply(1:S, function(s){ set.seed(s); h <- sample(ncol(Mt), floor(ncol(Mt)/2))
    a <- cor(t(Mt[, h]), use = "pairwise.complete.obs"); b <- cor(t(Mt[, -h]), use = "pairwise.complete.obs"); ut <- upper.tri(a); ok <- is.finite(a[ut]) & is.finite(b[ut]); cor(a[ut][ok], b[ut][ok]) }) }
  reptab <- data.frame(det_threshold = c(.5, .6, .75, .9), n_proteins = sapply(c(.5, .6, .75, .9), function(t) sum(rowMeans(!is.na(mat)) >= t)),
    rho = round(sapply(c(.5, .6, .75, .9), function(t) median(reprod_thr(t))), 2))
  ## (c) pair-observation floor (raw, det>=0.5 protein set held FIXED) -> isolates power from protein count
  floor_rho <- function(fl, S = 6){ sapply(1:S, function(s){ set.seed(s); h <- sample(ncol(M), floor(ncol(M)/2))
    A <- M[, h]; B <- M[, -h]; a <- cor(t(A), use = "pairwise.complete.obs"); b <- cor(t(B), use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
    na <- tcrossprod(!is.na(A)); nb <- tcrossprod(!is.na(B)); ok <- (na >= fl) & (nb >= fl) & upper.tri(a) & is.finite(a) & is.finite(b); cor(a[ok], b[ok]) }) }
  floortab <- data.frame(min_complete_obs_per_half = c(0, 20, 40, 50), rho = round(sapply(c(0, 20, 40, 50), function(f) median(floor_rho(f))), 2))
  R11 <- list(dettab = dettab, reptab = reptab, floortab = floortab); saveRDS(R11, .s11r)
}
## (d) partial correlation of the OXPHOS-mean and glycolysis-mean scores | log_sumsRI + PC1
ox <- intersect(complexes$OXPHOS, rownames(M)); gl <- intersect(glyc, rownames(M))
oxm <- colMeans(M[ox, ], na.rm = TRUE); glm <- colMeans(M[gl, ], na.rm = TRUE)
rp_raw <- cor(oxm, glm, use = "complete.obs")
rp_adj <- cor(residuals(lm(oxm ~ lrs + pc1v)), residuals(lm(glm ~ lrs + pc1v)))

knitr::kable(R11$dettab, caption = "(a) Complex covariation z vs a size-matched random null AND a DETECTION-matched null — the signal is not a well-detected-proteins artefact.")
knitr::kable(R11$reptab, caption = "(b) Split-half reproducibility rises toward the 0.8 gate as detection (=power) increases — power-limited, not absent structure.")
knitr::kable(R11$floortab, caption = "(c) With the protein set held FIXED (det>=50%), reproducibility rises to ~0.82 as pairs are restricted to more complete observations per half — isolates power from protein count.")
cat(sprintf("(d) OXPHOS-mean vs glycolysis-mean across cells: r = %+.2f raw; %+.2f after partialling out log_sumsRI + PC1 => POSITIVE, not anti-correlated.\n", rp_raw, rp_adj))
```

These confirm all three: the complex z-scores survive a detection-matched null; reproducibility
climbs from 0.72 to ~0.82 under either power lever (higher-detection proteins, or more
complete observations per pair with the protein set fixed) — the hallmark of a power limit,
not missing signal; and the metabolic modules stay positively coupled (partial *r* ≈ +0.5)
rather than antagonistic.

**Bottom line.** Our data reproduce the paper's *core* claim — functional protein sets
covary well above chance, reproducibly at the set level, without imputation — and this
holds within cell states. They do **not** support pair-level covariation networks
(reproducibility ρ ≈ 0.6–0.7 < 0.8) or the specific OXPHOS↔glycolysis anti-correlation,
both expected given ~11× fewer cells and ~75 % missingness. Every reported number is a
set-level aggregate with its detection count stated, per the SCP reporting standards
(Gatto/Vanderaa *et al.* 2023).

# Session 12 — Marker-anchored covariation (Leduc et al. 2022 CDC method, adapted) ⭐

Leduc *et al.* identify proteins co-varying with the **cell-division cycle** (Fig. 3) by
(i) building robust **phase-marker vectors** — the *averaged* profile of several proteins
that peak in the same CDC phase (averaging cancels per-protein noise), validated so that
same-phase markers correlate positively and different-phase markers negatively — then
(ii) correlating every well-detected protein's observed values against those marker
vectors (FDR < 5 %), and (iii) aggregating to functional sets with a **split-half
reproducibility** gate (ρ > 0.8). We adapt this to our **progenitor→neuron pseudotime**:
the two poles of the continuum play the role of the "phases."

One caveat is intrinsic. Leduc's CDC axis came from an *independent* assay (FACS DNA
content) analysed *within* a cell type, so it was orthogonal to the dominant cell-type
structure. Our pseudotime is *derived from* the proteome and *is* the dominant axis, so
anchoring on pseudotime markers and correlating across all cells partly **re-derives the
Session-10 drivers** — which makes this a valuable *model-free cross-check* of the
trajectory, and pushes the novelty into the **within-state** pass (§12.2). As in
Session 11, covariation is computed only after regressing out the per-cell loading
`log_sumsRI` (else the +0.64 baseline makes even the two opposite poles correlate positively).

## 12.1 Pole-marker vectors and proteome-wide covariation

```{r marker-covariation, fig.width=12, fig.height=5, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(SingleCellExperiment); library(ggplot2); library(patchwork)})
.s12 <- file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$obj, "S12_marker_covariation.rds")
M0raw <- as.matrix(assay(scp[["Protein.Group"]]))
lrs   <- as.data.frame(colData(scp))[colnames(M0raw), "log_sumsRI_NoCRAP"]
cl    <- setNames(as.character(as.data.frame(colData(scp))$Cluster), colnames(M0raw))
st    <- readRDS(file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$obj, "sce_trajectory.rds"))
pt    <- setNames(st$Pseudotime, colnames(st))
regress_out <- function(Mx, x) { R <- Mx
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(Mx))) { y <- Mx[i, ]; ok <- is.finite(y)
    if (sum(ok) < 8) { R[i, ] <- NA; next }; R[i, ok] <- residuals(lm(y[ok] ~ x[ok])) }; R }
zc <- function(x) (x - mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)
M0 <- regress_out(M0raw[rowMeans(!is.na(M0raw)) >= 0.30, ], lrs)     # log_sumsRI-cleaned
M  <- M0[rowMeans(!is.na(M0)) >= 0.5, ]                              # well-detected

## pole-marker vectors: averaged z-scored anchor profiles (curated IF markers)
anchor <- list(
  Neuronal   = intersect(c("DCX","STMN1","CRMP1","DPYSL3","DPYSL5","MAP1B","TUBB3","MAP2","ELAVL3","UCHL1","STMN2","DBN1","RTN1","GAP43"), rownames(M0)),
  Progenitor = intersect(c("SOX2","NES","VIM","FABP7","PTPRZ1","PCNA","HES1","TOP2A"), rownames(M0)))
pole <- as.data.frame(sapply(anchor, function(g) colMeans(t(apply(M0[g, , drop = FALSE], 1, zc)), na.rm = TRUE)))
pole$cell <- colnames(M0); anchors_all <- unlist(anchor); prot <- setdiff(rownames(M), anchors_all)
cn <- intersect(pole$cell, names(pt))

if (file.exists(.s12)) { S12 <- readRDS(.s12) } else {
  cor_to <- function(vec) { r <- sapply(prot, function(p){ y <- M[p, ]; ok <- is.finite(y) & is.finite(vec)
    if (sum(ok) < 20) return(c(NA, NA)); ct <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(y[ok], vec[ok], method = "spearman")); c(ct$estimate, ct$p.value) })
    data.frame(protein = prot, rho = r[1, ], p = r[2, ]) }
  neu <- cor_to(pole$Neuronal); neu$FDR <- p.adjust(neu$p, "BH")
  pro <- cor_to(pole$Progenitor); pro$FDR <- p.adjust(pro$p, "BH")
  rr <- sapply(1:8, function(s){ set.seed(s); h <- sample(ncol(M), floor(ncol(M)/2))
    f <- function(cols){ v <- pole$Neuronal[match(colnames(M)[cols], pole$cell)]
      sapply(prot, function(p){ y <- M[p, cols]; ok <- is.finite(y) & is.finite(v); if (sum(ok) < 10) NA else cor(y[ok], v[ok], method = "spearman") }) }
    a <- f(h); b <- f(setdiff(seq_len(ncol(M)), h)); ok <- is.finite(a) & is.finite(b); cor(a[ok], b[ok]) })
  S12 <- list(neu = neu, pro = pro, rr = rr); saveRDS(S12, .s12)
}
neu <- S12$neu; pro <- S12$pro; rr <- S12$rr
res <- merge(neu, pro, by = "protein", suffixes = c("_neu", "_pro"))

## validation + reproducibility + agreement with the S10.5 slingshot drivers
cat(sprintf("[A] pole validation: cor(Neuronal, Progenitor) = %+.2f (expect NEGATIVE) | pole~pseudotime: neuronal %+.2f, progenitor %+.2f\n",
    cor(pole$Neuronal, pole$Progenitor, use = "complete.obs"),
    cor(pole$Neuronal[match(cn, pole$cell)], pt[cn], method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"),
    cor(pole$Progenitor[match(cn, pole$cell)], pt[cn], method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")))
cat(sprintf("[B] neuronal-pole covarying proteins (FDR<0.05): %d | split-half reproducibility median rho = %.2f (Leduc gate 0.8)\n",
    sum(neu$FDR < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), median(rr)))
## compare the neuronal-pole covariation against the NEURONAL-lineage slingshot drivers
## (S10.5 is now per-lineage since the trajectory trifurcates; the clean C3->C2 neuronal lineage
## is the right comparison for the neuronal pole).
drv <- read.csv(file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$tab, "S10_drivers_absolute_neuronal.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
mm <- merge(neu, drv, by.x = "protein", by.y = "gene")            # rho.x = neuronal-pole, rho.y = neuronal-lineage pseudotime
cat(sprintf("[C] agreement vs S10.5 NEURONAL-lineage drivers: rho = %.2f over %d proteins (cross-validates the trajectory)\n",
    cor(mm$rho.x, mm$rho.y, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"), nrow(mm)))

pd <- pole; pd$pt <- pt[match(pd$cell, names(pt))]
pA <- ggplot(pd, aes(Progenitor, Neuronal, colour = pt)) + geom_point(size = 2.6) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(name = "pseudotime", na.value = "grey85") +
  labs(title = sprintf("Pole-marker vectors (anti-correlate r=%+.2f; track pseudotime)", cor(pd$Neuronal, pd$Progenitor, use = "complete.obs"))) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
res$mod <- ifelse(res$FDR_neu < 0.05 & res$rho_neu > 0, "neuronal", ifelse(res$FDR_neu < 0.05 & res$rho_neu < 0, "progenitor", "n.s."))
pB <- ggplot(res, aes(rho_pro, rho_neu, colour = mod)) + geom_point(size = 1, alpha = .6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(neuronal = "#B2182B", progenitor = "#2166AC", n.s. = "grey80"), name = NULL) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "rho to progenitor pole", y = "rho to neuronal pole", title = "Every protein classified by which pole it tracks") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
print(pA | pB); save_fig(pA | pB, "S12_pole_covariation.png", 12, 5)
```

The marker-anchored covariation **validates and sharpens** the trajectory. The two pole
vectors **anti-correlate** (as Leduc's different-phase markers do) and track pseudotime in
opposite directions; the neuronal-pole correlation vector is **reproducible at ρ ≈ 0.87**
— comfortably past the 0.8 gate and far above the pair-level ρ ≈ 0.6–0.7 of Session 11,
because averaging the anchor proteins cancels noise. It agrees with the Session-10
slingshot drivers at ρ ≈ 0.89, so the progenitor→neuron axis is not an artifact of the
slingshot step. The two-pole scatter cleanly partitions the proteome into a
**neuronal-covarying** module (top-left) and a **progenitor-covarying** module (bottom-right).

## 12.2 Functional-set and within-state covariation

```{r marker-covariation-sets, fig.width=8, fig.height=5, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
sets <- list(Ribosome = grep("^RP[LS][0-9]", rownames(M), value = TRUE),
  OXPHOS = grep("^NDUF|^UQCR|^COX[0-9]|^SDH[ABCD]$|^ATP5", rownames(M), value = TRUE),
  Spliceosome = grep("^SNRP|^SF3[AB]|^SRSF|^PRPF|^HNRNP", rownames(M), value = TRUE),
  Glycolysis = intersect(c("HK1","GPI","PFKL","ALDOA","TPI1","GAPDH","PGK1","PGAM1","ENO1","PKM","LDHA","LDHB"), rownames(M)),
  `Neuronal cytoskeleton` = intersect(c("TUBB2A","TUBB2B","TUBA1A","INA","NEFL","NEFM","DPYSL2","DPYSL4","BASP1","STMN2"), rownames(M)),
  `FA oxidation` = intersect(c("HADHA","HADHB","DECR1","ACADVL","ETFA","ETFB","CPT2","ACAA2"), rownames(M)),
  `AA catabolism` = intersect(c("GLUD1","ALDH6A1","ALDH7A1","HIBCH","BCAT2","PSAT1","PHGDH","ABAT"), rownames(M)))
setrho <- sapply(sets, function(g){ g <- intersect(g, neu$protein); if (length(g) < 3) return(NA); mean(neu$rho[neu$protein %in% g], na.rm = TRUE) })
sd_ <- data.frame(set = names(setrho), rho = as.numeric(setrho)); sd_ <- sd_[is.finite(sd_$rho), ]
pD <- ggplot(sd_, aes(reorder(set, rho), rho, fill = rho > 0)) + geom_col() + coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#B2182B", `FALSE` = "#2166AC"), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "mean rho to neuronal pole", title = "Functional-set covariation with the neuronal pole") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
print(pD); save_fig(pD, "S12_functionalset_covariation.png", 8, 5)
knitr::kable(sd_[order(-sd_$rho), ], digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Functional-set covariation with the neuronal pole (mean member ρ): neuronal cytoskeleton up, amino-acid/fatty-acid catabolism down — the trajectory's UP/DOWN programs, recovered marker-free.")

## within-state (novel): inside the neuronal cluster C2, covariation with the neuronal pole
c2 <- names(cl)[cl == "2" & !is.na(cl)]; Mc <- M[, c2]; Mc <- Mc[rowMeans(!is.na(Mc)) >= 0.5, ]
vc <- pole$Neuronal[match(c2, pole$cell)]
wc <- sapply(setdiff(rownames(Mc), anchors_all), function(p){ y <- Mc[p, ]; ok <- is.finite(y) & is.finite(vc); if (sum(ok) < 15) NA else cor(y[ok], vc[ok], method = "spearman") })
wc <- sort(wc[is.finite(wc)], decreasing = TRUE)
cat(sprintf("\n[E] WITHIN neuronal cluster C2 (n=%d): %d/%d proteins co-vary with the neuronal pole at |rho|>0.4\n", length(c2), sum(abs(wc) > 0.4), length(wc)))
cat("   top within-C2 module (axonal transport / cytoskeleton):", paste(head(names(wc), 12), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

**Interpretation.** The functional-set map recovers the trajectory's programs
**marker-free**: the neuronal cytoskeleton covaries strongly with the neuronal pole
(ρ ≈ +0.8), while **amino-acid and fatty-acid catabolism** covary with the progenitor pole
(ρ ≈ −0.4 to −0.5) and the ribosome mildly so — i.e. the biosynthetic/metabolic DOWN and
neuronal UP programs of Session 10, reached here without slingshot. The **within-state**
pass is the genuinely new view: *inside* the neuronal cluster, a coherent **axonal-transport /
cytoskeleton module** (TUBB2B, DYNC1H1, CLTC, KIF2A/KIF5C, RAB6A, DPYSL2) still co-varies
with the neuronal markers — a finer neuronal-maturation gradient beyond the main axis.
*Caveat:* a large fraction of the proteome co-varies even within C2, so at n = 57 this is a
suggestive maturation signal, not a cleanly isolated module — consistent with the pervasive,
power-limited covariation established in Session 11.

**Bottom line.** Adapting the Leduc CDC method with averaged pseudotime-pole markers gives a
covariation estimate that clears the reproducibility gate (ρ ≈ 0.87) where the pair-level
analysis did not, independently **cross-validates** the progenitor→neuron drivers (ρ ≈ 0.89),
and — via the within-state pass — points to an axonal-transport maturation module inside the
neurons that the trajectory-level analysis could not resolve.

# Appendix A — Imputed-matrix pipeline + reference annotation

<!-- The imputed branch lives here because the methods it enables REQUIRE a
     complete (no-NA) matrix. It is NOT the canonical pipeline (imputation
     conflicts with the missingness findings in Session 5) but is needed for:
       A.1  KNN imputation -> fixedPCA on HVGs -> reclustering -> scoreMarkers
       A.2  SingleR reference annotation on NON-centred log ABUNDANCE
            (Blueprint / Zhong / laManno / HNOCA) + scoring-quality panels
     SingleR cannot run on the NA-containing matrix (it rank-correlates against
     references), so it uses the KNN-imputed, NON-centred `Protein.Group_abund`
     (the centred Protein.Group distorts within-cell ranks). All refs are RNA-seq,
     so treat the calls as soft/coarse corroboration (protein-vs-RNA cross-modality;
     low confidence, but progenitor-type labels verifiably track low pseudotime). -->

## A.1 KNN imputation, PCA, re-clustering, markers

```{r appendix-impute, fig.width=7, fig.height=6}
## KNN-impute the normalized log2 protein matrix (impute::impute.knn under the
## hood; handles negative log-ratios fine, so no constant shift needed).
scp <- impute(scp, i = "Protein.Group", name = "Protein.Group_imptd",
              method = "knn", k = 3, rowmax = 1, colmax = 1,
              maxp = Inf, rng.seed = 1234)

sce_imptd <- as(scp[["Protein.Group_imptd"]], "SingleCellExperiment")
assayNames(sce_imptd) <- "logcounts"            # scran/scater default assay
colData(sce_imptd)    <- colData(scp)

## HVG selection + PCA on the complete (imputed) matrix
## Protein.Group is per-protein-centred (row-mean normalised), so all gene means
## are ~0 and modelGeneVar's mean-variance trend is ill-posed (it errors even with
## density.weights = FALSE). Select HVGs by raw variance on the imputed matrix.
v       <- apply(as.matrix(assay(sce_imptd, "logcounts")), 1, var)
hvg.var <- rownames(sce_imptd)[order(v, decreasing = TRUE)][seq_len(min(1000, nrow(sce_imptd)))]
set.seed(101)
sce_imptd <- fixedPCA(sce_imptd, subset.row = hvg.var, rank = 50)

## re-cluster + embed on the imputed PCA
colLabels(sce_imptd) <- clusterCells(sce_imptd, use.dimred = "PCA",
                                     BLUSPARAM = NNGraphParam(k = PROC$nn_k))
set.seed(101); sce_imptd <- runUMAP(sce_imptd, dimred = "PCA",
                                    n_neighbors = PROC$umap_nn)
print(plotUMAP(sce_imptd, colour_by = "label", text_by = "label",
               point_size = 3) + ggtitle("Imputed-matrix re-clustering"))

## scran scoreMarkers per imputed cluster (needs complete data -> lives here)
marker.info <- scoreMarkers(sce_imptd, colLabels(sce_imptd), lfc = 1.5)
top1 <- as.data.frame(marker.info[[1]])
print(head(top1[order(top1$median.logFC.cohen, decreasing = TRUE), 1:4]))
saveRDS(sce_imptd, file.path(PATHS$base, PATHS$obj, "sce_imputed.rds"))
```

## A.2 SingleR reference annotation (on NON-centred log abundance)

SingleR rank-correlates each cell against **absolute-expression** references, so its
input must be absolute log-**abundance** — not the per-protein-centred `Protein.Group`
used elsewhere. Centring re-orders genes within each cell and changes 60–90 % of the
calls (verified). We therefore annotate the non-centred `Protein.Group_abund`,
KNN-imputed (SingleR needs a complete matrix). All three references are RNA-seq, so
this is a cross-modality comparison: confidence is low and the calls are best read as
**soft, coarse** corroboration. (Verified: progenitor-type labels still track low
pseudotime, so the coarse progenitor→neuron axis is real even though fine subtypes
are not reliable — see the quality panels below.)

**Interpretation guardrails (for reporting).** SingleR here provides *directional
corroboration only, not cell-type calls*. Its resolution is capped by three factors:
(i) a **cross-modality** comparison — protein abundance vs RNA references — where
mRNA–protein correlation is only ~0.4–0.6, so within-cell rank profiles diverge;
(ii) **incomplete references** for developing human neural subtypes; and (iii) the SCP
**detection ceiling**, which omits the low-copy transcription factors and receptors
that define fine subtypes (missing-not-at-random / below-LOD, **not** biological
absence). We therefore report only the robust, directional signal — progenitor-type
labels enrich at low pseudotime and neuronal labels at high, concordant with the
marker-based trajectory — and assign **no discrete cell-type identities** from SingleR.

```{r appendix-singler-input, fig.width=7, fig.height=6}
## KNN-impute the NON-centred abundance protein matrix (complete matrix for SingleR)
scp <- impute(scp, i = "Protein.Group_abund", name = "Protein.Group_abund_imptd",
              method = "knn", k = 3, rowmax = 1, colmax = 1, maxp = Inf, rng.seed = 1234)
sce_sr <- as(scp[["Protein.Group_abund_imptd"]], "SingleCellExperiment")
assayNames(sce_sr) <- "logcounts"
colData(sce_sr)    <- colData(scp)
```

```{r appendix-singler, error=TRUE, fig.width=7, fig.height=6}
## Each reference is isolated so a download/normalisation hiccup can't kill the rest.
## Blueprint/ENCODE = bulk RNA-seq sanity ref; Zhong-2018 prefrontal + laManno-2016
## iPS = scRNA-seq counts (logNormCounts'd).
preds_sr <- list()
singler_one <- function(tag, get_ref, label_col, de.n = NULL) {
  pred <- tryCatch({
    ref  <- get_ref()
    args <- list(test = sce_sr, ref = ref, labels = colData(ref)[[label_col]],
                 assay.type.test = "logcounts")
    if (!is.null(de.n)) { args$de.method <- "wilcox"; args$de.n <- de.n }
    do.call(SingleR, args)
  }, error = function(e) { message(tag, " skipped: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })
  if (!is.null(pred)) {
    preds_sr[[tag]] <<- pred
    colData(sce_sr)[[paste0("SingleR_", tag)]] <<- pred$pruned.labels
    cat("\n", tag, ":\n"); print(table(pred$pruned.labels, useNA = "ifany"))
    save_tab(as.data.frame(table(pred$pruned.labels)), sprintf("A2_SingleR_%s.csv", tag))
  }
}
singler_one("Blueprint", function() celldex::BlueprintEncodeData(), "label.main")
singler_one("Zhong", function() {
  r <- scRNAseq::fetchDataset("zhong-prefrontal-2018", "2023-12-22")
  r <- r[, librarySizeFactors(r) > 0]; logNormCounts(computeSumFactors(r)) },
  "cell_types", de.n = 10)
singler_one("laManno", function() {
  r <- scRNAseq::fetchDataset("lamanno-brain-2016", "2023-12-17", path = "human-ips")
  r <- r[, librarySizeFactors(r) > 0]; logNormCounts(computeSumFactors(r)) },
  "Cell_type", de.n = 25)
```

### A.2.1 Classification-quality panels

```{r appendix-singler-quality, error=TRUE, fig.width=11, fig.height=7}
## (1) SingleR score heatmap per reference — cells x labels, the canonical QC plot
for (tag in names(preds_sr))
  print(plotScoreHeatmap(preds_sr[[tag]], show.pruned = TRUE,
                         main = sprintf("SingleR scores — %s", tag)))

## (2) Assignment confidence: delta = (top - 2nd) score per cell, by assigned label.
## Custom boxplot+jitter — robust to singleton labels (the default
## plotDeltaDistribution violins fail when a label has <2 cells).
dd <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(preds_sr), function(tag) {
  p  <- preds_sr[[tag]]; sc <- as.matrix(p$scores)
  d  <- apply(sc, 1, function(x) { xs <- sort(x, decreasing = TRUE); xs[1] - xs[2] })
  data.frame(ref = tag, label = as.character(p$labels),
             pruned = is.na(p$pruned.labels), delta = as.numeric(d))
}))
p_delta <- ggplot(dd, aes(reorder(label, delta, FUN = median), delta)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, fill = "grey92") +
  geom_jitter(aes(colour = pruned), width = 0.2, height = 0, size = 1, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey25", `TRUE` = "firebrick"),
                      name = "pruned (low conf.)") +
  facet_wrap(~ ref, scales = "free", ncol = 1) + coord_flip() +
  labs(x = "assigned label", y = "delta = top - 2nd score (higher = more confident)",
       title = "SingleR assignment confidence") + theme_bw(base_size = 11)
print(p_delta); save_fig(p_delta, "A2_SingleR_delta_confidence.png", w = 9, h = 11)

## (3) calls overlaid on the imputed-reclustering UMAP (from A.1; shared cells)
if ("UMAP" %in% reducedDimNames(sce_imptd)) {
  reducedDim(sce_sr, "UMAP") <- reducedDim(sce_imptd, "UMAP")[colnames(sce_sr), , drop = FALSE]
  for (tag in names(preds_sr))
    print(plotUMAP(sce_sr, colour_by = paste0("SingleR_", tag), point_size = 3) +
            ggtitle(sprintf("SingleR — %s", tag)))
}
```

```{r appendix-singler-hnoca, eval=FALSE}
## --- HNOCA (organoid atlas) -- requires the local consolidated .h5ad --------
## Set eval=TRUE once the path is confirmed; needs zellkonverter.
h5ad <- file.path(PATHS$base,
  "DIANN/DIANN/scp/HNOCA/h5ad/Cortical_subset/cortical_consolidated.h5ad")
ref_hn <- zellkonverter::readH5AD(h5ad, use_hdf5 = TRUE)
assayNames(ref_hn)[assayNames(ref_hn) == "X"] <- "counts"
ref_hn <- logNormCounts(ref_hn)
pred_hn <- SingleR(test = sce_sr, ref = ref_hn, labels = ref_hn$cell_type,
                   assay.type.test = "logcounts", de.method = "wilcox", de.n = 25)
colData(sce_sr)$SingleR_HNOCA <- pred_hn$pruned.labels
print(table(pred_hn$pruned.labels, useNA = "ifany"))
save_tab(as.data.frame(table(pred_hn$pruned.labels)), "A2_SingleR_HNOCA.csv")
```
